title: WCE Hackathon 2026
description: WCE Hackathon 2026 marks the 10th Edition of the flagship hackathon organized by WCE ACM Student Chapter, celebrating a decade of innovation, collaboration, and problem-solving excellence. WCE Hackathon 2026 will be conducted entirely in Offline mode for the implementation round. The first round will be conducted online, while the implementation round will be conducted offline. WCE Hackathon 2026 is a developing venture where participants are expected to complete product development as per the selected problem statements. In this hackathon, participants will innovate, strategize, code, and beat the odds with ingenious solutions to real-life problems. The Expert Track focuses on addressing Artificial Intelligence (AI) Systems through innovative solutions. Participants in this track will have the opportunity to create impactful solutions and may even secure internship opportunities with Zenteiq . Hackathon Phases: Official Announcement: February 2, 2026 Round 1 (Online): February 2, 2026 - February 25, 2026 Result Declaration of Round 1 (Expert Track): March 6, 2026 Result Declaration of Round 1 (Novice Track): March 8, 2025 Round 2 (Offline): March 20, 2026 - March 21, 2026 Result Declaration of Round 2: March 21, 2026 Tracks : The Hackathon will consist of 2 tracks i.e. Novice and Expert. Themes for the Novice Track are provided in the guidelines document included in the zip file shared with participants. Expert Track : Teams of students with at least one member from the 3rd or 4th year will compete in this track. The Expert Track includes problem statements related to Artificial Intelligence(AI) Systems created by Zenteiq. Note : BCA Final Year Students will be considered in the Expert Track. Note : Download the Brief/Case file attached in the Round 1 section to know the Presentation Format and also the Themes for both tracks. The file can be downloaded only after completing your registration.

title: IoT Hackathon
description: IoT Hackathon: A dynamic and inspiring event designed for tech enthusiasts, developers, and engineers to collaborate and innovate. Participants will engage in hands-on coding and problem-solving, leveraging connected devices to tackle real-world challenges. With a focus on redefining the boundaries of IoT applications, this hackathon serves as a platform for groundbreaking ideas and impactful solutions. Problem Statements: (Themes but not limited to): Healthcare: IoT-driven GPS Ambulance tracking for traffic-free transit IoT-based Elderly Care Monitoring System Real-time Guidance Assistant for Physically Disabled and Blind Individuals Automation: Smart Home Advancement for Automated Living IoT-based Automatic Movable Dustbins Fire Extinguishing Robot Sustainability: IoT-integrated intelligent energy management system for a sustainable future IoT-enabled water management system for smarter homes Industrial harmful gas detection and safety Environmental: IoT-Driven Precision Agriculture with farming solutions Marine Litter Detection and Removal Smart Wildlife Surveillance for Anti-Poaching Guidelines: The team leader is responsible for registering the team. title: Capture the Flag
description: Unleash your inner cyber detective and embark on a journey through the fascinating realms of ethical hacking, digital forensics, cryptography, and system exploitation. Whether you're a seasoned hacker sharpening your expertise or a curious beginner exploring the thrilling universe of cybersecurity, this CTF promises to test your problem-solving abilities and strategic thinking like never before. Get ready to tackle adrenaline-pumping challenges, decode mysteries, and conquer the digital battlefield in an electrifying competitive environment. Guidelines: General Rules: Participants must register as a team (Team size. 2-3 members). The event will run for a specified duration. All challenges must be completed within this timeframe. Any attempt to disrupt the CTF platform or other participants will result in immediate disqualification unless explicitly mentioned. The use of automated tools for solving challenges is prohibited unless explicitly allowed. The use of AI and AI-powered tools to solve challenges is strictly prohibited unless explicitly allowed for specific tasks. No physical machines or devices will be provided for attack purposes. Sharing or discussing flags with other teams is strictly forbidden. Code of Conduct: Follow the event's communication guidelines, including using only designated channels for queries or discussions. Challenge Rules: Challenges may include categories such as web exploitation, cryptography, reverse engineering, forensics, and binary exploitation. Each challenge will have a specific point value based on its difficulty. Teams must submit flags in the correct format to earn points (e.g., CTF{example_flag}). If you believe a challenge is broken or unclear, notify the organizers through the official communication channel. Do not exploit errors in challenge deployment. Platform Use: Only one account per team is allowed on the CTF platform. Teams are responsible for the security of their account credentials. Do not attack the CTF platform itself, including attempting to access unauthorized areas or data. Disqualification Criteria: Engaging in prohibited activities, including: Sharing flags or collaborating with other teams. Attacking other participants or the CTF infrastructure. Using unauthorized tools or scripts. Violating any rule will lead to immediate disqualification and removal from the event. The decision of the event organizers is final and binding in all matters. Termination Clause The organizers reserve the right to modify or terminate the event if unforeseen circumstances arise.
prize: Winner: INR750 | Runner Up: INR500

title: Sustainability Hackathon 2025
description: Theme: Revolutionizing Waste Management: Reduce, Recycle, Repurpose The urgency for innovative waste management solutions stems from the ever-growing environmental and social challenges caused by improper waste handling. As societies grapple with increasing waste generation, landfill overflows, and the adverse effects of pollution, the need to revolutionize waste management has never been more critical. This year's hackathon seeks entries focusing on reducing waste generation, enhancing recycling practices, and finding creative ways to repurpose waste, contributing to a cleaner and more sustainable world. Participants are encouraged to focus their solutions on waste management areas including, 1) Plastic Waste Management 2) Sanitary Waste Management 3) Electronic Waste Management Candidates are also free to choose any other specific waste management areas as well. Objective: The goal of this competition is to inspire participants to develop practical and scalable solutions to revolutionize waste management. The solutions can be products, services, or a combination of both. Important Dates: Hackathon Date: February 8, 2025 Registration Deadline: January 21, 2025 First Round Deadline: January 21, 2025 Eligibility & Team Details: Open to all Team Size: 2-5 members Modus Operandi: Three Rounds: Round 1: Idea Generation & Evaluation Form teams of 2-5 members. Submit a one-page proposal covering: Title of Idea Problem Statement Proposed Solution Sustainability Impact Implementation Plan & Challenges Format: Word document or PDF, 12-point font, 1.5 spacing, 1-inch margins. Naming Format: "TeamName_2025.pdf" or "TeamName_2025.docs". Style: 12-point font, 1.5 spacing, 1-inch standard margins. Submissions of more than a page or in incorrect formats will NOT be considered. Submission (Round 1): You can submit via email at sustainability@gim.ac.in Deadline: January 21, 2025 Round 2: Mentorship Selected teams will be allotted a professional mentor till the conclusion of the Hackathon. The teams can connect with their assigned mentors on the development of the Ideas, prototypes, implementation roadmaps, financial feasibility, and pssoible challenges. Round 3: Hackathon (February 8, 2025) Deliverables: Teams will submit a comprehensive report and deliver a presentation outlining the relevance, impact, and implementation plan for their idea. Evaluation: A panel of experts will evaluate the presentations and will adjudge the winner and runner-up of the Hackathon.

title: Innovate X Hackathon
organizer: Shyam Lal College, University of Delhi
description: Aim: Develop a practical solution for a specific problem within 24 hours. Competition Rules and Guidelines Team Guidelines: Each team can include up to 4 members. Teams must have a unique name and designate a representative. Communication with organizers should use the team ID rather than the team name. General Rules: Teams will select a problem statement on the event day and have 24 hours to develop an innovative solution. Problem statements will cover areas like: Web Development App Development Machine Learning Web3 And more Randomly timed challenges may appear for bonus points. All teams must pass a screening round prior to the hackathon. Round 1: Screening - Ideation Phase Teams will submit a proposal addressing the problem statement below, detailing their approach, anticipated features, and other creative solutions. Submissions should target real-world issues and showcase inventive solutions. Experienced judges will review entries and select the top 25 teams for the final round. Problem Statement for Screening Round: "Develop an EdTech platform specifically for students preparing for master's entrance exams. The platform should emphasize test series and practice exams rather than video lectures. Include a chatbot for real-time query resolution or to provide unique data insights. Add engaging UI/UX features to improve the learning experience." Submission Requirements: Submit a detailed presentation (PPT) outlining your problem approach, innovative features, and high-level technical approach. A GitHub link with relevant code may be included to showcase the approach. AI Usage Restriction: No AI tools are allowed in the project development. AI detectors will be used to ensure compliance. Round 2: Final Implementation Phase Teams will choose their final problem statement from a preselected category based on their screening submission. They will have 24 hours to develop their solution. Teams are free to participate in other concurrent events. Judges will review projects based on: Originality Comprehension of the problem Solution feasibility Design and functionality robustness The top 3 projects will be selected as winners. Judging Criteria: Problem Understanding: Clear identification of requirements and target audience. Innovation: Novelty and uniqueness in the proposed solution. UI/UX Design: Interface design that enhances user experience. Functionality: Practicality, reliability, and completeness of the final solution.
prize: Winner: INR5000 | First Runner Up: INR3000 | Second Runner Up: INR2000

title: AI/ML Hackathon on Road safety, NSS IIT Roorkee
description: NSS IIT Roorkee is proud to organize a Road Safety Week featuring dynamic Road Safety Hackathons. What sets these hackathons apart? They're AI/ML based, bringing innovation to the forefront of road safety solutions. Join us in this tech-driven journey towards safer roads for everyone! Judging Criteria: Quality and innovation of the idea - 30% Demonstration/Presentation of the solution- 30% Development and design of the solution- 40% Round 1: Round 1 will consist of an online submission of the idea developed by the team. The format of the presenting file could be of any form. The last date for submission is 11:59 PM, 26th January 2024 . The team may submit as many times till the deadline. Only the final submission will be considered. The team leader needs to submit the idea proposal explaining the solution, with the naming convention TeamName_RoadSafety. Round 2: Round 2 will consist of a presentation of the idea, design, developed solution and code which should be done within 10 minutes, and a 5 min Q&A (for IITR students it will be offline and for others it will be online) Round 2 will be conducted on 27th January 2024 Team will be required to present in front of the jury The presence of all the team members during the presentation is compulsory First slide of the presentation must include the Team name and all Team Members' Name Final judgment will be done after the submission of the developed solution and evaluation will be done based on the judging criteria mentioned. Problem Statement: Voice-Activated Driving Assistant Accident Prediction and Prevention Traffic Flow Optimization Open Theme (the top projects of each problem statement will be verified) Rules and Regulations: The digital solution could be made on any of the platforms. Each team can have a minimum of 1 & maximum of 5 members. Individuals can be members of only one team. The members can be from the same/different institutions. Each team must have a team leader. All submissions will remain the intellectual property of the individuals that developed them. The team should not present projects that have previously been submitted to other initiatives. If the submission is work-based on an existing application, the participant should have acquired sufficient rights to use it. Source code not to contain any element with patent or copyright beforehand. There is no age restriction on any individual to participate. Anyone, from students to working professionals across the nation, can participate. Evaluation criteria will include novelty of the idea, complexity, clarity and details in the prescribed format, feasibility, practicability, sustainability, scale of impact, user experience and potential for future work progression. The team must note that violating any of the above rules must directly lead to disqualification. For any queries, please contact: Diya Arora 9729378923 diya.sustainability.nssiitr@gmail.com

title: AFourathon 3.0 Hackathon
description: Get ready to join the revolution! AFour Technologies is back with its third edition of Hackathon in 2023, I.e., AFourathon 3.0, and this time; we're on a mission to hire the top Data Enthusiasts, Coding Ninjas, Ideation Stars, UX Wizards, Cybersecurity Enthusiasts, and Technical Geeks for our team. So, it's your chance to shine and be part of something extraordinary at AFour Tech! We're calling all B.Tech/M. Tech Aspirants, Graduates, PG Students, and Young Technocrats from all over the country. So, whether you are a fresher or you're a seasoned pro with a minimum of 3 years under your belt, this is your chance to showcase your skills and make a real impact. P.S This is not any ordinary hackathon. We want you to think outside the box, step out of your comfort zone, and unleash your creativity like never before. But that's not all! Our ultimate goal is to foster diversity in the tech industry. We're breaking barriers and inspiring innovation among all our participants. So, regardless of background or experience, AFourathon is your platform to shine and make your mark. Join us at AFourathon 3.0 and be part of the coding revolution. Together, we'll shape a better tomorrow. Are you up for the challenge? Let's hack the future! Note: Please Re-register your team on our official website by choosing the number of problem statements that you can solve. Benefits of participating in AFourathon 3.0 Hackathon: Unleash your creativity: Break free from boundaries and explore your innovative side. Solve real-world problems: Make a tangible impact by developing innovative solutions to real-world challenges. Learn from the best: Gain insights and knowledge from experienced mentors and professionals. Showcase your talent: Stand out among talented individuals and get recognized for your skills. Enhance your skills: Sharpen your technical skills, learn new technologies, and stay up to date with the latest trends. Career opportunities: AFourathon is not just a hackathon; it's a talent hunt. Fun and camaraderie: Enjoy a vibrant, dynamic atmosphere filled with excitement, teamwork, and friendly competition. Important Details: You need to register on AFourathon Official Website Win a Prize Pool of up to 1,00,000 Lakhs Winners will be eligible for PPIs or Internships Eligibility: Experience (0 to 3 Years), B.Tech/M.Tech Aspirants, Graduates, and PG Students Registration Fee: Free Dates: Registration ends on 15th June Team Size: 1 to 3 Problem Statements or Projects a Team can solve: No Restrictions Important Timelines: Hackathon Registration: Starts on 25th May <Start Coding/> Registration End Date: 15th June <30 Days Until First Demo Video Submission/> AFourathon Q/A Session: Date: 7th June at 8 PM & 10th June at 12 PM 1st Demo Submission: To be submitted by 15th July EOD <Requirements/> - 15 Min Demo Video of the Project with a Working Application - Digital Asset Engineering Updated Document - Code for Working Solution Next Round Details: Qualified Participants from 1st Demo Submission will proceed to the <Final Round aka D-Day/> Date: 18th or 19th July Final Presentation: Date: 20th and 21st July Projects: Solve Any (No Restrictions) Project A: Cab Management Project Cab Management Project is broken up as 3 problem statements. You can implement as many working solutions for problem statements as you can. You can use same or different tech stack/languages for coding each problem statement. Problem Statement 1 - Driver Details App Build an application that can be run as a container on the cloud for creating/updating/deleting a driver. The functionality of the application is: Allow user to add, update, delete a driver Each driver should have: Driver Name, Driver ID Number, Driver Email, and Driver Phone Number Persist all driver details in the database Problem Statement 2 - Cabs App Build an application that can be run as a container on the cloud for creating/updating/deleting a cab. The functionality of the application is: Allow user to add, update, delete a cab Each car should have: Cab Registration Number, Cab Model, and Cab Colour Persist all cab details in the database Problem Statement 3 - Cab Management App Build an application that can be run as a container on the cloud for lending/updating/deleting driver for each cab. The functionality of the application is: There should be 2 pages/screens/views - Driver Page and Cab Page On the Driver Page: The user should be able to select a driver from a list of drivers(From Problem Statement 1) and Then let them select, update, delete the cab (From Problem Statement 2) assigned for that driver On the Cabs Page: The user should be able to select a cab from list of cabs (From Problem Statement 2) and Then let them select, update, delete the driver that are assigned to that cab Persist all details in the database Project B: College Library Project: College Library Project is broken up as 3 problem statements. You can implement as many working solutions for problem statements as you can. You can use same or different tech stack/languages for coding each problem statement. Problem Statement 1 - Student Details App Build an application that can be run as a container on the cloud for creating/updating/deleting a student. The functionality of the application is: Allow user to add, update, delete a student Each student should have: Student Name, Student ID Number, Student Email, Student Phone Number Persist all student details in the database Problem Statement 2 - Books App Build an application that can be run as a container on the cloud for creating/updating/deleting a library book. The functionality of the application is: Allow user to add, update, delete a book Each book should have: Book Title, Book Author, Book Description, Book Code Persist all subjects in the database Problem Statement 3 - Book Lending App Build an application that can be run as a container on the cloud for lending/updating/deleting book for each student. The functionality of the application is: There should be 2 pages/screens/views - Student Page and Book Page. On the Student Page: The user should be able to select a student from a list of students (From Problem Statement 1), Then let them select, update, delete the book(s) (From Problem Statement 2) for that student. On the Books Page: The user should be able to select a book from list of books (From Problem Statement 2), Then let them select, update, delete the student that have chosen the book. Persist all details in the database. Project C: eCommerce Application Security Testing Project: eCommerce Application Security Testing Project is broken up as 1 problem statements. You can implement as many working solutions for problem statements as you can. You can use same or different tech stack/languages for coding each problem statement. Problem Statement - eCommerce Application Develop an effective web and mobile application security testing approach for website and mobile applications for any shopping site/app like flipkart.com, myntra.com, nykaa.com, etc. The testing approach should identify and mitigate potential security vulnerabilities in both the client and server sides of the application. The approach should include: Automated and manual testing techniques such as dynamic and binary analysis Penetration testing Reverse engineering and leverage threat modelling that identify vulnerabilities during the application design phase The solution should document: Approach including strategy Testing process/methodology Security tools List of test cases to be executed against the application. This approach will result in a practical and effective approach that organizations can use to enhance the security posture of their websites and mobile applications. Project D: Elective Subject Selection Project: Elective Subject Selection Project is broken up as 3 problem statements. You can implement as many working solutions for problem statements as you can. You can use same or different tech stack/languages for coding each problem statement. Problem Statement 1 - Student Details App Build an application that can be run as a container on the cloud for creating/updating/deleting a student. The functionality of the application is: Allow user to add, update, delete a student Each student should have: Student Name, Student ID Number, Student Email, Student Phone Number Persist all student details in the database Problem Statement 2 - Elective Subject App Build an application that can be run as a container on the cloud for creating/updating/deleting an elective subject. The functionality of the application is: Allow user to add, update, delete an elective subject Each elective subject should have: Elective Subject Name, Elective Subject Description, Elective Subject Code Persist all subjects in the database Problem Statement 3 - Elective Subject Selection App Build an application that can be run as a container on the cloud for selecting/updating/deleting elective subject for each student. The functionality of the application is: There should be 2 pages/screens/views - Student Page and Elective Subject Page On the Student Page: The user should be able to select a student from a list of students (From Problem Statement 1), Then let them select, update, delete the elective subject(s)(From Problem Statement 2) for that student On the Elective Subject Page: The user should be able to select an elective subject from list of elective subject (From Problem Statement 2), Then let them select, update, delete the student(s) that have chosen the elective subject Persist all details in the database Assessment Criteria: Code maintained on git with commit histories Readme or any other documentation created Follow coding best practices, including comments Design: Ensure SOLID/DRY principles are followed Design patterns are used Code as per the latest syntax using advanced language features Unit testing implemented in code Evaluate work through the commit history to see progress over time, showing consistency. Completeness: Complete the features. Are all the tests running? Correctness: Does the functionality work as per requirement? Maintainability: Is it written in a clean, maintainable way? Debug: Setup logging, linting, and debug capability Hosting: Host as a container application either on the cloud or on a local machine on Docker/Podman Deliverables Solution design and development support guide AFour to provide the template Code for the working solution Demonstration of the working solution Submission Presentation of the problem statement and solution design and approach Source code of the solution for a working solution Registration After registering on Unstop please visit our official AFourathon website and register your team again For more information regarding the Hackathon Timelines please visit our website

title: GPU Hackathon 2023
description: Together with NVIDIA and OpenACC.org, Brookhaven National Laboratory (BNL) will host a virtual Hackathon starting August 15 and concluding August 24, 2023. Open Hackathons provide exciting opportunities for scientists to accelerate their AI or HPC research under the guidance of expert mentors from national laboratories, universities and industry leaders in a collaborative environment. Representing distinguished scholars and preeminent institutions around the world, these teams of mentors and attendees work together to realize performance gains and speedups using a variety of programming models, libraries and tools. Goal: The goal of the Open Hackathon is for computational scientists to port, accelerate and optimize their scientific applications to modern computer architectures, including CPUs, GPUs and other computing technologies. Participating teams should leave the event either with their applications accelerated and/or optimized on the latest supercomputing hardware or a clear roadmap of the next steps needed to leverage these resources. Prerequisites: This Hackathon is open to everyone looking to take their projects to the next level; however, priority acceptance will be given to BNL-affiliated scientists and their collaborators. Teams are expected to be fluent with the code or project they bring to the event and motivated to make progress during the hackathon. A minimum of 3 team members must participate throughout the entire event. Lack of participation for the duration of the Hackathon may cause the entire team to be excused. Projects brought to the event are required to have a license attached and detailed in the application.

title: Blackstone Shipping Hackathon
description: Attention all aspiring engineers, tech enthusiasts and product teams! Are you ready to put your imagination and problem-solving skills to the test and build a product that can revolutionize the logistics and supply chain industry? Then join us for a once-in-a-lifetime hackathon experience where you can showcase your creativity, innovation, and technical proficiency in building a minimum viable product (MVP) or prototype solution that addresses the challenges faced by the supply chain industry. This is your chance to form your own product teams and build your own tech products from scratch! A unique opportunity for you to work on a real-world problem, learn from industry experts, and develop your own product from scratch. By participating in this hackathon, you will not only improve your technical and entrepreneurial skills, but also have the chance to be part of the team that creates the next big thing in the supply chain industry. So, gather your friends, form a team, and let's work together to create something amazing. Join us in this exciting journey to become the best product team and make your mark in the tech world. The stage is set, the challenge is on. Are you ready to build the future and be the change you want to see? " Every success story starts with the decision to TRY " About Us: At Blackstone Shipping, we do more than just moving container boxes. As a dynamic 3-year-old start-up, we are focused on revolutionizing the logistics industry with our innovative approach to freight forwarding, custom clearance, 3PL and 4PL supply chain management services. Our expertise in the field and commitment to customer success has propelled us to grow rapidly, With 20 branch offices spanning across Europe, Asia, the UK, and the USA, we're connecting businesses of all sizes to the world with ease and efficiency.​ We at Blackstone Shipping, strive towards offering sustainable logistics services that seamlessly integrate with real-time data flow, powered by cutting-edge digital technologies. Our diverse talent workforce and rich industry experience allow us to offer end-to-end logistics solutions that are tailored to the unique needs of each client, making international logistics simple and stress-free. ​ Objective: The challenge is to ideate & conceptualize a digital solution and create a functional prototype for the same, to address and solve specific problems faced in logistics & supply chain management by the industry and the respective stakeholders involved in it. Solution Submission Format: The solutions can be in the form of software, website, mobile app, or any other digital solution which effectively solves the above supply chain problems. Ideation Stage: A detailed description of the MVP/prototype solution, including its features, functionalities, and how it addresses specific supply chain challenges. Maximum 5 slides, excluding name & title slides Prototype/Build Stage: A live functional demo of the MVP/prototype, to showcase its capabilities and demonstrate how it solves the supply chain problems. Technical documentation that clearly explains the architecture, technologies used, and step by step implementation details of the MVP/prototype. All prototypes submitted should be original solution submitted by the participating team. However, participants can make use of open-source repositories, API's or no code build platforms to develop their solutions. All such usage of open-source repositories, codes, API integration should be clearly documented. Bonus Round (The Pitch): A business plan that outlines the commercial viability of the MVP/prototype, including its target market, pricing strategy, and go-to-market plan. Expectations: Teams should present a functional MVP/prototype solution that demonstrates its capabilities to address the supply chain challenges. Teams should have a clear understanding of the target market and commercial viability of their solution. Teams should demonstrate creativity, innovation, and technical proficiency of their solutions. Mentoring will be provided to all teams during the prototyping stage to assist with the development of their MVP/prototype solutions. This mentoring will include technical guidance, advice on product design and functionality, and support on business planning and commercial viability. Teams are expected to fully utilize the mentoring sessions to further refine and improve their MVP/prototype solutions. Teams should provide a comprehensive business plan that outlines the commercial viability of their solution. Teams should be prepared to answer questions and provide detailed explanations of their solutions during the final presentation. General Rules: Eligibility: Participants must be currently enrolled in an accredited university or college, or have graduated from one within the past 12 months. Team Size: Teams must consist of no more than four participants. Participants may only belong to one team. Idea Ownership: All ideas and projects developed during the hackathon belong to the participants. However, by participating in the hackathon, participants grant the organizers the right to review and evaluate their ideas and projects for potential commercialization. The decision to pursue any commercialization opportunities will be made solely by the organizers and the participants will be duly compensated for their ideas and projects. Code of Conduct: Participants are expected to behave professionally and respectfully towards all other participants, judges, and organizers. Any form of harassment or discrimination will not be tolerated and may result in disqualification. Judging Criteria: Projects will be judged based on creativity, innovation, technical difficulty, and potential for scalability. Judges' decisions are final. The organizers reserve the right to prioritize solutions that have the potential for commercialization. Prizes: Prizes will be awarded to the top three teams, consisting of INR 50000, INR 30000, and INR 20000 respectively. However, the organizers may choose to award additional compensation for ideas or projects that have a potential for commercialization. Logistics: The final stage of the hackathon will be held on a specific date and location, which will be provided in advance. Participants are responsible for their own transportation and accommodation. Refreshments will be provided by the organizers during the hackathon. Code of Conduct: By participating in the hackathon, participants agree to abide by the code of conduct, which includes provisions against harassment, discrimination, or any other inappropriate behavior. Intellectual Property: All intellectual property developed during the hackathon belongs to the participants. However, participants agree to cooperate with the organizers in evaluating potential commercialization opportunities for their ideas and projects. The decision to pursue any commercialization opportunities will be made solely by the organizers and the participants will be duly compensated for their ideas and projects. Disqualification: Participants who violate any of these rules may be disqualified from the hackathon. The organizers reserve the right to disqualify any participant at any time, for any reason. These rules are intended to ensure a fair and productive hackathon experience for all participants. Participants should read and understand the rules before registering for the event. By participating, participants agree to cooperate with the organizers in evaluating potential commercialization opportunities for their ideas and projects.

title: Kartexage Hackathon: Improving Existing and Future Application Platforms
description: Kartexage Hackathon provides a unique opportunity for developers and enthusiasts to work together on an open-source project aimed at improving existing and future application platforms. By participating in the hackathon, participants will have the opportunity to contribute to a project that has a clear mission and vision to deliver the most compelling web and mobile experiences. They will also get to work with natural language processing technology to analyze and convert website and mobile app content into interactive and engaging content. Through contributing to the project, participants will be able to develop their skills and knowledge in natural language processing technology, web and mobile development, and open-source collaboration. They will also have the chance to interact with a community of like-minded individuals, share knowledge, and learn from others. The hackathon provides an excellent opportunity to gain experience in real-world development projects, and contribute to a valuable resource that will benefit the wider community. Participants will have the satisfaction of knowing that their contribution will help enable brands to deliver highly engaging content and products to their customers, ultimately making it easier for users to interact with their favourite brands in a meaningful way. Overall, the Kartexa Hackathon provides a unique and rewarding opportunity to work on a project with a clear mission and vision, while developing skills and knowledge, and contributing to a valuable open-source resource. Eligibility Criteria and Rules: Eligibility: The Kartexa Hackathon is open to all developers with 6-7 years of JavaScript experience with frameworks. Individuals, teams, and organizations are welcome to participate. Submission: Participants can submit their contributions to the project on the official GitHub repository. All contributions should adhere to the project's guidelines and quality standards. Intellectual property: All contributions to the project should be original and not infringe on any intellectual property rights. By contributing to the project, participants grant permission for their work to be used and distributed under the project's open-source license. Judging: Contributions will be evaluated based on their quality, relevance, and impact. Judges will be appointed by the project organizers, and their decisions will be final. Code of conduct: All participants are expected to adhere to the project's code of conduct, which promotes respect, inclusivity, and professionalism. Relevant information: Participants should be familiar with the project's mission, vision, features, installation instructions, and natural language processing technology. They should also have relevant knowledge and experience in web and mobile development and open-source collaboration. The rules are subject to change, and any updates will be communicated through the event organizer. Round 1: Introduction: Start with an introduction to the project and the hackathon, including the project's mission, vision, and goals. Give a brief overview of your approach to contributing to the project. Project Analysis: Describe your analysis of the project and its existing features. Highlight any areas where you feel you can make improvements or contribute new features. Approach: Outline your approach to the hackathon and your strategy for making contributions to the project. Discuss your plans for collaborating with others and your proposed timeline for completing your contributions. Technical details: Provide technical details of your proposed contributions, including any relevant code snippets or diagrams. Discuss the technologies and frameworks you plan to use and how they will support your contributions. Resources: Discuss any resources you may need to complete your contributions, such as hardware, software, or other support. Conclusion: Wrap up your presentation with a summary of your proposed contributions and how they will improve the project. Encourage the judges to consider your proposal and express your enthusiasm for participating in the hackathon. Remember to keep your presentation clear, concise, and well-organized. Use visual aids where appropriate and be prepared to answer any questions the judges may have. Good luck with your submission!

title: Pickl.AI's Datathon - 4
description: Overview- Pickl.AI's Datathon presents participants with an opportunity to work on a real, data-heavy business case to test their analytics skills against the best minds in the country. Dabble yourself in such a ubiquitous aspect of the modern world. Pickl.AI is an emerging name in the Data Science ed-tech platforms. We at Pickl.AI have decided to bridge the gap between Data Science skills required to actually solve a business problem and that are currently being taught by a myriad of online courses, regularly conducting hackathons and events in various colleges across India. Link to join Pickl.AI's Data Science Community: https://discord.com/invite/ UYRbTdd2Pk Problem Statement : Customer Segmentation- The growing complexities of customer demand have made it mandatory for companies to focus on customer satisfaction. Segmenting customers based on their preferences, age groups, and geographical locations can help organizations create a tailored experience for each user group. Thus enhancing brand loyalty. For example, if an e-commerce business segments its customers by age and preferences, then it can curate product recommendations based on them. This personalization shows customers that their individual needs are a priority for organizations. Thus it keeps them coming back for more purchases. Problem Statement 1: Project Micro App Build an application that can be run as a container on the cloud for creating/updating/deleting a project. The functionality of the application is: Allow users to add, update, and delete a project Each project should have: the project name, project start date, project end date, project manager name, project manager email, daily status report mailing list Persist on all status items in the database Problem Statement 2: Update Status Micro App Build an application that can be run as a container on the cloud for creating/updating/deleting status for each project. The functionality of the application is: Allow the user to add, update, and delete status for a selected week for each project selected by the user from a list of projects (Problem Statement 1) Each team should have: Status, Highlight, Risk, Week ending date Persist on all items in the database Problem Statement 3: Email Report Micro App Build an application that can be run as a container on the cloud for sending out weekly status emails for each project. The functionality of the application is: Allow the user to select a week and a project and then send out the status email based on a template so that all emails look identical The email subject should be Status of (Project Name) for the week ending (Date) The emails should be sent to recipients updated for each project (Problem Statement 1) Skills Database Project: Skills Database Project is broken up into 3 problem statements. You can implement as many working solutions for problem statements as you can. You can use the same or different tech stack/languages for coding each problem statement. Problem Statement 1: Skills List Micro App Build an application that can be run as a container on the cloud for creating/updating/deleting a tech/business skill. The functionality of the application is: Allow users to add, update, or delete a skill - ( Eg: C++, JavaScript, Sales, PM, etc.) Each skill item should have: Skill, Domain - Tech/Business/Leadership Persist on all status items in the database Problem Statement 2: Choose Skills Micro App Build an application that can be run as a container on the cloud for creating/updating/deleting a skill. The functionality of the application is: Allow users to add, update, and delete their own skill level for skills (Created in Problem Statement 1) Each skill item should have: Domain selected from the drop-down list, skill selected from the drop-down list (auto-populate a list for each domain - Tech/Business/PM), Skill Level - Basic/Intermediate/Expert, Years of Experience Persist on all status items in the database Problem Statement 3: Skills Report Micro App Build an application that can be run as a container on the cloud for viewing list of team members based on skill criteria. The functionality of the application is: Allow users to display a list of team members based on filter criteria for skills Allow user to download the filtered team member list as an MS Excel report Daily Status Reporting Project: Daily Status Reporting Project is broken up into 4 problem statements. You can implement as many working solutions for problem statements as you can. You can use the same or different tech stack/languages for coding each problem statement. Problem Statement 1: Project Micro App Build an application that can be run as a container on the cloud for creating/updating/deleting a project. The functionality of the application is: Allow users to add, update, or delete a project Each project should have: Project Name, Project Start Date, Project End Date, Project Manager Name, Project Manager Email, Daily Status Report Mailing List Persist on all status items in the database Problem Statement 2: Team Micro App Build an application that can be run as a container on the cloud for creating/updating/deleting a team in the project. The functionality of the application is: Allow the user to add, update, or delete a team in a selected project (Created in Problem Statement 1) Each team should have: Team Name, Team Start Date, Team End Date, Team Lead Name, Team Lead Email, List of team members Persist on all teams in the database Problem Statement 3: Status Micro App Build an application that can be run as a container on the cloud for creating/updating/deleting daily status for each project by a team member. The functionality of the application is: Allow user to select themselves from list of team members in the a list of teams (Problem Statement 2). Then let them add, update, delete daily status for themselves Each status item should have: Ticket ID, Hours Spent, Status - In Progress/Blocked/Completed/PTO/In Review, Comments Persist all status items in the database Problem Statement 4: Email Report Micro App Build an application that can be run as a container on the cloud for sending out daily status emails for each project. The functionality of the application is: Every weekday at 10 PM send out the daily status email based on a template so that all emails look identical The email subject should be the Daily Status Report of (Project Name) for (Date) The emails should be sent to all team members in that project and also to recipients updated for each project (Problem Statement 1) Assessment Criteria: Code maintained on git with commit histories Readme or any other documentation created Follow coding best practices including comments Design: ensure solid/ dry principles are followed, design patterns are used, code as per the latest syntax using advanced language features, unit testing is implemented in the code Completeness: Complete the features. Are all the tests running? Correctness: Does the functionality work as per requirement? Maintainability: Is it written in a clean, maintainable way? Debug: Setup logging, linting, and debug capability Hosting: Host as a container application either on the cloud or on a local machine on Docker/ Podman Deliverables: Solution design and development support guide (AFour to provide the template) Code for the working solution Demonstration of the working solution Submission: Presentation of the problem statement and solution design and approach Source code of the solution for working solution Disclaimer: Kindly visit our official website and re-register for our Hackathon event by choosing the number of Problem Statements and Projects you can solve. You will find the details on our event promo banner!

title: Genie X Hub represents Project : Eclipse Hackathon
description: Genie X Hub Presents: PROJECT ECLIPSE HACKATHON Build AI That Thinks, Acts & Automates - Not Just Answers. Project Eclipse Hackathon is a hybrid AI-focused hackathon by Genie Hive Private Limited , designed for college students, developers, AI enthusiasts, designers, and innovators who want to build practical solutions using Generative AI, Agentic AI, Autonomous Systems, and Intelligent Automation . This is more than a conventional chatbot-building competition. Participants are challenged to build systems that can understand problems, reason, use tools and APIs, execute actions, verify outcomes, and involve humans when necessary . The hackathon features 5 curated real-world AI challenges + 1 Open Innovation challenge . Whatsapp Community: Join this community for all the event updates : https://chat.whatsapp.com/CwOLKlgym1W4TpcNDx8TUC THE ECLIPSE CHALLENGE AI is moving beyond systems that simply generate responses. Project Eclipse focuses on systems that follow the workflow: INPUT → UNDERSTAND → PLAN → USE TOOLS → ACT → VERIFY → RECOVER / ESCALATE Participants are encouraged to build working AI systems that solve meaningful problems and demonstrate real task completion rather than simply generating convincing text. CHALLENGE TRACKS Participants can choose one of five curated challenges or participate in the OPEN-X Open Innovation Challenge . 01 - AI Agent for Production Incident Investigation & Recovery Build an autonomous production-operations agent that investigates a simulated production incident across application logs, infrastructure metrics, deployment history, Git commits, alerts, and service dependencies. The system should demonstrate capabilities such as: • Multi-source investigation • Tool/API calling • Reasoning over temporal events • Root-cause hypothesis generation • Confidence estimation • Remediation planning • Human approval for high-impact actions • Recovery verification • Post-incident report generation 02 - Autonomous Resolution of Cross-System Transaction Mismatches Build an AI agent that investigates transaction mismatches across invoices, payment records, purchase orders, emails, spreadsheets, and accounting/ERP systems. The system should be able to: • Ingest data from multiple sources • Match transactions/entities • Retrieve supporting evidence • Classify discrepancies using context • Detect partial, duplicate, or missing payments • Recommend appropriate actions • Maintain an auditable action trail • Use human approval for consequential updates 03 - From Contract Language to Executable Business Actions Build an AI agent that converts contracts into executable compliance workflows. Your system should be able to: • Extract obligations • Identify responsible parties and deadlines • Reason over conditional clauses • Generate tasks and workflows • Send reminders and escalations • Maintain compliance records • Handle document hierarchy and amendments • Resolve conflicts between contract documents and instructions 04 - Autonomous Requirement-to-Quotation Procurement System Build an AI procurement agent that takes a natural-language purchase requirement and analyzes vendor quotations. The system should: • Understand requirements • Parse quotations from documents, emails, or structured files • Normalize specifications • Check mandatory constraints • Compare cost and trade-offs • Detect anomalies • Simulate vendor clarification/negotiation • Prepare a recommendation for human approval The goal is not simply to identify the cheapest quotation, but to determine whether a quotation actually satisfies the required specifications. 05 - Issue-to-Pull-Request AI Engineering Agent Build an AI software-engineering agent that receives a repository, issue description, and acceptance criteria and takes the problem from: ISSUE → INVESTIGATION → IMPLEMENTATION → TESTING → PULL REQUEST The agent should demonstrate: • Repository exploration • Issue and acceptance-criteria understanding • Technical hypothesis formation • Code modification • Test execution • Failure analysis and iteration • Patch/PR generation • Human review before deployment OPEN-X - OPEN INNOVATION Have your own problem worth solving? Build beyond the brief. In OPEN-X , participants can define their own real-world problem and build an original solution using Generative AI, Agentic AI, Autonomous Workflows, or Intelligent Automation . Your submission should explain: Problem - What real-world problem are you solving? Target Users - Who experiences this problem? Existing Gap - Why are existing approaches insufficient? Proposed Solution - What are you building and how does it work? AI / Agent Component - Why does the solution meaningfully require GenAI, agents, or intelligent automation? Demonstration - Can you demonstrate the system working end-to-end? Impact - What changes if your solution is deployed? A conventional application with an AI label added on top is not sufficient for the Open Innovation challenge. ️ HACKATHON TIMELINE Registration 20 September - 30 September 2026 Online Round 1 - Idea Submission 01 October - 06 October 2026 Online Shortlisted Teams Announcement 09 October 2026 Round 2 - Building Phase 11 October - 23 October 2026 Online Finalists Announcement 25 October 2026 Grand Finale 27 October 2026 Offline - Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India Grand Finale venue: To Be Announced All preliminary rounds will be conducted online. title: Solve - a - Thon | National Hackathon
organizer: Swami Rama Himalayan University (SRHU), Baksar Wala, Uttarakhand
description: Overview: AI for Sustainable Development Goals (AI for SDGs): Solve-a-Thon 2026 is a National 24-Hour Hackathon organized by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering, School of Science & Technology (SST), Swami Rama Himalayan University (SRHU), Dehradun, Uttarakhand. Scheduled for 27-28 November 2026, Solve-a-Thon is designed to bring together student innovators, programmers, AI/ML enthusiasts, developers, researchers, and multidisciplinary problem-solvers from across India to develop innovative technology-driven solutions for real-world challenges aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The hackathon focuses on the theme "AI for SDGs", encouraging participants to explore the use of Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Data Science, Software Development, and other relevant emerging technologies to address challenges in areas such as Healthcare, Education, Climate Action, Agriculture, Smart Cities, Governance, Clean Water, and Open Innovation. Solve-a-Thon is designed as more than a conventional coding competition. It provides participants with an opportunity to identify a meaningful problem, develop an innovative solution, build a functional prototype, receive technical guidance, and demonstrate their work before an expert evaluation panel. The Solve-a-Thon Challenge: The challenge is simple: Identify a real-world problem. Build an innovative technology-driven solution. Demonstrate how your solution can create meaningful impact. Participants will work in teams to transform their ideas into functional prototypes, applications, models, or demonstrable proofs of concept. The hackathon emphasizes not only coding and technical implementation but also innovation, problem relevance, feasibility, practical applicability, social/environmental impact, scalability, and the team's understanding of the proposed solution. Hackathon Themes: Participants can develop solutions under any of the following themes: AI for Healthcare: Develop innovative AI-powered solutions addressing healthcare challenges, patient support, health monitoring, diagnostics, preventive healthcare, accessibility, and related real-world healthcare needs. AI for Education: Build intelligent solutions that can improve teaching and learning, personalized education, assessment, educational accessibility, student engagement, and other challenges in the education ecosystem. AI for Climate Action: Use AI and emerging technologies to address climate-related challenges, environmental sustainability, monitoring, resource optimization, climate resilience, and awareness. AI for Agriculture: Develop technology-driven solutions for smart agriculture, crop monitoring, agricultural decision support, resource optimization, sustainable farming, food security, and other agriculture-related challenges. AI for Smart Cities: Create intelligent solutions for urban challenges including public services, mobility, infrastructure, resource management, citizen services, safety, sustainability, and other smart-city applications. AI for Governance: Explore innovative solutions that can improve public services, citizen engagement, administrative processes, accessibility, transparency, and data-driven decision-making. AI for Clean Water: Develop solutions addressing water quality, conservation, monitoring, contamination, distribution, sustainable water management, and other clean-water challenges. Open Theme: Have an innovative idea outside the listed themes? The Open Theme provides participants with the flexibility to identify a meaningful real-world problem and develop an innovative technology-based solution. Who Can Participate? The hackathon is open to eligible students participating through their institutions. Participants should have an interest or background in areas such as: Programming Artificial Intelligence Machine Learning Data Science Software Development Emerging Technologies Participants from multidisciplinary backgrounds are encouraged to form teams, bringing together different technical and domain perspectives to create stronger solutions. Team Size: Each team must consist of 3 to 5 members. Every team must nominate one Team Leader, who will be responsible for official communication and submission-related activities. Each team may also have one mentor to provide guidance and support during the hackathon. Mentor details are to be submitted to the Organizing Committee during registration. Hackathon Format: Solve-a-Thon will follow a two-stage process consisting of an initial online screening round followed by the main offline hackathon. Round 1 - Online Screening: Teams will first complete the prescribed registration process and undergo verification by the Organizing Committee. Registered teams will submit their problem statement in the prescribed HIMOVATION 2026 template within the announced deadline. The submitted problem statements will be evaluated by the designated evaluation panel, and eligible teams will be shortlisted for the next stage. Round 2 - Offline 24-Hour Hackathon: Shortlisted teams will be invited to Swami Rama Himalayan University (SRHU), Dehradun for the main hackathon. The offline stage will begin with an orientation covering the hackathon guidelines, rules, schedule, evaluation criteria, and other important information. Teams will then begin the development and coding phase and work continuously on their proposed solutions. The hackathon will include: Orientation Coding & Development Progress Review Overnight Development Final Submission Presentation & Demonstration Final Evaluation Teams will receive technical guidance and mentoring during the development phase. A progress evaluation will also be conducted during the hackathon to review the development status of participating teams. At the end of the 24-hour development period, teams will submit their completed projects in the prescribed format and present their final solutions before the evaluation panel. What Should You Build? Teams are expected to develop an original and innovative solution addressing a clearly identified problem. The final project may take the form of a: Functional prototype Application AI/ML model Software solution Demonstrable proof of concept Participants should clearly demonstrate: The problem being addressed The proposed solution How AI or relevant emerging technologies are being used Relevance to the selected SDG or real-world problem Technologies, tools, datasets, and frameworks used Working functionality or proof of concept Potential practical application and impact Teams must also ensure that their submitted work does not violate applicable intellectual property or copyright requirements. What Will the Jury Look For? Projects may be evaluated on the following parameters: Innovation & Originality: How innovative and original is the proposed solution? Problem/Theme Relevance: How effectively does the solution address the selected problem or theme? Technical Implementation: How well has the proposed solution been technically implemented? Use of AI/Emerging Technology: How effectively are AI or relevant emerging technologies utilized? Feasibility & Practical Applicability: Can the solution realistically be implemented and used? Social/Environmental Impact: What potential impact can the solution create? Scalability: Can the solution be expanded or adapted for larger-scale use? Prototype Quality: How functional, complete, and demonstrable is the prototype? Presentation & Demonstration: How clearly does the team communicate and demonstrate its solution? Teamwork & Understanding: Do team members demonstrate clear understanding of their solution and effective collaboration? 24-Hour Build Experience: Solve-a-Thon is a continuous 24-hour coding and development challenge. Teams will have to effectively manage their time between ideation, development, testing, debugging, documentation, and final presentation. Mandatory progress reviews will be conducted during the hackathon, and teams must remain prepared to demonstrate the progress and functionality of their solutions. The overnight development phase will provide teams with an opportunity to refine, test, and strengthen their prototypes before final submission. Food & Refreshments: During the hackathon, running tea and snacks during the daytime, along with dinner, will be provided to participants. Additional meals, refreshments, or personal food requirements will be the responsibility of participants. Food stalls will also be available at the venue on a paid basis. Rest Area & Hackathon Arena: Separate rest areas will be provided for male and female participants. Participants are required to follow the instructions of the Organizing Committee regarding the use of these facilities. For effective participation and monitoring, at least 50% of each team must remain present in the Hackathon Arena throughout the event. Rules & Responsible Participation: Participants are expected to maintain professional conduct throughout the hackathon. Solutions must be developed during the designated competition period, subject to the rules announced during orientation. Plagiarism and direct copying of another team's work are strictly prohibited. Teams may use publicly available libraries, frameworks, APIs, and datasets in accordance with their applicable licenses. Any external work, resource, dataset, or pre-existing component must be properly declared wherever required. Failure to submit the project within the prescribed deadline may result in disqualification. Teams must be prepared to demonstrate their working prototype before the jury. Prizes & Recognition: The total cash prize pool for Solve-a-Thon 2026 is ₹93,000. 1st Prize: ₹51,000 2nd Prize: ₹31,000 3rd Prize: ₹11,000 Winners will receive Certificates of Achievement along with the announced cash prizes. Registration: Registration Fee: ₹800 per team Teams must complete the registration process within the announced deadline. Registration details must include the names and institutional details of all team members. As per the hackathon guidelines, the initial online screening stage is conducted before the main offline stage. Teams participating only in Round 1 are not required to pay the registration fee at that stage. The applicable registration fee is required only for shortlisted teams proceeding to the subsequent stages, subject to the instructions and deadline communicated by the Organizing Committee. Registration will be confirmed only after successful payment and verification by the Organizing Committee. Event Details: Event: Solve-a-Thon 2026 - National 24-Hour Hackathon Theme: AI for Sustainable Development Goals (AI for SDGs) Date: 27-28 November 2026 Duration: 24 Hours Mode: Offline / On-Campus for shortlisted teams Venue: School of Science & Technology (SST), Swami Rama Himalayan University, Dehradun, Uttarakhand Team Size: 3-5 Members Registration Fee: ₹800 per shortlisted team Prize Pool: ₹93,000 Why Solve-a-Thon? Solve-a-Thon gives participants the opportunity to move beyond classroom exercises and work on problems that have real-world relevance. It is an opportunity to: Compete at a National-Level Hackathon Build an AI-powered solution for an SDG-linked challenge Work on a real-world problem within a 24-hour development environment Collaborate with a multidisciplinary team Receive technical guidance and mentoring Showcase a functional prototype before an expert jury Strengthen programming, AI, problem-solving, teamwork, and presentation skills Explore the practical application of emerging technologies Connect innovation with social and environmental impact Ready to Solve? You have 24 hours to turn an idea into a solution. Choose a problem that matters. Build something meaningful. Use technology intelligently. Demonstrate your impact. Think. Build. Solve. Impact.

title: Cerebro Hackathon
description: CEREBRO - Neural Sentiment Hackathon Where minds decode emotion at machine speed. CEREBRO is a 36-hour online hackathon organized by the Department of Computer Science & Engineering, Institute of Engineering & Management (IEM), Kolkata . The hackathon challenges participants to build systems that can understand and analyze human emotion, sentiment, and tone across different forms of communication. Participants will choose one of three problem statements and develop a functional solution using their own technology stack, models, and approach. CEREBRO focuses on practical applications of Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Natural Language Processing, Speech Processing, and Affective Computing . Problem Statements PS-01 - Tone Intelligence in Conversations First Prize: ₹5,000 Chat conversations contain more than words. They can reveal tension, sarcasm, warmth, frustration, and escalation. Build a system that analyzes the emotional arc of a multi-turn conversation and identifies changes in tone throughout the conversation. Key requirements: Multi-turn chat sentiment and tone tracking Sarcasm, passive-aggression, and irony detection Emotion-arc visualization over the conversation Support for chat formats such as WhatsApp, Slack, Discord, or similar exports Participants must source their own data and develop their own approach PS-02 - Voice as a Mood Signal Second Prize: ₹3,000 The emotional state behind a sentence can change dramatically depending on how it is spoken. Build a system that extracts emotional information directly from raw audio , using characteristics such as pitch, prosody, speech rate, and pauses. Key requirements: Audio-based emotion classification Continuous valence and arousal estimation Robustness to noisy, accented, or code-switched speech Emotion should primarily be inferred from the audio signal itself Participants must source their own training data PS-03 - Sentiment Drift in Social Threads Third Prize: ₹2,000 Online discussions can begin calmly and quickly become hostile or toxic. Build a system that analyzes a sequence of comments and identifies where the emotional tone changes , including the specific point where sentiment significantly deteriorates. Key requirements: Sequential or graph-based thread modelling Sentiment drift detection Early-warning toxicity signals Data sourced from platforms such as Reddit, X, or YouTube Interpretable output showing which reply contributed to the sentiment shift Prize Pool Total Prize Pool: ₹10,000 Problem Statement Prize PS-01 - Tone Intelligence in Conversations ₹5,000 PS-02 - Voice as a Mood Signal ₹3,000 PS-03 - Sentiment Drift in Social Threads ₹2,000 Total ₹10,000 Schedule Date & Time Event October 15, 2026 Registration opens on Unstop November 1, 2026 Problem statements published November 2, 2026 - 9:00 PM IST Hackathon begins November 3, 2026 - 9:00 AM IST Halfway mark and optional mentor Q&A November 4, 2026 - 3:00 AM IST 6 hours remaining November 4, 2026 - 9:00 AM IST Submissions close November 4, 2026 - 12:00 PM IST Judging begins November 5, 2026 Winners announced Hackathon Duration: 36 hours Format: Fully online Registration: Free What CEREBRO Is About: CEREBRO is built around the intersection of AI and human emotion . Participants are encouraged to go beyond basic sentiment classification and explore how machines can understand changing emotional states across conversations, speech, and social interactions. Participants are free to choose their own programming languages, frameworks, models, datasets, and development approaches. The focus is on building a real, functional system rather than simply wrapping an existing AI API with a user interface. Who Can Participate? CEREBRO is open to students, developers, researchers, AI/ML enthusiasts, and anyone interested in building technology around emotion and sentiment intelligence. Teams can participate in the hackathon and work remotely from anywhere. Organized by Department of Computer Science & Engineering Institute of Engineering & Management (IEM), Kolkata CEREBRO - Neural Sentiment Hackathon November 2-4, 2026 · 36 Hours · Online

title: WebRush - 6-Hour Frontend Hackathon
description: Overview WebRush - 6-Hour Frontend Hackathon WebRush is a fully online, individual frontend hackathon where participants get 6 hours to build a complete web solution for a given challenge . But there's a twist - you don't get just one shot at your score. The Challenge At the beginning of the hackathon, one common problem statement will be provided to all participants. Your task is to design and develop the best possible frontend solution within the 6-hour time limit . You can choose your own approach, design, frontend framework, libraries, and tools - but your final submission must follow the challenge requirements. Automated Evaluation with FAIE Engine Your project will be evaluated automatically using the FAIE Engine , an automated frontend evaluation and scoring system. The evaluation focuses on aspects such as: UI/UX & Visual Quality Required Features & Functionality Code Quality & Structure Responsiveness Accessibility & Performance Project Documentation Overall implementation of the given challenge No manual judging panel is required for scoring. Your submission is analyzed and scored through the evaluation engine. 3 Chances to Improve Your Score Every participant gets up to 3 chances to submit and improve their project during the allowed submission window. You can use these attempts strategically: Build → Evaluate → Improve → Resubmit Each evaluation provides a score, allowing you to identify areas that need improvement and work towards a better final score. Your highest valid score will be considered for the final leaderboard. Leaderboard = Final Results This isn't just about completing the challenge - your score determines your position. Participants will be ranked on the final leaderboard based on their highest achieved score . Highest Rank → Winner Second Highest Rank → Runner-Up Other top-ranked participants → As per the final leaderboard ️ Technology Rules Individual participation only. Fully online hackathon. Frontend development only. Modern frontend frameworks, libraries, UI tools, and development tools are allowed. Backend technologies and backend implementation are not allowed. The project must be developed within the 6-hour hackathon duration . Previously built projects cannot be submitted. Submission Participants will submit: Live deployed website GitHub repository Required project details All submissions must be made within the specified hackathon timeline. One Challenge. Six Hours. Three Chances. One Leaderboard. Build fast. Get evaluated. Improve your score. Climb the leaderboard. Welcome to WebRush.

Hackathon Welcome to the Innovation Hackathon, a competition where teams collaborate to develop innovative solutions for the provided problem statements. The task involves creating a Microsoft PowerPoint presentation consisting of a maximum of 8 slides, excluding the Welcome and Thank You slides. It is important to note that the term "Hack" in Hackathon refers to development and creative problem-solving, not any illegal activity. Each Hackathon is unique, with different themes, rules, and participant demographics. Participants are required to provide comprehensive details about their proposed solutions, including relevant technical components such as circuit diagrams, program flowcharts, mechanical designs, models, or other applicable elements. This ensures clarity, thorough understanding, and transparency in presenting their ideas. Success in this competition relies on creativity, originality, innovation, and the ability to effectively address the given problem statement. Detailed Description Phase 1 - Registration and Submission Round Greetings, Participants! We are thrilled to present you with an opportunity to not only showcase your skills but also contribute towards solving significant real-world and global challenges. Each participant/team will receive a set of problem statements from which they must choose one problem statement and develop a suitable solution. Each team can consist of a maximum of 4 members. Female participation in the team is preferable. Originality is key. Any form of plagiarism may result in immediate disqualification. Your presentation should consist of a maximum of 8 slides, excluding the Welcome and Thank You slides, incorporating the following elements wherever applicable: Introduction Problem Understanding Proposed Solution Operational Mechanism / Working Principle Real-World Applications Advantages and Limitations Cost Analysis Future Scope Depending on the nature of your chosen problem statement, clearly present the relevant technical depth, such as: Circuit Diagram Program Flowchart Working Mechanism Chemical Reaction Mechanical Design or Modeling AI/ML-Based Approach System Architecture Include only the technical elements that are relevant to your proposed solution. In this phase, teams will have the opportunity to present and pitch their proposed solution before the judges. Each team will have a maximum of 8 minutes to provide a comprehensive explanation of their solution. Teams should clearly explain their proposed solution and its working mechanism and should be prepared to answer questions related to their idea, technical implementation, feasibility, and real-world applications. Be prepared to delve into the intricacies of your presentation and impress the judges with your innovative ideas and thorough understanding of the problem statement. Let's make this Hackathon an unforgettable journey towards innovation, creativity, and problem-solving! Analyze technical design, energy storage, load management, cost, and social acceptance. Effective Monitoring and Alternative System to Prevent Stubble Burning Propose a practical solution to monitor and reduce stubble burning in Punjab-Haryana, with alternative uses such as animal feed or biofuel. Groundwater Conservation and Over-Extraction Control System Design an integrated system to control excessive groundwater extraction in agricultural regions using monitoring and awareness mechanisms. Low-Cost Safety and Monitoring System for Elderly Living Alone Develop an affordable monitoring system that detects falls or unusual activity among elderly people and alerts their family members. Transparent and Leakage-Free Public Distribution System (PDS) Design a practical model using biometric and digital tracking to reduce corruption and leakage in the Public Distribution System. Source Segregation and Optimized Waste Collection System Design an efficient urban waste management model that promotes source segregation and optimizes waste collection routes. Affordable Crop Preservation / Cold Storage for Small Farmers Propose a low-cost cold storage or preservation method for vegetables and fruits to reduce post-harvest losses. Mental Health Support System for Schools and Colleges Design a practical and privacy-preserving system that helps students manage mental stress and connects them to appropriate counseling support. Urban Flood Early Warning and Evacuation Planning System Develop an integrated plan for flood prediction and safe evacuation during heavy rainfall in urban areas. Affordable Mobility Assistive Device for Persons with Disabilities Design a low-cost and functional wheelchair or mobility aid with a focus on ergonomics, affordability, and usability. Air Pollution Monitoring and Public Health Alert System for Industrial Areas Propose a system to monitor air quality in industrial zones and provide timely health alerts to nearby residents. Improved Resource Management Model for Hospitals Design a smart management system for the efficient allocation of hospital resources such as beds, oxygen, equipment, and staff. Skill-Based Income Generation Platform for Rural Women Create a platform concept that maps the skills of rural women and connects them with suitable income-generating opportunities. Sustainable Urban Farming Model for Limited Spaces Design a cost-effective model for growing vegetables in limited urban spaces such as rooftops, balconies, or small residential areas. Smart Community Health Monitoring for Water-Borne Diseases in Rural Areas Design an integrated solution for early warning and community health monitoring of water-borne diseases in rural areas. Smart Tourist Safety Monitoring & Incident Response System Design a complete system using AI, Geo-fencing, and Digital ID for tourist safety, especially in hilly or remote regions. Water-Borne Disease Early Warning System (Community Level) Design a system that monitors water quality and basic health indicators to provide early warnings for water-borne diseases. title: Data Analytics Hackathon
description: This is a build-and-analysis-focused Data Analytics Hackathon designed for students, aspiring analysts, data professionals, and problem-solvers who want to turn raw data into meaningful insights and actionable recommendations. What You'll Do: On 27th September , 11 AM to 12 PM (IST) participants will work with a real-world dataset provided by the organizers and perform an end-to-end data analysis by: Understanding the business problem and dataset. Cleaning, transforming, and preparing the data. Exploring patterns, trends, and relationships. Performing quantitative and statistical analysis. Building meaningful visualizations and dashboards. Identifying key insights and actionable recommendations. Presenting your analysis and findings. The challenge is centered around using data to solve real-world problems by turning raw datasets into clear insights and data-driven decisions. By the end of the Hackathon, you'll have a complete analysis project that can be showcased in your portfolio, discussed during interviews, or further developed into a real-world analytics solution. Who Can Participate? Individuals and teams are welcome. Recommended team size: Max 2 members & Individualy can also Participate. Beginners and experienced analysts can participate. Participants can use Python, SQL, Excel, Power BI, Tableau, and other analytics tools. Project Requirements: Every team must: Perform the analysis using the dataset provided during the event. Clearly document the analysis process and methodology. Explain the problem statement, approach, findings, and recommendations. Submit a complete and functional analysis with supporting visualizations. Submission Checklist: To complete your submission, provide: Final analysis report or presentation. Dashboard and/or data visualizations. Source code/notebook or analysis file, where applicable. Brief explanation of the methodology and key findings. Key insights and actionable recommendations. Rules & Judging Criteria: Event Rules: Participants must use the dataset provided by the organizers. Pre-built analyses or previously completed projects are not permitted. External tools, libraries, and publicly available resources may be used. Any form of plagiarism or unauthorized copying will result in disqualification. Participants must disclose the use of AI tools in their analysis or submission. All submissions must be completed and submitted before the official deadline. Evaluation Areas: Projects will be assessed based on: Data cleaning and preparation. Analytical approach and problem-solving. Quality and accuracy of insights. Data visualization and storytelling. Depth of analysis. Business relevance and actionable recommendations. Overall presentation and completeness. Turn data into insights, uncover the story behind the numbers, and show how analytics can drive better decisions.
