Themes & Broad Problem Areas: Problem Statements Track 1: Edge AI & Computer Vision PS-01: AI-Based Smart Campus Safety System Develop an edge-AI solution that can detect potentially unsafe situations such as crowding, falls, unauthorized entry, or abnormal activity using cameras and provide real-time alerts without continuously sending sensitive video data to the cloud. PS-02: Intelligent Road Hazard Detection Develop an on-device computer vision system that identifies potholes, road cracks, obstacles, pedestrians, and other hazards in real time and provides alerts to drivers or authorities. PS-03: AI-Based Waste Segregation Build an intelligent system capable of identifying different categories of waste using computer vision and automatically assisting in segregation at the point of disposal. PS-04: Smart Retail Shelf Monitoring Develop an edge-AI solution that detects empty shelves, misplaced products, and inventory conditions using cameras and provides real-time notifications. Track 2: Healthcare & Assistive Technology PS-05: AI-Powered Assistive System for Visually Impaired People Develop a portable intelligent device that uses computer vision and on-device AI to identify obstacles, objects, signs, or people and communicate useful information through audio or haptic feedback. PS-06: Edge AI-Based Elderly Fall Detection Develop a privacy-preserving system that detects when an elderly person falls and automatically generates an emergency alert without requiring continuous cloud processing. PS-08: Smart Medicine Management System Develop an intelligent connected device that helps users manage medication schedules, detects missed doses, and provides alerts to caregivers when necessary. PS-10: Smart Energy Optimization Build an IoT and Edge AI solution that monitors electricity consumption and intelligently recommends or automatically implements energy-saving actions. PS-11: AI-Based Water Leakage Detection Develop a sensor-based intelligent system that detects abnormal water flow or leakage and generates real-time alerts to minimize water wastage. PS-12: Smart Air Quality Monitoring Develop a low-cost connected device that monitors environmental parameters and uses edge intelligence to identify pollution patterns and provide actionable alerts. PS-14: AI-Based Driver Assistance System Develop an edge-AI solution capable of detecting driver distraction, drowsiness, lane departure, or nearby obstacles and generating timely warnings. PS-15: Smart Agricultural Rover Develop an autonomous agricultural robot that can monitor crops, identify plant health conditions, detect weeds, or assist with precision agriculture. PS-16: Search-and-Rescue Intelligent Robot Develop a robotic system capable of navigating hazardous or difficult environments while detecting people, obstacles, temperature anomalies, or other indicators useful during rescue operations. Track 5: Connected Intelligence & IoT PS-17: Smart Home Energy Guardian Develop an intelligent IoT system that monitors household appliances and automatically identifies unnecessary energy consumption and abnormal usage patterns. PS-18: Intelligent Industrial Monitoring System Develop an edge-IoT solution that monitors machines using sensors and detects abnormal operating conditions before equipment failure occurs. PS-19: Smart Agriculture Monitoring Platform Build an IoT system that monitors soil moisture, temperature, humidity, and other agricultural parameters & uses AI to recommend irrigation or crop-management actions. PS-20: Connected Disaster Alert System Develop a resilient IoT-based system capable of detecting conditions such as floods, fires, earthquakes, or other environmental hazards and distributing local emergency alerts even when conventional connectivity is limited

title: Built With Talent S1 | Hiring Hackathon
description: Build. Compete. Solve. Showcase. Build With Talent S1 is a 7-day remote team-based hackathon designed to challenge students, developers, and technology enthusiasts to solve a real-world problem by turning an idea into a functional and practical solution. Participants will form teams, receive a problem statement, and work together to ideate, design, develop, test, and present their solution within a defined 7-day challenge period. The competition focuses on problem-solving, technical execution, creativity, innovation, product thinking, teamwork, and the ability to build a meaningful solution under a deadline. Whether you are an experienced developer or participating in your first hackathon, this is an opportunity to challenge yourself, collaborate with others, and build something you can proudly showcase. One problem. Seven days. One team. One solution. Who Can Participate? The hackathon is open to: College and university students Aspiring developers and technology enthusiasts Students interested in software development and technology Individuals interested in product building and problem-solving Anyone passionate about building innovative technology solutions Participants from different colleges, cities, and backgrounds are welcome to form teams. The hackathon is completely remote, allowing participants to collaborate from anywhere. Eligibility: Participants must be 18 years or older . Open to students. Teams must consist of 2-4 members . Each participant can be part of only one team . Cross-college and cross-city teams are allowed. All team members must complete the required registration. Participants must be able to commit to the complete 7-day development period . All submitted work must be original and attributable to the registered team. How the Competition Works: Stage 1 | Registration: Participants register individually or as a team and provide the required participant and team information. Teams may collaborate with members from different colleges, cities, and institutions. Stage 2 | Assessment: Registered participants may be required to complete an online aptitude and problem-solving assessment. The assessment may cover areas such as: Logical reasoning Analytical thinking Problem-solving Basic technical understanding Decision-making Stage 3 | Team Shortlisting: Eligible teams will be shortlisted based on the applicable competition criteria and assessment performance. Shortlisted teams will receive the information required to participate in the main hackathon challenge. Stage 4 | Problem Statement: Shortlisted teams will receive a real-world problem statement along with the challenge requirements, expectations, evaluation criteria, and submission guidelines. Once the challenge begins: The 7-day clock starts. Stage 5 | Build for 7 Days: Teams will work remotely to transform the problem statement into a functional solution. Participants are encouraged to demonstrate: Problem understanding Product thinking Technical execution Creativity Innovation Team collaboration Practical implementation Teams are free to plan their own workflow and divide responsibilities among members. Stage 6 | Submission: Teams will submit their completed solution before the announced deadline. Depending on the challenge requirements, submissions may include: Project repository Deployed application Demo video Project documentation Presentation Technical details Other materials specified in the problem statement Stage 7 | Evaluation: Submitted projects will be reviewed by the evaluation panel. Projects will be evaluated according to the published competition criteria, with emphasis on the quality, creativity, functionality, and practical value of the solution. Stage 8 | Final Results: The highest-performing teams will be selected based on the overall evaluation. Final results will be announced after completion of the evaluation process. Outstanding teams and participants may receive recognition, certificates, awards, or other benefits according to the final event structure. Hackathon Format: Stage Format Registration Online Assessment Online Team Shortlisting Based on applicable criteria Problem Statement Released digitally Development 7 Days - Fully Remote Submission Online Project Evaluation Evaluation Panel Final Results Based on Competition Performance Recognition Selected Participants/Teams What You Need to Build: Once your team is selected for the main challenge, you will receive a problem statement describing a real-world challenge. Your objective is to transform that challenge into a functional, thoughtful, and practical solution . Think: Understand → Ideate → Plan → Design → Build → Test → Deploy → Present The goal isn't simply to write code. We're looking for teams that can understand a problem, make thoughtful decisions, build effectively, and present a solution that provides genuine value. Evaluation Criteria: Problem Understanding: How clearly does the team understand the given problem, its requirements, and its potential users? Solution Quality: How effectively does the proposed solution address the problem statement? Technical Execution: How well does the solution work? Is the implementation technically sound, functional, and reliable? Innovation & Creativity: Does the solution demonstrate an original, creative, or improved approach to the problem? User Experience: Is the solution intuitive, accessible, and thoughtfully designed? Completeness: How much of the proposed solution has been implemented within the challenge period? Scalability & Practicality: Could the solution realistically be developed further or applied in a real-world environment? Team Collaboration: How effectively did the team collaborate, divide responsibilities, and work together throughout the challenge? Presentation & Demonstration: How clearly can the team explain its solution, decisions, implementation, challenges, and results? Competition Rules: Participation: Each participant can register with only one team . Each team must have 2-4 members . Team members may belong to different colleges, cities, or institutions. Team composition cannot be changed after shortlisting unless explicitly permitted by the organizers. Project Development: The project must be developed during the designated 7-day hackathon period . Previously developed projects cannot be submitted as the primary solution. Teams may use publicly available libraries, frameworks, APIs, and development tools unless specifically restricted in the problem statement. Teams must be able to explain and demonstrate the work submitted. Submission: Only one final submission is permitted per team. Submissions must be made before the announced deadline. Late submissions may not be considered. Teams may be required to provide a repository, deployed application, demo video, documentation, presentation, or other materials specified by the organizers. Integrity: Plagiarism, impersonation, falsification, or submission of another team's work will result in disqualification. Sharing complete solutions or substantial portions of project work between teams is prohibited. Any attempt to manipulate the assessment or evaluation process may result in immediate disqualification. All team members must make a genuine contribution to the submitted project. General: Final results will be determined based on the published evaluation criteria and the evaluation panel's assessment. Participants are responsible for ensuring that their submissions comply with all applicable rules and requirements. The organizers reserve the right to modify the schedule, evaluation process, eligibility requirements, or competition structure when necessary. Decisions made by the evaluation panel regarding final results will be considered final. What We're Looking For: We're not necessarily looking for the team using the most complicated technology. We're looking for teams that can: Think clearly. Understand problems. Build practical solutions. Work effectively as a team. Learn and adapt quickly. Make thoughtful technical decisions. Present their work confidently. A simple solution executed exceptionally well can be stronger than a complex solution that fails to solve the actual problem. What You Can Gain: Real-World Problem-Solving: Work on a practical problem and experience the process of turning requirements into a working solution. Build a Showcase Project: Create a project that demonstrates your technical, creative, and problem-solving abilities. Team Collaboration: Experience working with teammates from different colleges, cities, and backgrounds. Practical Development Experience: Go through the complete product-building cycle within a defined deadline. Innovation & Creativity: Explore new ideas and experiment with technologies while solving a meaningful challenge. Recognition: Outstanding projects and participants may receive recognition according to the final competition structure. Certificates: Eligible participants may receive certificates based on the applicable participation and achievement criteria. The 7-Day Challenge: 7 Days. 1 Problem Statement. 1 Team. 1 Working Solution. You don't need to have everything figured out on Day 1. You need to be willing to: Build. Learn. Adapt. Collaborate. Finish. Don't just talk about what you can build. Build it. Register → Form Your Team → Take the Assessment → Get the Problem → Build for 7 Days → Submit → Get Evaluated → Get Recognized Contribution: Contributed by IIT Delhi This hackathon is conducted online through Unstop.

title: Global SDG & AI Hackathon 2026
organizer: Bharati Vidyapeeth College of Engineering Pune
description: Download Problem Statements from our website and get more details: https://www.sdg-hackathon.in/ Build AI that solves real problems. This hackathon is organized by the ACM Student Chapter at BV(DU) College of Engineering, Pune (Department of Computer Science & Engineering). Students are invited to build practical, responsible AI solutions for real-world problems connected to the UN's Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). How It Works Register your team and pick one main problem area (SDG track). Submit your idea online (a short slide deck). Reviewers screen all ideas remotely. Top teams are shortlisted and invited to Pune. Selected teams attend an online briefing, then come onsite for 2 days to build, test, and present their project. Final pitches, judging, and prize distribution happen on the last day. Important Dates Last date to register and submit idea: 20 Sep 2026, 11:59 PM Online screening: 21-22 Sep Results (finalists announced): 23 Sep (top 20 teams) Online oreintation for finalists: 25 Sep, 6 PM Onsite hackathon: 26-27 Sep, 11 AM-7 PM (both days) Final presentations and awards: 27 Sep, by 7 PM Note: This is NOT an overnight/48-hour hackathon. No overnight stay is needed or allowed. You go home each evening. Choose a Problem Area Pick one topic to focus on: Hunger, Health, Education, Gender Equality, Clean Water, Clean Energy, Jobs & Economy, Infrastructure, Reducing Inequality, Smart Cities, Responsible Consumption, Climate Change, Ocean Life, Land & Nature, or Justice & Good Governance. Each topic has specific real-world challenges listed on the website with challenge IDs - pick one and quote it in your submission. What to Submit First (Round 1) A short presentation (5-7 slides, PPT or PDF) that covers: The problem you're solving and who it affects Which SDG goal it connects to Your proposed solution and how it works How AI actually helps (not just AI for the sake of it) Your technical plan (data, models, tools, possible risks) Expected impact and your team's roles Onsite Finale Schedule Day 1 (26 Sep): Reporting and opening brief, build begins, lunch break, mentor check-in, progress review, day ends by 7 PM Day 2 (27 Sep): Build continues with mentor support, lunch break, final code submission, judges review projects, top teams present, prizes and closing ceremony Prizes - Total Rs. 15,000 (funded by ACM India) 1st Place: Rs. 8,000 2nd Place: Rs. 5,000 3rd Place: Rs. 2,000 Extra sponsor prizes may be added later How You'll Be Judged (out of 100 points) Real-world impact - 25 points How well it works (technical build) - 25 points Creativity - 15 points Safe and responsible use of AI - 15 points Practicality (can it actually be used?) - 10 points How well you explain and demo it - 10 points Rules to Keep It Fair If you reuse any code, data, AI models, or prompts, you must clearly mention it. Explain where your data comes from and how you're keeping AI use safe and responsible. Your final submission should include a working prototype, code repository, slide deck, and demo. Be respectful, follow campus rules, and respect others' intellectual property. You can use AI tools and open-source code, but must disclose them. Your team keeps ownership of your original work (though third-party tools/data follow their own rules). Who Can Join Any student currently enrolled in a recognized college or university Team size: 2 to 4 members All members must be 18+ on the day of registration (if someone is under 18, contact the organizers beforehand for guardian consent) Registration Fee Rs. 100, one-time, per team (not per person). What You Get at the Venue Wi-Fi, power, seating/workspace, food and refreshments, mentor support, jury feedback, and certificates for eligible finalists. What You Should Bring Laptop, charger, valid college ID, any datasets/API keys you plan to use, personal essentials, and a demo-ready prototype by Day 2. Other Things to Know Travel and accommodation are not provided or reimbursed by the organizers.

title: EIC VentureX: Idea To Impact Hackathon
description: EIC VentureX: Idea to Impact Stop scrolling, start building. Most people have ideas. Very few have the guts to build and pitch them in front of VCs, founders, and industry leaders. EIC VentureX: Idea to Impact is your shot. Organized by the Entrepreneurship & Incubation Cell (EIC), VentureX is a premier startup pitching competition open to students and working professionals across India. This isn't just a hackathon, it's a launchpad. A room full of the right people, the right energy, and the right opportunities to turn your idea into something real. What Makes VentureX Different? Forget participation trophies and hollow certificates. Venture Capitalists will be present at the Grand Finale, and your pitch could literally change your life. Top 3 winning teams get a curated, invite-only networking lunch with founders and co-founders, worth ₹5,000 per team. Top 2 teams get a dedicated opportunity to pitch directly in front of Venture Capitalists, an experience worth ₹10,000, absolutely free for you. Shortlisted finalists also get exclusive access to our E-Summit, where you network with the startup ecosystem, investors, entrepreneurs, mentors, and innovators all under one roof. This is the room you've been trying to get into, and VentureX opens the door. Who Should Apply? VentureX is for you if you have an idea that solves a real problem, want to experience what a real startup pitch feels like, are ready to be challenged by mentors, judges, and VCs, and want to build your network beyond your campus. Open to undergraduate students, postgraduate students, and working professionals across India. Cross-college teams are welcome, and so are cross-city teams. Competition Structure VentureX runs across three stages. Round 1A is a mandatory online Team Quiz lasting 20 minutes, covering entrepreneurship basics, problem-solving aptitude, and general startup thinking. Every team member must participate individually, and no retakes are allowed. Round 1B is the Online Pitching Round, spread over 2 days. Once registrations close, your team can pick a problem that already excites you or take on one of ours, and go from zero to pitch-ready. Teams must submit a 6 to 7 slide Solution Deck covering the problem, your solution, how it works, market opportunity, business model, and your team, with an optional slide for traction or roadmap. A ready-to-use template will be shared with all registered teams. Submissions are accepted as PDF or PPT only, with a max file size of 20 MB. A short 2-4 minute video pitch is optional but recommended, uploaded to YouTube (unlisted) or Google Drive. Round 2 is the Grand Finale, held in person (tentatively) at PEC, Chandigarh. Only the best teams from Round 1 make it here, and this round is not just another pitching round, it's an on-site hackathon where shortlisted teams take their ideas from concept to a functional product. Teams are expected to build a finished MVP that can be demonstrated during the final pitch, functional enough to show the core value proposition and key working aspects of the solution. You're free to use any tools you're comfortable with, including vibe coding, no-code or low-code tools, and AI-powered development tools. The focus isn't on how you write every line of code, it's on whether you can turn your idea into a functional product. Final deliverables include a finished MVP, a PPT pitch deck, a product demonstration, and any supporting material needed to communicate your solution effectively. Round 1: prove it. Round 2: build it. Final Pitch: defend it. VentureX: Idea to Impact.

title: Dogfood | 72-Hour Hackathon
description: About the Hackathon Dogfood 2026 is a 72-hour online hackathon built around one challenge: build the platform that will judge you. Hackathon Raptors has run 35+ hackathons across 85+ countries, and this challenge comes directly from the problems encountered while running them. Registration, team formation, submissions, eligibility, judge assignment, scoring, normalization, results, certificates, and archiving all form one complex data pipeline. Your challenge is to build a modern, open-source, self-hostable hackathon submission and judging platform that handles this entire lifecycle. Everyone builds the same product against the same published specification. There are no tracks. This is not a hackathon where you build a demo of a platform. We are asking you to build ours. The winning project will be forked, self-hosted, and put into production for Hackathon Raptors events. You keep ownership of your work, and the project remains open source. The platform must run locally with a single command. A working submission should start with docker compose up , seed itself with the provided fixture data, and work without a cloud account, hosted database, authentication provider, external API, or network connection. Stay Updated All announcements, specification releases, rule clarifications, fixture data, acceptance suite updates, submission instructions, FAQs, and live support happen through the official Hackathon Raptors Discord. Discord Server Invite: Join the Hackathon Raptors Discord Event Website: dogfoodhack.com Organizer: raptors.dev Why Participate Hackathon platforms have largely converged on the same basic features. The interesting engineering problems are what happens underneath them: fair judging, role isolation, score normalization, abuse prevention, reliable data flows, APIs, and software that an organizer can actually self-host and operate. Participants will get to: Build a complete hackathon platform from registration through results. Work on authentication, authorization, teams, submissions, galleries, dashboards, and exports. Design backend-enforced role isolation and permission systems. Build weighted and configurable judging rubrics. Solve cross-judge score normalization. Design fairer community voting and anti-abuse mechanisms. Work with assignment algorithms, ranking systems, and statistical methods. Build an API-first, self-hostable platform. Practice production-oriented DevOps and local deployment. Create software that may actually be used in future Hackathon Raptors events. Demonstrate engineering judgment, technical depth, and ability to ship under constraints. AI coding assistants are allowed and expected. The challenge is not whether AI helped. It is whether you can ship, test, explain, and defend what you built. Eligibility Dogfood is open to: Students. Software developers. Engineers. Researchers. Professionals. Open-source contributors. Full-stack developers. Backend and API engineers. Frontend and design-system builders. Data and algorithms enthusiasts. Security engineers. DevOps and self-hosting enthusiasts. Anyone interested in building serious software, from any country. Team Size 1-4 members. Solo participation is allowed. Teams of 2-4 are recommended. Cross-college teams are allowed. Cross-disciplinary teams are allowed. Event Format The hackathon runs entirely online for 72 hours. Every team builds the same product: an open-source, self-hostable hackathon submission and judging platform. During the event, teams are expected to: Design and implement the platform against the published specification. Build the required core functionality. Implement judging, scoring, normalization, and role isolation. Test the platform against edge cases and failure scenarios. Run the provided acceptance suite against their implementation. Document the architecture, data model, judging system, and technical decisions. Verify that the project can run locally without hosted-service dependencies. Prepare a working demonstration. Submit the required source code, documentation, acceptance report, and demo video. Tier Ladder There are four tiers. Everyone builds against the same specification, and teams are evaluated based on how far they climb and how correctly they implement each tier. T1 - Core: Authentication and sessions, participant/judge/organizer/admin roles, event creation, configurable dates, tracks and prizes, team formation through invite links, project submission with draft and edit functionality, deadline enforcement, and a searchable public gallery. T1 is the minimum requirement to be judged. T2 - Judging: Judge invitation and assignment, batch or algorithmic assignment, weighted and configurable judging rubrics, backend-enforced role isolation, judge progress dashboards, cross-judge score normalization, and CSV export throughout the workflow. T3 - Public: Configurable community voting, comments, hidden results during voting, randomized project ordering, rate limiting, duplicate detection, audit trails, or an alternative voting mechanism that can be technically defended. T4 - Stretch: REST API and webhooks covering UI actions, certificate and record generation, signed and publicly verifiable judge participation records, an embeddable gallery widget, and bulk import and export. A clean, correct T2 is better than a broken T4. Tier claims are verified through the acceptance suite, not through the README. What Counts as Done Your project must produce a working portal from a single command. docker compose up must start a seeded, working platform locally. The project must not depend on: Hosted databases. Authentication-as-a-service. External APIs. Cloud accounts. Proprietary services. Network connectivity. The acceptance suite will run against your build and produce a tier-by-tier pass report. The acceptance report must be included in your public repository. If the project cannot run on a laptop with the network turned off, it cannot be adopted. AI Tools AI coding assistants are allowed and expected, including Claude Code, Cursor, Aider, GitHub Copilot, local AI models, and others. AI usage itself is not scored. We evaluate whether the final implementation works, whether the architecture and data model are sound, and whether the team can explain and defend the software it built. What You Need to Submit Each team must submit: Public GitHub repository. OSI-approved open-source license. Working implementation. docker compose up setup that starts a seeded portal. acceptance-report.txt . README.md . ARCHITECTURE.md . DATA-MODEL.md . JUDGING.md . Tests. 5-minute demo video showing one complete event lifecycle. Your JUDGING.md should explain your judge assignment strategy, scoring methodology, normalization method, and the reasoning behind your approach. Your ARCHITECTURE.md should explain the system design and major technical decisions. Your DATA-MODEL.md should document the schema and import/export paths. Judging Criteria Projects will be evaluated on: Tier Completion & Correctness - 40%: How far up the tier ladder the project reaches, verified by the acceptance suite. Correctness matters more than feature count, and honest gap reporting is rewarded. Judging Integrity - 25%: How well the platform handles role isolation, judge assignment, score normalization, auditability, and voting abuse. The judging system must be technically defensible. Adoptability & Operability - 20%: Whether Hackathon Raptors could realistically run the software. One-command startup, seeded data, documentation, migration paths, clean licensing, and self-hosting all matter. Code Quality & Innovation - 15%: Code quality, maintainability, schema design, architecture, and the technical decisions that make the project stand out. Bonus Challenges Optional bonus challenges are available: Normalization Proof (+5): Implement cross-judge normalization and demonstrate its effect using the provided fixture data. Pairwise Mode (+5): Add pairwise project comparisons and recover rankings using a Bradley-Terry style estimator or another defensible method. Threat Model (+3): Publish a written threat model covering voting and submission abuse, including attacks such as Sybil voting, ballot stuffing, submission scraping, judge collusion, and deadline gaming. API First (+3): Expose every UI action through a documented API and publish an OpenAPI specification. Maximum bonus: +16 points. One challenge done properly beats four unfinished features. Prizes ₹250000 Total Prize Pool 1st Place - Grand Prize: ₹80000 2nd Place - Runner-Up: ₹50000 3rd Place: ₹35000 4th Place: ₹20000 5th Place: ₹15000 Best Judging Engine: ₹10000 Write Up Quest: 4 winners × ₹10000 = ₹40000 The 1st-place project will be forked, self-hosted, and put into production for Hackathon Raptors events. The winning team keeps ownership of its repository. Hackathon Raptors does not require an assignment, transfer, CLA, or exclusivity agreement. Rules Teams must contain 1-4 members. Solo participation is allowed. All project code must be written during the official 72-hour hackathon window. Planning, research, documentation reading, and AI prompt preparation are allowed before kickoff. No project code may be committed before kickoff. T1 must be completed for the project to be judged. The submitted GitHub repository must be public at submission time. The project must use an OSI-approved open-source license. The project must run locally without hosted-service dependencies. docker compose up must produce a working, seeded portal. The final project must be self-hostable and work without network connectivity. Existing projects cannot be submitted as-is. Renamed copies or rewrites of existing open-source hackathon platforms are not allowed. Tier claims must be honest and supported by the acceptance report. AI coding assistants are allowed. Frameworks, libraries, boilerplate generators, and development tools are allowed. The final software must be something the team can explain and defend. Any project that cannot be run and evaluated as required may not be considered for adoption. Important Dates August 24, 2026: Registration opens. September 4, 2026: Judging panel announced. September 21, 2026: Team formation. September 24, 2026: Full specification published. September 25, 2026 at 18:00 UTC: Hackathon begins. September 28, 2026 at 18:00 UTC: Code freeze and submission deadline. September 28 to October 8, 2026: Judging window. October 5, 2026 at 18:00 UTC: Write Up Quest closes. October 9, 2026: Winners announced. About Hackathon Raptors Hackathon Raptors is a Community Interest Company that runs online hackathons for working engineers and developers. 35+ hackathons run since 2023. Participants from 85+ countries. Roughly a dozen events run each year. 300+ projects have been submitted in our last hackathon. Events are designed around practical engineering challenges rather than purely conceptual ideas. Dogfood is built around one simple proposition: Build the platform that will judge you.

title: Myntra HackerRamp: WeForShe 2025
description: At Myntra, we have taken conscious efforts to build an inclusive workplace. Women constitute over 50% of our customer base, hence "gender inclusion" has been a significant part of our inclusion journey. WeForShe is our focused effort towards creating equitable growth for women. As a part of this initiative, we are back with another season of HackerRamp: WeForShe ! This is an opportunity for all women coders from engineering colleges across the country to create and innovate through technology. Are you ready for a journey that will give you an adrenaline rush by letting the "geek goddess" in you creatively solve for areas in fashion tech? Not just that, you will also have an opportunity to be mentored by some of the best tech minds in our engineering teams as you inch closer to the finale! Excited as we are? Hop on the bandwagon and begin this journey with us! Eligibility: HackerRamp: WeForShe 2025 is open to only female students across all engineering colleges in India who are pursuing: B.Tech/B.E. programs (full-time), and are currently in their 3rd or 4th year . Dual Degree engineering programs (full-time), and are currently in their 4th or 5th year . Competition Structure: This year, we've revamped the competition to challenge you at every step of your journey from code to concept to creation. Stage 1: Registration: This is the first step of your journey. To participate in the competition, you must register your team before the deadline. Make sure to provide all the required information accurately to ensure your team's entry is successfully submitted and you're ready for the next stages of the challenge. Stage 2: The Competition Kick-off - Webinar 1: Your journey begins here. Join us for an exclusive webinar designed to equip every participant with a comprehensive understanding of the competition. We'll walk you through the journey ahead, detailing the rules, expectations for each stage, and how to navigate your path to success. This is your essential guide to understanding the full scope of the challenge and making the most of this unique opportunity. Stage 3: The Tech Gauntlet - Online Assessment Round: The Online Assessment Round is designed to test your fundamental problem-solving abilities, data structures, and algorithmic skills. Top-performing teams will demonstrate their coding prowess and advance to the next stage, where the real-world challenges of fashion-tech await. Each individual of the team needs to take the coding assessment and qualify to proceed to the next stage. Stage 4: The Strategic Briefing - Webinar 2: Having proven your coding prowess, it's time to build your blueprint for success. This webinar will provide a deep dive into the competition themes, offering strategic guidance on how to ideate and architect a groundbreaking solution. Stage 5: Mentorship from Myntra Experts: Following Webinar 2, each team will be assigned a dedicated expert mentor who will guide you through the process of refining your concept, creating a working model of your proposed solution, and preparing for your submission. Stage 6 & 7: The Solution Blueprint - Ideation, Submission & Presentation: As you move ahead, your task is to select ONE THEME from the given list of themes and identify a business problem statement from the world of fashion technology. Your task is to architect an innovative and feasible solution, while your assigned mentors will help you refine your vision. You will be required to submit a comprehensive presentation that details: The chosen theme and the problem statement The proposed solution and its key features. The technology stack you plan to use. The high-level architecture and data flow. Submission Guidelines: Submit your ideas as a presentation in PPT/PPTX format. The deck should not exceed six slides. The presentation must be prepared using the template provided by Myntra. In addition to the points in the template, you must also include: A video (screen recording) of the Minimum Viable Product (MVP) of your proposed solution or app. The video should include all the functional flows of the App. Links to code repositories. You may use free services from GitHub or GitLab for this. PPT Naming Convention: InstituteName_TeamName.ppt/pptx After submission, each team will have the opportunity to present their work to our panel of judges in a virtual session. This is your chance to impress them with your creativity and strategic thinking. Please note that you must use the same PPT you submitted for your presentation, along with a live demo of the MVP/app. Stage 8: The Grand Finale - On-Campus Showcase: The final showdown! The top 6 teams will be invited to the Myntra campus in Bengaluru for the Grand Finale. Here, you will not just present your idea, but a fully functional working prototype of your solution to our esteemed jury of senior technology leaders. This is your ultimate opportunity to bring your vision to life, showcase your technical skills, and compete for the top spot. General Rules & Guidelines: Candidates must be above 18 (eighteen) years of age. Interested candidates must register in teams of 2-3 members . Participants in a particular team can be from different batches and specialisations. Cross-college teams are NOT eligible to participate. 1 (one) participant cannot be a member of more than 1 (one) team. Modification of teams post-registration is not allowed. Participants are required to fill out a registration form with their details and agree to the IP Terms. All decisions regarding eligibility, authenticity, and final judgment rest with Myntra. Any unfair practices or deviations from the above rules will result in the immediate disqualification of the entire team. Rewards and Prizes: We believe in rewarding innovation and hard work. Here's what's at stake: Winners: INR 3,00,000 total (INR 2,00,000 cash and Myntra vouchers worth INR 1,00,000) 1st Runners-Up: INR 1,00,000 total (INR 50,000 cash and Myntra vouchers worth INR 50,000) Remaining Finalist Teams: Myntra vouchers worth INR 15,000 per team Pre-Placement Interview (PPI) Opportunities: All teams that qualify for the Grand Finale (Top 6) will receive Pre-Placement Interview opportunities for an internship at Myntra, provided they are in their final year of study. Participation Certificates: All teams that submit their PPTs and present them same format in Stage 7 will receive a digital Participation Certificate. Ready to code the future of fashion? Register now and let your journey begin.

title: Changethon
description: Problem Statement : Bridging the Educational Divide Education is a fundamental right, yet millions of people worldwide, particularly those from marginalized communities, people with disabilities, and economically weaker sections, face significant barriers in accessing quality learning opportunities. These barriers include financial constraints, lack of infrastructure, digital divide, language barriers, accessibility challenges, and limited availability of inclusive learning resources. Your challenge in Changethon is to develop innovative, scalable, and sustainable solutions that address these obstacles and empower every individual with equitable educational opportunities. Potential Focus Areas: Digital Accessibility: Develop AI-driven tools, mobile apps, or assistive technologies (e.g., screen readers, voice-based learning, or AR/VR solutions) that make online education more inclusive for people with disabilities. Affordable Learning Solutions: Create low-cost or open-source educational platforms, low-data-consuming apps, or community-driven learning models to bridge the economic gap in education. Infrastructure & Connectivity: Propose solutions that bring education to remote areas, such as offline-first learning models, solar-powered digital classrooms, or mobile education hubs. Inclusive Content: Design multilingual, culturally relevant, and disability-friendly educational resources to ensure learning is accessible to all. Financial Aid & Support: Develop innovative financial models, scholarship platforms, or community-driven micro-funding systems to support students from economically weaker sections. Your solution should be technologically innovative, socially impactful, and practically implementable . The best projects will not only identify the root causes of educational inaccessibility but also propose real-world, scalable solutions that can be deployed effectively. Are you ready to create education for all ? Let's innovate for change! About: Hey changemakers! Are you ready to create a world of difference? title: Reverse Engineering
description: Tired of the same old classic coding contests? Bored of the same old format of getting the problem statement along with sample input/output and creating a solution program? Students of all universities and institutes are eligible to participate in this challenge. Guidelines : Participants must join the WhatsApp group for all updates and clear communication regarding the event: whatsapp group Teams will be given an encoder file that takes an input, let's say X (can be in any format, might be a string, an excel file, a video, an image, or audio) and processes that input to return an output Y (again, this can be in any format, might be a string, an excel file, a video, an image, or audio). Teams must craft a decoder program (in any language) that takes input Y (or similar file/input) and returns output X. It won't be this simple, The event shall have lots of twists and turns. There will be multiple Levels for the event. Each level will require the team to submit a decoder file. The team passes to the next level if the decoder file can pass all our custom test cases. The top 3 teams to pass the final level will be declared winners. Rules: A team can have either 1 or 2 member(s). Timeline: Total 3 hours. Any college student is eligible to participate. Cross College Teams are allowed. The decision of the organizing committee will be final Any misbehavior on the part of any team member will result in the team's immediate disqualification. Any damage to the college property will lead to immediate disqualification. Basic knowledge of C++ and Python is required. Participants are requested to bring their laptops along with them.

title: Quant Quest by AlgoBulls
description: Prepare for a Revolution in Trading: Introducing "Quant Quest" by AlgoBulls. Get ready to embark on an extraordinary journey into the realm of algorithmic trading with Quant Quest, the ultimate competition for crafting high-performing trading strategies! In partnership with the prestigious Finance and Analytics Club at IIT Kanpur for Non-Core Weekend, the annual flagship finance festival of IIT Kanpur in association with Teckriti, IIT Kanpur, AlgoBulls presents Quant Quest - a thrilling journey designed to challenge your trading skills, foster innovation, and connect you with a vibrant community of like-minded individuals. Let's delve into the essence of Quant Quest. Purpose and Objective: Quant Quest isn't just about winning prizes; it's about acquiring knowledge, forming connections, and embarking on an exciting trading adventure. Join us, and let's redefine the future of algorithmic trading together! Educate: We aim to provide participants with valuable insights into algorithmic trading, empowering them with knowledge that extends beyond the competition. Challenge: Quant Quest encourages participants to push their limits, testing their trading strategies in real market scenarios. Connect: We foster a sense of community, where traders can network, learn from experts, and grow together. Develop and test trading strategies using our cutting-edge Gen AI tool, and customizable templates, or create your strategies from scratch within a simulated market that mirrors real-world conditions. (No coding expertise is needed.) Scope of the Competition: Participants will leap into action by crafting their own 'Quantitative Strategies' using AlgoBulls' state-of-the-art algorithmic trading platform. Collaborate with your teammates to develop, fine-tune, and execute strategies to perfection. Utilizing data provided by AlgoBulls, you'll optimize your strategies to maximize returns and claim the trading crown. The competition can be structured as : Main Competition: The heart of Quant Quest, where participants develop and execute algorithmic trading strategies. Side Competitions: Additional challenges, like Bug Bounty Program Best AI Prompt Award Most Valuable Feedback Award etc. Learning and Community: Beyond competition, Quant Quest provides webinars, workshops, and a supportive community to facilitate learning and networking. These challenges offer participants diverse avenues to showcase their skills. Knowledge is Power : To empower you on this exciting journey, access AlgoBulls' comprehensive documentation site. Here, you can delve deeper into the platform's functionalities and unlock its secrets. Plus, prepare for a pre-event workshop featuring a product demo by the AlgoBulls team. They will guide you through the platform's intricacies and reveal the competition details. What You'll Gain: Explore the Magic of Algorithmic Trading: Discover the potential and advantages of algorithmic trading. Master the Lingo of the Trading World: Understand industry jargon and trading terminology. Craft Killer Trading Strategies: Learn to create powerful trading strategies using the best tools available. Competition Structure: The main competition is meant to last for about 9 days with a max extension of 3 days depending on the need. This is a coding round where participants need to create a strategy. The strategy can be created in any of the 3 ways: Using a ready template Using our Generative AI Coding a strategy from scratch Upon creating or choosing a strategy of their liking, participants need to backtest the strategy in specified market conditions over a given period of time to generate the highest Gross ROI in a single execution. Participants can analyze and tweak their strategy codes or configure the strategy parameters to increase their Gross ROI over the span of the competition. The team with the highest Gross ROI for a single execution will emerge as the winner of the competition. Important Links: Link to competition site: Link Recording of Pre-event Webinar 31st October (9PM) : Link Link to documentation site : Link Link to join "Algo Trading Ninjas" Slack Community: Link Link to pyalgotrading github repo : Link Link to free pool of strategies on github : Link Link for "Python Algorithmic Trading Cookbook": Link Link for "Python Build" Youtube tutorial playlist : Link Platform Demo: Strategy Creation using Python Build Ready templates Tweak strategy parameters on Python Build Rules and Regulations: Participants can join the competition solo or in a team of a maximum of 3 members. Participants shall use the dedicated AlgoBulls platform for the entire competition. During registration on the AlgoBulls platform, participants need to make sure to enter their name in the format <Name>-<TeamName>-<OrganisingInstituteName> . For example - If Aman Verma is from team Rising Raider and the hosting institute is IIT Kanpur, the name should be "AmanVerma-RisingRaider-IITKanpur". In case a participant fails to keep his/her name in this format, their executions will not be considered for the leaderboard. Upon registration, each participant will have our "Quant Quest Advanced Developer Plan" activated in their portal. Registered participants can use this plan to learn about the platform before the competition and then continue with the competition after the date of commencement. Participants can create their trading strategies using our Generative AI, or they can code their strategies from scratch. Alternatively, they can choose a strategy from our pool of ready templates. Craft strategies for Indian Markets in the Equity or F&O Segments; or US Markets in the Equity segment. Each participant will be given a virtual fund of Rs 100 crores for the Indian Market and $1 Billion for the US Market. The teams have to get creative using any candle, quantity, stock, or strategy parameters and maximize the returns for their virtual funds. Participants will backtest their strategies for the specified backtest period. The team with the highest Gross ROI in a single run shall be crowned the champion of the competition. In case of a tie, the team with the best "Average Hit Ratio" for that strategy shall be placed at the winning position. Hard coding of any parameter like date, quantity, etc is not permitted. This will lead to rejection of the strategy run. Continuous use of hard-coded strategies will lead to disqualification of the participant from the competition. A Community for Support and Learning To ensure smooth and efficient communication throughout the competition, we've established a dedicated private Slack channel. This channel is hosted within the "Algo Trading Ninjas" Slack community, designed for individuals passionate about enhancing their Algo trading knowledge. By joining this private channel, you'll be able to: Stay Informed : Get real-time updates, announcements, and important notifications related to the Quant Quest competition. Learn Continuously : Our "Algo Trading Ninjas" community is a knowledge hub for Algo trading enthusiasts. Even after the competition concludes, you can continue to learn, grow, and network with fellow traders and experts. Exclusive Access : Gain exclusive access to resources, discussions, and insights that can give you an edge in the competition and beyond. Joining the Algo Trading Ninjas Slack community will not only enhance your Quant Quest experience but also provide you with a lifelong learning platform. We encourage you to be an active part of this vibrant community as you embark on your algo trading journey.

title: Cyber-O-Day 2.0
description: Registration Link: https://vtopcc6.vit.ac.in/chennai-events/eventPreview/326 Cyber-O-Day 2.0 is a 24-Hour event organized by Linux Club scheduled for October 6th and 7th, 2023, dedicated to imparting crucial knowledge about today's most pressing societal concerns: Cybersecurity and Ethical Hacking. It's a structured and entirely hands-on workshop run by our own technical team. The topics that will be covered are: Linux Fundamentals: Linux Fundamentals are the building blocks of understanding the Linux operating system, which is pivotal in cybersecurity. Participants will delve into the core concepts, file structure, and command-line interface, gaining essential skills for server management and security analysis. Cryptography: Cryptography forms the bedrock of secure communication and data protection. This segment explores encryption, decryption, and cryptographic protocols that safeguard information integrity, confidentiality, and authentication in the digital realm. OSINT and Reconnaissance : Open-source Intelligence (OSINT) and Reconnaissance involve honing skills to gather critical information about potential targets. title: Aurora'23 The Cryptic Hunt
description: Date: 4 PM 27/05/23 - 6 PM 28/05/23 Location: BR Auditorium, Delhi Technological University Important Links: Rulebook: https://bit.ly/cryptic-hunt-rulebook Discord: https://discord.gg/9Q6mnwWdzM About the Event: Cryptic hunts are the online equivalent of treasure hunts and require you to hunt the internet for clues to solve given questions, which are supposed to be solved using a plethora of online tools - cipher decoders/encoders and other common methods of data relaying like barcodes, OR codes, etc. They generally revolve around tech, trivia, pop culture, and most anything you can find on the internet. Googling is allowed and heavily encouraged, but it won't directly get you the answer in most cases. Think logically, and make connections between different parts of levels. Make sure you check the source of the webpage for any hints hidden there. Cryptic hunts are all about connecting the dots and finding solutions. Keep getting your leads confirmed from the organizers. If you think you've gotten stuck somewhere, ask for personal/public hints. Lead confirmations are short yes or no confirmations that can be asked from event moderators, to confirm whether you're on the right path while solving the question. You can regularly ask the moderators for confirmation that you're progressing correctly and applying the right logic while solving the level. Format: Roundtable's Aurora presents the first-ever 24-hour Cryptic Hunt The first to complete all levels wins. Priority ranks will be given to those who finish the levels first. MODS would be active and all important information will be directed through Discord. For a better understanding refer to the Rulebook for Aurora'23 The Cryptic Hunt Guidelines: Any illegal move that includes asking fellow participants for hints/answers, SQL injection on the site, etc would lead to direct disqualification. The decision of the MODS would be final and discreet. Hints will be released publicly at regular intervals of time so no repeated personal requests for hints will be entertained. Ensure a good backup internet connection (Mobile Data) to avoid any hassle. FAQs: What is the eligibility criteria? Anyone and everyone is free to participate. Be it a school student/college student or a working professional, you are cordially invited for the event. There are no charges for the event. I am a total beginner. I don't know anything about hunts. Can I participate? Yes, you can definitely participate. It will be a fun and beginner-friendly event. You don't need any pre requisites for the same. Just bring your laptop/tablet/phones along with your extension cords. Will network connectivity be provided? DTU's WiFi will be of very limited bandwidth, we advise everyone to arrange or their own. The same would be advised for Extension Cords, we advise participants to carry their own extension cords as per their own requirements. Will food be provided to the participants? Food arrangements will be done by Roundtable for all the participants. Will the event be offline? Yes, the event will be held in an offline manner. All participants should reach the BR Auditorium, DTU 30 minutes prior to the event. Will you provide accomodation? No, the event will go on non stop for 24 hours and we are not responsible for providing any kind of accommodation for anybody.

We have come up with something new for you! Combine your coding skills with your logical thinking skills and come forward to compete in Reverse Engineering. Students of all universities and institutes are eligible to participate in this challenge. Guidelines : Participants must join the WhatsApp group for all updates and clear communication regarding the event: https://chat.whatsapp.com/K3FREkM7ywvAKBAiucNoGr Teams will be given an encoder file that takes an input, let's say X (can be in any format, might be a string, an excel file, a video, an image, or audio) and processes that input to return an output Y (again, this can be in any format, might be a string, an excel file, a video, an image, or audio). Teams must craft a decoder program (in any language) that takes input Y (or similar file/input) and returns output X. It won't be this simple, The event shall have lots of twists and turns. The event will not be based entirely on your coding skills. The event shall test your deductive skills and knowledge of different existing technical tools. The encoder program file can contain the following languages: C++, and Python. However, there is no restriction to any coding language for the decoder file. There will be multiple Levels for the event. Each level will require the team to submit a decoder file. The team passes to the next level if the decoder file can pass all our custom test cases. The top 3 teams to pass the final level will be declared winners. Rules: A team can have either 1 or 2 members (s) Timeline: total 3 hours Any college student is eligible to participate Cross College Teams are allowed The decision of the organizing committee will be final Any misbehavior on the part of any team member will result in the team's immediate disqualification Any damage to the college property will lead to immediate disqualification Basic knowledge of C++ and Python is required Participants are requested to bring their laptops along with them

title: APL Apollo Tubes - 1 Pixel Designathon
organizer: Indraprastha Institute of Information Technology (IIIT), Delhi
description: Guidelines: Entry Requirements: Each team must submit its research proposal and a one-page brief explaining the concepts. You can use visual design concepts for submitting your Design proposal. Options include (but are not limited to): Poster Prototype Presentation Short video or Animation (optional) Rules: Submission: Dec 27, 2022, @12:00 A.M.IST - Jan 9, 2022, @11:59 P.M.IST: Each team, will receive a design brief at the scheduled date and time: Dec 28, 2022 @12:00 A.M., The participants, need to submit their projects as ZIP files on the Unstop by Jan 9, 2022 . Judging Criteria: Social Impact Sustainability Research & Feedback Accessibility & Inclusivity Emotional Quotient Practicality Cost factor Judging Panel: The registered participants will go through an initial filter process, after which five teams will get selected for the final round. The filtering process will get conducted by a judges panel. A panel of a minimum of four will witness the selected teams' final pitch. The panel will comprise industry specialists and research faculties with subject matter knowledge. You will be given a chance to present your ideas and design process in front of these industry specialists. Tracks: Track 1: APL Apollo Green Construction One potential solution to the environmental impacts of deforestation and wood consumption in general goods production is to use more sustainable and environmentally-friendly manufacturing materials. One such material that has been suggested is steel pipes. However, it remains to be seen whether steel pipes can effectively serve as an alternative to wood in all cases and the potential trade-offs and challenges in implementing this change. Therefore, it is crucial to explore the feasibility of using steel pipes as a more sustainable manufacturing material to reduce deforestation and wood consumption. This may involve rethinking the current use of wood in various applications and identifying opportunities to shift to steel pipes or other allied materials that are greener and have a lower environmental impact. It will also be necessary to consider the potential trade-offs and challenges in implementing this change and determine the most effective and efficient approach. Can APL Apollo steel pipes be used as a more sustainable manufacturing material to reduce deforestation and wood consumption in general goods? Can we consider alternative materials, such as steel or other environmentally-friendly options, to decrease the environmental impact and reduce reliance on wood? Track 2: Reimagining Hemp as green substitute Despite the numerous benefits of hemp as a sustainable and versatile crop, the hemp industry faces several challenges that limit its growth and development. These challenges include outdated regulations, a lack of awareness and understanding about the potential of hemp, and a lack of investment and infrastructure to support the cultivation and processing of hemp. One of the main problems is that hemp is often lumped together with marijuana, even though it contains only trace amounts of THC (the psychoactive compound found in marijuana). This has led to hemp being heavily regulated and, in some cases, outright banned. Another issue is that hemp is not widely cultivated, meaning it is not widely available as a resource. This lack of availability makes it difficult for people to access the numerous benefits of hemp, including its use as a sustainable building material, biofuel, and food source. Furthermore, many farmers are unaware of the potential benefits of hemp or are hesitant to invest in a crop that is not widely cultivated. This lack of knowledge and investment limits the growth and development of the hemp industry and prevents farmers from taking advantage of the economic opportunities that hemp could provide. In addition, there is a lack of infrastructure and support for the processing and distribution of hemp products, which limits the ability of the industry to reach a broader market. This lack of infrastructure makes it difficult for farmers to access the resources and support needed to cultivate and process hemp effectively. Overall, there is a need to address these issues and support the development of a sustainable and thriving hemp industry. By doing so, we can increase the cultivation and availability of hemp, improve access to its numerous benefits, and help uplift farmers by providing them with new economic opportunities. Happy Ideating!

title: Google Code Jam
description: Pump up the Code Jam! Google's longest-running global coding competition, Code Jam, call on programmers around the world to solve challenging, algorithmic puzzles against the clock. Contestants advance through four online-hosted rounds to compete at the annual Code Jam World Finals that is held at a different international Google office each year. Each round brings new challenges, and in the end, 25 contestants will have the ultimate chance to put their skills to the test, vying for cash prizes and the coveted championship title at the World Finals. Register and compete in Code Jam's Online Qualification Round. It lasts 27 hours, but you won't need that long to earn the round's qualifying point minimum. Once you do, you'll advance to Online Round 1. We offer three sub-rounds for Round 1, and you can compete in as many as it takes for you to finish in the top 1,500 of any of these rounds. The top 1,500 from each sub-round move on to compete for a spot in the top 1,000 contestants of Code Jam Online Round 2. These top 1,000 contestants advance to Online Round 3 and earn a limited edition Code Jam t-shirt. The top 25 contestants from Code Jam Online Round 3 will compete in the Virtual World Finals for the championship title and a cash prize of $15,000 USD. Eligibility: The exact details are explained in the Terms, but here are some of the requirements that you have to meet at the time of registration: You are 16 years of age or older. Only those who are 18 years of age or older around the time of the final round (see theTerms for the exact date) are eligible to attend the onsite finals. You are not a current employee/intern of Google Inc. or an employee of any Google affiliate or subsidiary. If you have a job offer from Google, you must stop competing when you become an employee. Note that if you advance to the final round, and become a Google employee before the final round, you will not be eligible to travel to or compete in the final round. You are not an immediate family member (parent, child, sibling, or spouse) of, or living in the same household as, a Google employee or an employee of any Google affiliate or subsidiary. You are not a resident of Quebec, Crimea, North Korea, or anywhere that the contest is prohibited by law. You will be disqualified if you gained information on a problem as a participant in a Google-managed program or by working as an employee, intern, contractor, director, officer, or other official office-holder of Google, you will be disqualified from a contest if you submit a submission for that problem. Rewards and Prizes : Code Jam T-Shirt (You are eligible to receive one (1) t-shirt if you are one of the 1,000 highest-ranked contestants from Code Jam Round 2) Code Jam Cash Prizes (You are eligible to receive one of the following cash prizes if you advance to and make at least one submission in the Final Round of Code Jam): Competitor Rank Prize Money 1st Place $15,000 USD 2nd Place $2,000 USD 3rd Place $1,000 USD 4th-25th Place $100 USD
prize: Winner: ₹15000 | First Runner Up: ₹2000 | Second Runner Up: ₹1000 | For Positions 4th to 25th: ₹100

title: HackOverflow
description: HackOverflow is a software development hackathon aimed at college students. Get building, learning, and creating technology projects from scratch. Websites and mobile apps are common types of hacks, but you can build anything! Think outside the box : ) It's true that being a specialist in one's field and gaining mastery of a particular aspect of technology has distinct advantages, but as technology rapidly expands and evolves, industries are constantly changing. With this change comes the need for skills branching out to multiple technologies and the ability to build end-to-end products to potentially transform the way people live around the world! With prizes worth 20,000 up for grab and perpetual fame on the line, choose a track, get those creative juices flowing and start building! Tracks: Education: The Education track aims to empower students and teachers by exploring the ways that Education Technology (EdTech) can augment learning. As schools navigate the return to in-person teaching, it is especially important that we adapt remote teaching tools and support students in making up for a lost time in their education. Projects in this track will encourage a love of learning, recognize a variety of learning styles, and aim to make education more accessible. Infotainment: The Infotainment track promotes the use of technology as a means of expression, encouraging hackers to explore the ways that we create, consume, and share content. Projects in this track will make the most of hackers' interdisciplinary skills, perhaps by incorporating music, graphics, and other creative mediums, as well as keeping the user at the forefront of design. Sustainability: The Sustainability track encourages hackers to use technology to pursue a more sustainable future on environmental, economic, and social levels. As sustainability encompasses all aspects of human life, projects in this track will address a diverse range of topics like food, finance, energy, transportation, water, awareness & accountability, and fashion. Rules and Guidelines: Teams can select only one track need and need to develop their hack in the given timeframe Inter-college team member participation and solo member participation are allowed Plagiarised submissions/ submissions utilizing predefined templates would be disqualified Prizes: Perks worth up to Rs.10,000 for the top 3 submissions along with a shoutout on our handles Prices for the most minimalistic hack, most creative hack and so on
prize: Winner: INR10000 | First Runner Up: INR6000 | Second Runner Up: INR4000

title: Code with Globalshala 3.0
description: If you are someone who is passionate about designing robust solutions that help organizations stay relevant in our evolving digital world- this challenge is for you! The Code with GlobalShala Hackathon hopes to recognize those students who are willing to take risks in their innovations, helping us to create technical solutions to fulfill real world workplace demands. This challenge will provide its participants the opportunity to delve into the minds of an entrepreneur in order to create technologies enabling better efficiency and productivity at a workplace. Apart from conventional cash prizes, the winner(s) of this Hackathon will have the chance to win scholarships upto $12,000 to pursue their post-graduation degree in one of the US' Top 100 colleges- Saint Louis University for courses such as Artificial Intelligence, Computer Science and Cybersecurity. Moreover, they will also have the opportunity to secure an internship at GlobalShala, empowering them with real world skills to prepare them for their careers ahead. We invite you to help create a technological revolution in business management! Eligibility: High School Students Undergraduate Students Timeline: Idea Submission Round: Hurry! Idea submission round ends on 13th July 2022 Presentation Round: Shortlisted teams to start building the prototypes. Prototypes will be presented online in front of the Globalshala jury at the end of this round! Themes: Employee Engagement Platform: Employee success is critical to business success. However, one of the biggest challenges of growing businesses is maintaining employee engagement. A good employee engagement program should help in collecting employee feedback, recognize performance, tracking and setting goals and connecting engagement data to employee performance. We are looking to create a which will improve the workplace experience by boosting employee morale, productivity, and company alignment. Example: Humu ; Kazoo HR Workflow Automation System: The main goal of the HR team in companies is to drive employee success, however, it also involves some repetitive and mundane responsibilities such as creating different kinds of letters, onboarding, off boarding forms etc. We are looking for a platform to enhance the efficiency of the HR department by freeing employees from tedious manual tasks, and allowing them to focus on complex tasks like decision making and strategizing. By automating standard and repetitive HR activities, organizations can reduce the cost and time they spend on manual HR planning and processing. This includes automation of the creation of different types of letters, certificates, badges etc, which can be completed in a few clicks. Example: KissFlow Team Progress Tracker: Our teams and our people are learning and evolving everyday! Each new milestone in their journey is an important one, be it the first time they lead a team meeting, or finish their first project report- however, most times, we lose track of their achievements and progress, and more importantly don't reward their skill improvements. We are looking for a platform to ​​assess, track and report on the skill and interest levels of all people, which will help not only the company but also the employee to map out their own journey. Example: SkillBase ; Regroove To succeed in the Hackathon, it will help if you are able to: Capture and present your idea in an informative and succinct manner which answers any key theme above Create a basic functional prototype which is able to display the key features of your platform Present your prototype during a live demonstration to the judges Your solution/idea will be evaluated based on the following parameters: Concept Understanding the problem being addressed Background research on existing techniques Creativity Novelty and innovativeness of the idea Maturity of technology used Impact Practical usability potential Viability on a global scale Implementation Feasibility and scalability Complexity and constraints

title: Data Challenge II
description: Data Challenge is the integral event of WiDS. WiDS Delhi is an independent event that is organized by Delhi Ambassadors of WiDS as part of the annual WiDS Worldwide conference organized by Stanford University and an estimated 150+ locations worldwide, which features outstanding women doing outstanding work in the field of data science. All genders are invited to attend all WiDS Worldwide conference events. Udbhav & Henry Harvin Education are the community partners for WiDS. The Global Women in Data Science (WiDS) Conference aims to inspire and educate data scientists worldwide, regardless of gender, and support women in the field. This annual two-day technical conference provides an opportunity to hear about the latest data science-related research and applications in a broad set of domains. The goal of this event is to bring women leaders in data science together from across the globe.

title: CRSU Hackathon 2026
description: Overview: Research it. Build it. Prove it. A two-stage innovation challenge that starts with research and ideation and ends with an intensive online build and presentation phase . Open to everyone. Teams of 1 to 3. CRSU Hackathon 2026 is for people who want to do more than pitch an idea. The programme follows a simple progression: Understand the problem → Propose a Research → Build it → Prove it The hackathon begins with research and ideation. Teams will work on a single problem statement, understand the user or context, develop a solution and plan how they would build it. The strongest teams will then advance to the final build phase, where the focus shifts to execution, testing, iteration and presenting a working prototype . The entire programme is fully online , allowing participants from anywhere to take part without needing to travel to CRSU. Teams can bring together different strengths across coding, design, product, research, data and presentation . At a Glance: Eligibility: Everyone can apply Team Size: 1 to 3 members Mode: Fully online Final Build Stage: 30 teams Data: Synthetic data throughout Winning Team: Internship opportunity with Romeo & Juliet How It Works: The hackathon takes place across two competitive stages. Stage: Research & Ideation: 5th to 11th October 2026 Teams will study the problem, understand the user or context, identify the core challenge and develop a credible solution. The focus is on research, reasoning and solution design before implementation. Teams will work on areas such as: Understanding the problem Identifying users and context Developing hypotheses Designing a proposed solution Planning implementation Thinking through feasibility and limitations Stage: Final Build & Presentation: 12th to 18th October 2026 The strongest teams from Round 1 will advance to the final build phase. 30 teams will be selected to continue. Teams will turn their ideas into working prototypes and focus on: Building Testing Iterating Validating Demonstrating Presenting The final phase will be conducted entirely online . Who Can Participate?: Everyone can apply. You do not need to belong to a specific college, degree programme or academic discipline. Eligibility: Open to everyone Academic Background: No specific college, degree or discipline required Team Size: 1 to 3 members Format: Fully online Teams are encouraged to combine complementary skills across: Coding · Design · Product · Research · Data · Presentation What You Will Do: Research & Ideation: Understand the problem, research the context and develop a solution and make research paper. Shortlisting: 30 teams selected for the final build. Final Build: Build, test and iterate on your solution. Presentation: Demonstrate and explain your working prototype. The aim is to move beyond an idea and demonstrate what you can actually build and prove . Data & Ownership: The competition uses synthetic data throughout . Participants will not be asked to provide dating, relationship or compatibility information. No real Romeo & Juliet member data will be used. Participants retain ownership of the code, models, reports and other work they submit. Participation does not transfer ownership of a submission to Romeo & Juliet. Romeo & Juliet retains ownership of its own platform, technology, materials and work developed by or for the company before, during or after the programme.
