title: Byteathon
organizer: Noorul Islam Center for Higher Education
description: BYTEATHON 2026 is a 24-hour innovation and technology hackathon organised by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Noorul Islam Centre for Higher Education (NICHE), Kanniyakumari. BYTEATHON brings together innovators, developers, programmers, designers, engineers, creators, and problem-solvers to transform real-world challenges into practical, innovative, and scalable solutions. Participants will work in teams to analyse problem statements, design solutions, select suitable technologies, develop prototypes, and demonstrate their implementation before an expert judging panel. The hackathon focuses on: Innovation and originality Technical implementation Problem-solving ability Functional prototype development Feasibility and scalability User experience Real-world applicability and impact Presentation and technical understanding With a ₹70,000 cash prize pool, an online preliminary round, and a 24-hour offline Grand Finale at NICHE, Kanniyakumari, BYTEATHON is designed to give participants an opportunity to build, experiment, collaborate, and demonstrate what they can create under real hackathon conditions. BYTEATHON 2026 at a Glance Event: BYTEATHON 2026 Organiser: Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Noorul Islam Centre for Higher Education (NICHE) Finale Venue: Noorul Islam Centre for Higher Education, Kanniyakumari, Tamil Nadu Format: Online Preliminary Round + Offline Grand Finale Grand Finale Duration: 24 Hours Team Size: 1-4 Members Eligibility: Open for everyone Inter-college Teams: Allowed Inter-specialisation / Inter-department Teams: Allowed Prize Pool: ₹70,000 Round 1 Submission Deadline: 2 October 2026 Grand Finale: 15 October 2026 Finalists: 30 Teams Round 1 Registration/Submission Fee: ₹400 per team Competition Format BYTEATHON 2026 will be conducted in two stages. Round 1 - Online Preliminary Round Round 1 is an online idea and solution submission round. Teams can choose from five curated problem statements or participate under the Open Innovation category. Participants are expected to identify the problem clearly, propose an innovative solution, explain its technical implementation, and demonstrate the feasibility and potential real-world impact of their idea. Round 1 Submission Requirements Teams must submit: 1. Presentation - 10 to 12 Slides The presentation should cover: Team details Selected Problem Statement / Problem Statement Code Problem understanding Proposed solution How the solution works Technology stack System architecture or workflow Innovation and uniqueness Feasibility Usability Real-world use cases Scalability and potential impact Key differentiators 2. Demo / Explanation Video - 3 to 5 Minutes The video should clearly explain: Selected problem statement Proposed solution Core idea and workflow Technical approach Technology stack Code or implementation overview, where applicable Feasibility Innovation Use cases What differentiates the solution from existing approaches 3. Prototype - Optional for Round 1 A prototype, mock-up, proof of concept, repository, or demonstrable implementation may be submitted where applicable. While a complete prototype is not mandatory for Round 1, teams capable of demonstrating technical progress are encouraged to do so. Round 1 Deadline : 2 October 2026 All submissions must be completed before the announced deadline. Submissions will undergo a multi-stage evaluation process, after which 30 teams will be shortlisted for the BYTEATHON Grand Finale. Round 2 - 24-Hour Offline Grand Finale The shortlisted teams will be invited to participate in the 24-hour offline BYTEATHON Grand Finale at Noorul Islam Centre for Higher Education (NICHE), Kanniyakumari. Grand Finale Date: 15 October 2026 To maintain fairness among all finalists, teams will receive the applicable final-round problem statements/challenges as instructed by the organisers for the Grand Finale. During the 24-hour hackathon, teams will: Analyse the challenge Brainstorm and design their solution Develop the system architecture Build and integrate components Test their implementation Develop a functional prototype Prepare their final presentation Demonstrate the solution before the judging panel At the end of the hackathon, every team must present a working prototype or demonstrable implementation and explain its architecture, technology stack, design decisions, functionality, feasibility, limitations, and potential real-world impact. Judges may question teams regarding any part of their implementation to verify their understanding and contribution. Problem Statements BYTEATHON Round 1 consists of: 5 Curated Problem Statements 1 Open Innovation Track Teams may select one of the provided challenges or participate through Open Innovation where applicable. The challenges are designed around real-world problem-solving, technology, innovation, software development, engineering, AI, cybersecurity, automation, digital solutions, and practical applications of emerging technologies, depending on the individual problem statement. Participants are encouraged to develop solutions that are: Technically sound Innovative Practical User-focused Feasible Scalable Impactful Detailed problem statements, requirements, templates, and submission instructions will be available through the official BYTEATHON communication channels and platforms. Who Can Participate? BYTEATHON is open for everyone who wants to build, innovate, and solve problems. Participants with backgrounds or interests in areas such as the following are welcome: Computer Science Information Technology Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning Data Science Cybersecurity Electronics Robotics Engineering UI/UX Design Web Development Mobile App Development Cloud Computing IoT Automation Product Development Entrepreneurship Design Innovation Participants do not need to restrict their teams to a single discipline. Team Rules Each team can consist of 1 to 4 members. Solo participation is allowed. Inter-college teams are allowed. Inter-specialisation and inter-department teams are allowed. Participants from different academic years may form a team. Cross-disciplinary teams are encouraged. A participant may be registered with only one team. Each team must nominate one member as the Team Leader. Participant details submitted during registration must be accurate. Identification may be requested by the organisers wherever required for verification. Evaluation Criteria Projects may be evaluated based on: 1. Problem Understanding How clearly the team understands the selected challenge and its underlying requirements. 2. Innovation and Originality The uniqueness, creativity, and novelty of the proposed approach. 3. Technical Implementation Quality of architecture, engineering, programming, integration, algorithms, technologies, and implementation decisions. 4. Prototype Functionality How effectively the prototype demonstrates the proposed solution. 5. Feasibility Whether the solution can realistically be implemented, deployed, maintained, or expanded. 6. Real-World Applicability The relevance of the solution to practical problems and real users. 7. Impact Potential social, technological, commercial, environmental, institutional, or user impact, depending on the problem. 8. Scalability Ability of the solution to grow beyond the prototype stage. 9. User Experience Usability, accessibility, interface design, and overall experience where applicable. 10. Presentation and Demonstration Clarity and effectiveness of the team's final presentation and live demonstration. 11. Technical Understanding The team's ability to explain, justify, debug, modify, and defend its own implementation during interaction with the judging panel. Use of AI and Development Tools AI-assisted development tools are permitted in BYTEATHON unless explicitly restricted for a particular problem statement. Participants may use: AI coding assistants Generative AI tools Open-source libraries Frameworks APIs SDKs Development environments Public datasets Cloud platforms Design tools Automation tools Publicly available technical resources However, participants must understand the solution they submit. A team must be able to explain and justify: Code Architecture Algorithms APIs AI-generated components Models Data flow Design decisions Security considerations Technical implementation Judges may request participants to explain, modify, reproduce, debug, or demonstrate portions of their solution to verify their understanding and contribution. Using AI as a development tool is permitted. Submitting work that the team cannot explain or falsely representing externally developed work as its own is not permitted. Open-Source and Pre-Built Components Pre-existing open-source libraries, APIs, frameworks, SDKs, development tools, datasets, models, templates, and publicly available resources may be used. However: Their use must be disclosed wherever applicable. Previously developed components used by the team must be declared. Teams must clearly distinguish between existing components and work developed specifically for BYTEATHON. External resources must not be misrepresented as original work created by the team. The focus of evaluation will be on how effectively the team designs, integrates, implements, and understands its complete solution. Plagiarism and Originality The solution submitted must represent the genuine work and contribution of the registered team. The following may result in disqualification: Copying another team's solution Submitting another person's project Submitting an existing project without disclosure Plagiarism Misrepresenting third-party work as original Falsifying implementation or results Using prohibited resources where restrictions have specifically been announced The organising committee and judges may conduct technical verification wherever necessary. General Rules Participants must complete registration before the specified deadline. Participants may compete only as part of their registered team. Team members should not be changed after the registration deadline without prior approval from the organisers. A participant cannot represent more than one team. Teams must work on only one selected problem statement or Open Innovation submission unless otherwise instructed. All required submissions must be provided within the specified deadlines. Late or incomplete submissions may not be evaluated. Participants must follow the prescribed submission format. Teams are responsible for ensuring that submitted presentation links, video links, repositories, documents, prototypes, and other materials are accessible to the evaluation panel. Offensive, unlawful, deliberately harmful, unsafe, or unethical projects may be rejected or disqualified. Participants must maintain professional conduct throughout BYTEATHON. Harassment, deliberate damage to property, misconduct, or violation of institutional rules may lead to disqualification. Final-round participants are responsible for bringing their own laptops, chargers, development environments, adapters, and specialised personal equipment unless specifically stated otherwise. Internet access, mentoring facilities, or other resources offered by the organisers will be subject to availability. Participants are responsible for maintaining appropriate backups of their work. Teams must comply with venue and institutional regulations during the offline Grand Finale. Judges may evaluate both the final product and the team's understanding of how it was built. The decision of the judging panel and organising committee will be final. The organising committee reserves the right to modify the event schedule, rules, problem statements, judging process, or competition format where reasonably necessary. Important changes will be communicated through official BYTEATHON channels. Prize Pool - ₹70,000 BYTEATHON 2026 features a total cash prize pool of ₹70,000. Winner - ₹40,000 1st Runner-Up - ₹20,000 2nd Runner-Up - ₹10,000 Winners will be selected by the official judging panel according to the announced evaluation criteria. Certificates and other recognition or opportunities associated with BYTEATHON will be communicated through official event channels. Finalists and Grand Finale A total of 30 teams will be shortlisted from the preliminary round for the offline Grand Finale. title: The Sequential Matching Problem
description: The Sequential Matching Problem: Romeo & Juliet × IIT Madras An Applied Machine Learning Programme & Hackathon How should a system decide who should be introduced to whom when it does not know everything about the people involved, feedback arrives over time, and each decision changes the options and information available later? The Sequential Matching Problem explores this question through an applied machine learning programme focused on matching, recommendation systems, optimisation and sequential decision-making . The programme is designed to go beyond a conventional hackathon. Participants will first explore the challenge through workshops and research before moving into implementation, experimentation and mentorship. The Challenge: The challenge explores how intelligent systems can make matching decisions when information is incomplete, feedback changes over time, and each decision can affect what happens next. Participants will explore questions such as: How should a system make decisions with incomplete information? How should it respond when feedback arrives over time? How should uncertainty be handled? What information is worth acquiring? How should different possible outcomes be compared? How can a system make decisions that remain effective as conditions change? The programme brings together ideas from machine learning, recommendation systems, optimisation and sequential decision-making . Participants will work with a controlled environment using synthetic data, allowing them to experiment with these ideas without using real-world personal data. How The Programme Works: The programme is structured across three stages. 1. Workshops & Research: 5 to 11 October 2026 The first stage focuses on learning, research and technical reasoning. Participants will attend technical sessions, explore the challenge and work with their teams to develop their approach. Teams will investigate: Problem interpretation Technical assumptions Modelling approaches Decision strategies Uncertainty Experimental design Potential limitations and failure cases Teams will then submit their research and proposed approach before moving into the build phase. 2. Build & Mentorship: 12 to 18 October 2026 Selected teams will move into the implementation phase. Teams will gain access to the development environment and turn their ideas into working systems. During this phase, teams will: Implement their approach against the simulator Compare their approach with supplied baselines Run experiments and ablations Investigate performance under different conditions Study the effects of incomplete, noisy or delayed information Take part in technical mentorship and office hours Prepare a reproducible final submission 3. Final Evaluation: Following the build phase, selected teams will enter the final evaluation process. Systems will be evaluated in controlled environments, including private environments that are not identical to the public development environment. This is designed to assess how well an approach generalises beyond the development setting. Finalists will also present their work and answer technical questions about their approach, experiments and findings. The Development Environment: The competition will use a Python-based sequential simulator with documentation and baseline examples. The simulator provides a controlled environment where teams can make decisions, observe outcomes and study how their systems behave over time. The underlying outcome-generating process will remain hidden from participants. Data & Privacy: The competition uses synthetic data throughout . Participants will not be asked to provide dating, relationship or compatibility information. No real Romeo & Juliet member data will be used. Participants retain ownership of the code, models, reports and other work they submit. Participation does not transfer ownership of a submission to Romeo & Juliet. Romeo & Juliet retains ownership of its own platform, technology, materials and work developed by or for the company before, during or after the programme. Participation, or a similarity between a submission and Romeo & Juliet's work, does not give a participant ownership of Romeo & Juliet's independently developed work. If Romeo & Juliet wishes to use a participant's submitted work in its product, the parties will discuss that separately and agree the terms in writing. Who Can Participate?: The programme is open to students from IITs across India . Eligibility: Any year of study Any academic discipline or degree programme Teams of 1 to 4 students You do not need to be enrolled in a formal machine learning course. Participants should be comfortable with at least one quantitative or technical area such as coding, mathematics or data analysis . Recommended Preparation: The following are recommended, but not mandatory: Python Basic probability and statistics Introductory machine learning Students from computer science, data science, mathematics, physics, engineering, economics and related disciplines are encouraged to participate. Programme Timeline: Phase Dates Registration & Team Formation 25 Sep to 2 Oct 2026 PS Release 5 Oct 2026 Workshops & Research 5 to 11 Oct 2026 Build & Mentorship 12 to 18 Oct 2026 Final Evaluation After 18 Oct 2026 Final Presentations & Judging Date to be announced Format: Fully remote Team Size: 1 to 4 students Data: Synthetic throughout What You Will Submit: Round 1: Research & Approach Teams will develop and submit their proposed approach, covering areas such as: Problem interpretation Key hypotheses Proposed modelling approach Decision or allocation strategy Treatment of uncertainty Learning strategy Planned experiments Relevant baselines Expected failure modes Build Stage: Selected teams will submit: Working implementation Source code or repository Reproducible environment Experimental and ablation results Comparison against supplied baselines Short technical report Final Submission: Finalists will be expected to provide: Final reproducible system Technical report and experimental analysis Private evaluation execution Presentation or demonstration Technical Q&A GitHub repository URL Workshops & Technical Learning: The programme will explore topics across applied machine learning and technical decision-making. Reciprocal Matching & Recommendation Systems: Two-sided recommendation, directional outcomes and the difference between ranking pairs and allocating across a pool. Learning From Noisy & Incomplete Data: Missing information, uncertainty, sparse observations and cold-start scenarios. Optimisation Under Constraints: Global matching, constrained optimisation and computational trade-offs. Exploration, Exploitation & Online Learning: Selective feedback, information value and sequential learning. Building Robust ML Systems From Messy Data: Experimental design, validation, reproducibility and failure analysis. From Technical Model To Real Product: Connecting technical performance with practical constraints and user value. How Will Teams Be Evaluated? Evaluation will consider the quality and performance of the systems developed throughout the programme. Areas may include: Technical performance Matching and allocation quality Handling of uncertainty and incomplete information Robustness Experimental quality Research reasoning Reproducibility Detailed evaluation criteria will be provided as part of the competition documentation. Beyond The Hackathon: The programme also provides an opportunity to connect with the technical team at Romeo & Juliet . Selected participants may be considered for paid internship opportunities with Romeo & Juliet. Internship consideration may take into account technical work, independent problem-solving, experimentation, scientific and engineering judgement, ability to explain technical trade-offs and subsequent technical discussions or interviews. Exact internship terms will be communicated separately once finalised. Registration: There Are Two Steps To Complete Your Registration Step 1: Register On Unstop Create or join your team on Unstop. After forming or joining your team on Unstop, proceed to the official event website and complete the registration process. You will provide the required participant and team information and complete a short interaction with Juliet , Romeo & Juliet's AI onboarding agent. The interaction takes approximately five minutes and consists of six questions. There are no right or wrong answers.

The event is intended for participants who want a technical and challenge-driven quantum experience, with clear instructions on permitted knowledge, tools and resources. Each challenge will have clearly defined instructions, point values and submission requirements. Teams must submit the correct flag through the designated submission mechanism to receive points. Challenges may involve Python, Qiskit, quantum circuits, probability, quantum information, cryptography, logic, debugging and data interpretation . Teams may divide challenges among members according to their individual strengths. Team members may communicate and collaborate with each other during the competition. Teams must respect the announced time limit and submission deadline. Scores will primarily be determined by the number and point value of successfully verified flags. The organizers' decision regarding challenge verification, scoring and final results will be final.

description: Description Circuit Optimization Challenge is a hands-on quantum computing competition focused on improving the efficiency of quantum circuits. Participants will receive one or more quantum circuits and will be asked to optimize them while preserving the required computational behaviour or output. The challenge may involve reducing unnecessary gates, lowering circuit depth, improving gate usage, simplifying equivalent operations, and considering practical hardware constraints. Participants are expected to work with concepts such as quantum gates, circuit depth, qubit operations and Qiskit-based circuit construction. The event tests whether participants can move beyond simply writing a circuit and instead reason about how a circuit can be made more efficient and execution-friendly. A short qualifier or sample optimization task can be used to verify readiness before the main challenge. Evaluation can consider correctness, degree of optimization, resource usage, technical reasoning and compliance with stated constraints. The challenge is suitable for participants who have basic exposure to quantum circuits and Python/Qiskit and want to apply those concepts in a practical setting. Duration Total Duration: 90-120 minutes Rules & Guidelines Participants must compete individually. Participants will be provided with one or more quantum circuits for optimization. The optimized circuit must preserve the required computational behaviour or specified output. Participants may reduce unnecessary gates, circuit depth, qubit operations, or other specified resource usage. Python and Qiskit may be used for circuit construction, analysis, simulation, and optimization. Participants must follow any gate, qubit, depth, or hardware constraints specified by the organizers. Solutions should be submitted within the allotted time. Participants may be required to provide the optimized circuit along with a brief explanation of the changes made. Evaluation may consider correctness, circuit optimization, resource usage, technical reasoning, and compliance with constraints . Plagiarism, copying another participant's solution, or using unauthorized external assistance is not permitted. The organizer's decision regarding evaluation and final results will be considered final. Modern Technology Requirement: PROMPT RUN is specifically focused on modern web development . Participants are required to use a modern framework, library, or technology stack to build their project. Examples of acceptable technologies include: React Next.js Vue Nuxt Svelte SvelteKit Angular Astro Remix TypeScript-based modern frameworks Modern UI/component libraries Modern CSS frameworks and styling systems Frontend animation and interaction libraries Modern backend and API technologies where required Participants are free to choose the technology stack that best suits their solution. Standalone Technologies Are Not Permitted as the Primary Stack: Raw HTML-only projects Raw CSS-only projects Vanilla JavaScript-only projects Static HTML/CSS/JavaScript websites without a modern framework or technology stack HTML, CSS, and JavaScript may naturally be generated or used internally by modern frameworks, but the project itself must be built using a modern web development stack . Three Submission Chances: Every participant gets 3 submission chances during the hackathon. These three chances allow participants to improve and refine their project during the event. Participants can: Build → Submit → Evaluate → Improve → Resubmit However, there is an important rule: The Latest Submission Is Always Considered: The final score will be calculated from the latest valid submission made by the participant. The highest score among the three submissions will not be automatically retained. Example: Submission 1 - 72 points Submission 2 - 86 points Submission 3 - 79 points The final considered score will be: 79 points because Submission 3 is the latest valid submission. Participants should therefore use their three chances strategically and ensure that their final submission represents their strongest version. FAIE - Automated Evaluation Engine: PROMPT RUN uses FAIE - Frontend Arena Intelligent Evaluation Engine to automatically evaluate submitted projects. FAIE is an automated evaluation engine based on predefined evaluation criteria and technical checks . It is not an AI judge. The same evaluation process is applied to participant submissions according to the defined hackathon evaluation framework. FAIE evaluates multiple aspects of the submitted project, which may include: UI/UX Quality Functionality Performance Code Quality Responsiveness Accessibility Problem Statement Alignment Overall Technical Implementation After evaluation, FAIE generates a score for the submitted project. Live Leaderboard: PROMPT RUN features an official leaderboard where participants can track their current ranking. After a submission is evaluated: Submission → FAIE Evaluation → Score → Leaderboard If a participant submits again, their previous submission is replaced by the latest valid submission for leaderboard purposes. Therefore, the leaderboard always reflects the participant's latest valid evaluated score . The leaderboard will be used to determine the final results of the hackathon. Final Positions: Rank #1 - WINNER Rank #2 - RUNNER-UP Rank #3 - SECOND RUNNER-UP The final winners will be determined according to the official final leaderboard ranking . How PROMPT RUN Works: 01 - Start: Receive the hackathon challenge and understand the problem statement. 02 - Prompt: Use your preferred Vibe Coding workflow and development tools to plan and build your solution. 03 - Build: Develop a modern web application using an eligible technology stack. 04 - Submit: Submit your working project for automated evaluation. 05 - Evaluate: FAIE automatically evaluates your submission and generates your score. 06 - Improve: Use your remaining submission chances to refine your project. 07 - Climb: Your latest valid score is reflected on the official leaderboard. 08 - Finish: When the submission window closes, the final leaderboard determines the winners. Rules & Guidelines: PROMPT RUN is an individual participation hackathon. Team submissions are not allowed. The total hackathon duration is 6 hours . The event is conducted fully online . The project must be related to web development and must follow the given challenge. Participants must use a modern web development framework, library, or technology stack . Raw HTML-only, CSS-only, or Vanilla JavaScript-only projects are not permitted as the primary project stack. Vibe Coding and AI-assisted development tools are allowed. Participants may use their preferred modern frameworks, libraries, APIs, development tools, and supporting technologies. Participants receive 3 submission chances . Every new valid submission replaces the previous submission for leaderboard purposes. Only the latest valid submission will be considered for the final score. The highest score among the three submissions will not automatically be retained. All submitted projects will be evaluated through FAIE - Frontend Arena Intelligent Evaluation Engine . Participants must ensure that their submitted project is functional and accessible for evaluation. Projects should be developed within the official hackathon duration. Participants may use publicly available documentation, libraries, frameworks, and development resources. Participants must not submit plagiarized or substantially copied projects. Any attempt to manipulate the evaluation engine, leaderboard, submission system, or scoring process may result in disqualification. Participants are responsible for testing their project before making their final submission. Submissions made after the official deadline will not be considered. Participants must comply with all technical and submission requirements specified by the organizers. The final results will be determined according to the official final leaderboard . The organizers reserve the right to disqualify submissions that violate the rules or compromise the integrity of the competition. Who Can Participate?: PROMPT RUN is open to: Students Web Developers Frontend Developers Full-Stack Developers UI/UX Designers Vibe Coders AI-assisted Developers Technology Enthusiasts Anyone interested in modern web development, Vibe Coding, rapid prototyping, and building digital products can participate. The Challenge: Participants will be given a specific problem statement at the start of the hackathon. Your task is to understand the challenge and build a creative, functional, and modern web solution within six hours. The project should demonstrate: Clear understanding of the problem Creative solution design Strong UI/UX Functional implementation Modern technology usage Effective development workflow Attention to performance and usability Final Result: The competition follows a simple progression: BUILD → SUBMIT → FAIE → SCORE → LEADERBOARD Every participant gets three chances to improve their project. But remember: Your latest submission is the one that counts. At the end of the hackathon, the final leaderboard will determine the winners. One Participant. Three Chances. Six Hours. One Leaderboard. PROMPT. BUILD. RUN.
prize: Winner: Awarded to the Rank 1 participant on the final PROMPT RUN leaderboard in recognition of outstanding performance, creativity, and successful completion of the hackathon challenge. | Runner-Up Certificate: Awarded to the Rank 2 participant for achieving one of the highest final scores and demonstrating strong technical execution and problem-solving. | Second Runner-Up Certificate: Awarded to the Rank 3 participant for achieving a top position on the final leaderboard and delivering an impressive project. | Certificate of Participation: Awarded to all participants who successfully participate in PROMPT RUN, recognizing their effort, creativity, and contribution to the hackathon.

title: Drishti
description: Drishti is a UI/UX Design hackathon by Vidyalankar Institute of Technology (VIT), Mumbai, designed for team participation. Conducted through online and offline stages, it gives participants the opportunity to demonstrate their creativity, design thinking, and user-focused problem-solving abilities. Participants can showcase their skills in User Experience (UX) Design, User Interface (UI) Design, teamwork, and collaboration. From presenting past work to creating a working prototype and delivering a final pitch, Drishti offers a focused platform to transform ideas into compelling design solutions. Competition Structure: Round 1 - Shortlisting Round: This online selection round focuses on each team's previous work. Both team members must submit their resume and portfolio or case study. Submissions will be assessed on design thinking, creativity, UX/UI skills, problem-solving ability, and overall design potential. The top 35 participants will advance to the offline finale. This round runs from 24 September 2026 to 2 October 2026. Round 2 - Offline Designathon & Final Pitch: Shortlisted teams will compete in an offline Designathon at Vidyalankar Institute of Technology, Mumbai. Teams will receive a new problem statement, then have 2 hours to understand the problem, ideate, design, and develop a working prototype. The round takes place on 9 October 2026. Rewards and Prizes: Rank 1: A cash prize of ₹10,000 and a certificate, recognising the leading team's design achievement. Rank 2: A cash prize of ₹5,000 and a certificate, celebrating an outstanding design performance. Bring your team, showcase your UI/UX talent, and take on Drishti by Vidyalankar Institute of Technology (VIT), Mumbai. Register to turn your design thinking into a working prototype and a powerful final pitch.

title: HackRobo 2.0
description: Overview: HACKROBO 2.0 is a 2-day national hardware hackathon that challenges undergraduate engineering students to design, build, and demonstrate innovative robotic solutions for a real-world environmental challenge. The 2026-27 edition focuses on Riverbank & River Cleaning Robots , with participants working on solutions that can operate in open water while reaching and retrieving debris accumulated along riverbanks. The hackathon encourages teams to combine mechanical design, electronics, embedded systems, robotics, and software to develop a functional prototype addressing the given problem statement. Date: 10-11 October 2026 No. of Days: 2 Days Duration: 36 Hours Members Count: 3-5 per team Eligibility: Undergraduate Engineering Students Inter-Specialization Teams: Allowed Mode: Offline Registration Fees: ₹2,000 per team Venue: Pillai College of Engineering, New Panvel East, Navi Mumbai Theme / Domain: Riverbank & River Cleaning Robots The hackathon focuses on developing robotic solutions for riverbank and river cleaning . Conventional aquatic cleanup systems primarily target floating waste in open water, while significant amounts of plastic and other debris accumulate along muddy riverbanks above the waterline. These areas can be difficult to access using conventional cleanup vessels. Participants are challenged to: Design a robot that can move through open water and reach riverbank debris without getting stuck. Teams are encouraged to explore solutions involving autonomous navigation, manual control, robotic manipulation, buoyancy, waterproofing, and stable operation near challenging shoreline conditions. Suggested Technical Approach Teams may explore a hybrid Autonomous Surface Vessel (ASV) incorporating: Dual-Mode Control: Autonomous GPS/waypoint navigation for open water with manual RC override near the shoreline. Articulated Arm: A 2-4 DoF robotic arm capable of retrieving debris without grounding the vessel. Power & Buoyancy: A stable and waterproof vessel capable of maintaining stability even when the arm is fully extended. Integrated Systems: Combination of mechanical, electronic, embedded, and software systems to achieve the required functionality. Event Format The event will be conducted over 24 hours across two days . Day 1: Registration, orientation, opening ceremony, hackathon commencement, mentoring, networking and jamming session. Day 2: Mentoring, final project submission, judging and winner announcement. Teams will work continuously on their prototypes during the hackathon. Mentors and volunteers will be available to provide technical guidance throughout the event. The detailed schedule is tentative and may be modified by the organizers. Judging Projects will be evaluated based on: Innovation Functionality Impact Presentation Working prototype/demonstration A functional working prototype is strongly encouraged for the final evaluation. Facilities & Perks On-campus accommodation Meals throughout the event Workspace access Mentorship from industry experts Networking opportunities Participation certificates Winner recognition Industry exposure Opportunity to build a real hardware prototype Rules & Guidelines: Teams must consist of 3 to 5 members . Inter-specialization teams are allowed , provided all members are undergraduate engineering students from the same institution. Participants must work on the designated Riverbank & River Cleaning Robots domain. Teams are expected to develop and demonstrate a functional robotic solution to the given problem statement. Teams must complete and submit their project within the specified hackathon timeline. Teams must follow all instructions provided by the organizers and mentors. Only approved resources may be used during the hackathon. Participants must maintain fair play, discipline, and professional conduct throughout the event. Teams must be available for mentoring and evaluation rounds as scheduled. The final project must be submitted before the final judging round. Judges may evaluate the project based on innovation, functionality, impact, and presentation . Any violation of the event guidelines or engagement in unfair practices may result in disqualification. The event schedule is tentative and may be modified by the organizers if required. Decisions made by the organizing and judging committee regarding the competition will be considered final. Prize Pool: ₹75,000 The prize pool will be distributed among the top-performing teams, along with possible special recognition awards. Why Participate? Build a real-world hardware solution Gain hands-on experience in robotics and engineering Work on an environmental challenge Receive mentorship and technical guidance Network with students, mentors, and professionals Gain industry exposure Strengthen your engineering portfolio Earn certificates and recognition Experience an intensive 24-hour hardware hackathon HACKROBO 2.0 is an opportunity to move beyond ideas and build, test, and demonstrate a real robotic solution to a real-world problem.

title: Narayana National Hackathon 2026
organizer: Jai Narayan Vidya Mandir, Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh
description: Narayana National Hackathon 2026 is a multi-stage technology and innovation hackathon organized by Jai Narayan Vidya Mandir, Uttar Pradesh , to provide students, developers, innovators, and emerging technologists with a platform to identify real-world problems, develop technology-driven solutions, build functional prototypes, and present their innovations before an evaluation panel. The hackathon is designed as a 5-round competitive innovation journey , beginning with registration and idea submission and progressing through idea evaluation, prototype development, technical evaluation, and finally the Grand Finale . Participants will have the opportunity to work on innovative solutions across domains such as Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning, Web Development, Mobile Applications, Cloud Computing, Data Science, Cybersecurity, Blockchain, IoT, Automation, SaaS, and other emerging technologies , depending on the selected problem statement or theme. The objective is not simply to develop an idea, but to transform that idea into a practical, technically feasible, scalable, and impactful solution . Registration: Registration Fee: FREE Registration for Narayana National Hackathon 2026 is completely free of cost . Participants are not required to pay any registration fee or participation fee to register for the hackathon. Why Participate? Narayana National Hackathon 2026 provides participants with an opportunity to: Solve real-world and technology-driven problems. Convert innovative ideas into functional prototypes. Work with modern technologies and development frameworks. Demonstrate technical and problem-solving skills. Gain experience in product development and innovation. Present their solutions before an evaluation panel. Compete with teams from different colleges and institutions. Receive recognition for their innovation and technical contribution. Build a project that can potentially be developed further beyond the hackathon. Experience the complete journey from Idea → Validation → Development → Evaluation → Final Presentation . Compete for a total prize pool of ₹1,00,000 . Hackathon Format The competition will be conducted through 5 rounds . Round 1: Registration & Idea Submission Participants will register for the hackathon and form their teams according to the participation guidelines. After registration, teams will select a suitable problem statement/theme and submit their initial idea. The submission may include: Team details Problem statement/title Problem identification Proposed solution Key features Target users Expected impact Proposed technology stack Initial implementation approach The purpose of this round is to understand the problem being addressed and the innovation proposed by the team . Teams should clearly explain what problem they are trying to solve and how their proposed technology-based solution can address it. Round 2: Idea Evaluation & Shortlisting All submitted ideas will go through an evaluation process. The evaluation may consider: Understanding of the problem Relevance of the proposed solution Innovation and originality Technical feasibility Practical applicability Scalability Potential impact Clarity of the proposed approach Based on the evaluation, selected teams will move to the prototype development stage. Teams qualifying for the next stage will receive further instructions regarding the development and submission requirements. Round 3: Prototype Development This round focuses on converting the selected idea into a working prototype or Minimum Viable Product (MVP) . Teams will be expected to develop a demonstrable version of their proposed solution. Depending on the selected problem statement, the prototype may include: Web application Mobile application AI/ML solution SaaS platform Cloud-based application Data-driven solution Automation system IoT-based solution Blockchain-based solution Cybersecurity solution Developer tool Digital platform Other technology-driven solutions Open Innovation Teams should demonstrate the actual functionality of their solution rather than presenting only a conceptual idea. Prototype Submission Teams may be required to provide: Project description Functional prototype/MVP Source code/repository, where applicable Presentation/PPT Architecture diagram Technology stack Feature explanation Demo video Live deployment/prototype link, wherever applicable Additional supporting information The project submission structure will focus on the proposed solution, architecture, innovation, technical details, existing-solution comparison, demonstration, and live deployment/prototype wherever applicable. Round 4: Technical Evaluation & Project Demonstration Shortlisted teams will proceed to the technical evaluation stage. Teams will demonstrate their developed prototype and explain how their solution addresses the selected problem. The evaluation panel may consider: Problem Understanding How clearly does the team understand the problem? Innovation How innovative or differentiated is the proposed solution? Technical Implementation How effectively have the selected technologies been implemented? Functionality Does the prototype work as intended? User Experience Is the solution understandable, usable, and accessible to its intended users? Scalability Can the solution potentially support a larger number of users or expanded use cases? Feasibility Can the solution realistically be implemented beyond the hackathon? Impact What potential value can the solution create? Presentation How clearly does the team communicate its idea, architecture, implementation, and future scope? Demonstration How effectively does the team demonstrate its working prototype? Round 5: Grand Finale The Grand Finale will be the final stage of Narayana National Hackathon 2026. Top 20 Teams A total of 20 teams will be selected for the Grand Finale based on their performance throughout the preceding rounds. These 20 finalist teams will receive instructions regarding: Final presentation Prototype demonstration Presentation format Schedule Participation mode Technical requirements Grand Finale process Hybrid Grand Finale - Offline + Online To make the Grand Finale accessible to participants from different locations, Narayana National Hackathon 2026 will provide a hybrid participation option. The Grand Finale will support both: Offline Participation Teams who are able and willing to travel to the designated Grand Finale venue can participate physically at the venue . Offline finalists will be able to: Present their solution in person. Demonstrate their prototype before the evaluation panel. Interact with judges and organizers. Interact with other finalist teams. Participate in the on-ground Grand Finale experience. Online Participation Teams that are unable to attend the physical Grand Finale due to: Travel constraints Distance from the venue Location-related limitations Academic commitments Other genuine circumstances will have the option to participate in the Grand Finale online . Online finalists will receive the necessary instructions for: Virtual presentation Online prototype demonstration Video conferencing Screen sharing Technical setup Final evaluation Important Grand Finale Policy The Grand Finale is not restricted exclusively to teams that can travel to the physical venue. All 20 selected finalist teams will have the option of participating through the applicable offline or online mode , subject to the final instructions and technical arrangements communicated by the organizers. The hybrid format is intended to provide finalists with flexibility and ensure that travel or geographical limitations do not prevent a selected team from presenting its innovation . Prize Pool Total Prize Pool: ₹1,00,000 The Narayana National Hackathon 2026 will offer a total prize pool of ₹1,00,000 across multiple award categories. Award Prize Prize Money Winner ₹30,000 First Runner-Up ₹20,000 Second Runner-Up ₹20,000 Best Prototype Project ₹10,000 Best Women Team - Idea Award 1 ₹10,000 Best Women Team - Idea Award 2 ₹10,000 Total Prize Pool ₹1,00,000 Winner The team selected as the overall Winner of Narayana National Hackathon 2026 will receive a prize of: ₹30,000 First Runner-Up The team selected as the First Runner-Up will receive: ₹20,000 Second Runner-Up The team selected as the Second Runner-Up will receive: ₹20,000 Best Prototype Project A special award will be presented to the team demonstrating an outstanding functional prototype/project , with a prize of: ₹10,000 This category recognizes strong prototype development, implementation, functionality, and demonstration. Best Women Team - Idea Awards Two teams will be recognized under the Best Women Team Idea category. Best Women Team Idea - Award 1: ₹10,000 Best Women Team Idea - Award 2: ₹10,000 Total Women Team Idea Awards: ₹20,000 These awards are intended to recognize innovative ideas presented by eligible women-led teams, subject to the eligibility and evaluation criteria communicated by the organizers. Grand Finale Presentation During the Grand Finale, each finalist team will present its solution before the evaluation panel. Teams should be prepared to explain: Problem Statement Problem Background Proposed Solution Target Users Key Features Innovation Technical Architecture Technology Stack Development Approach Working Prototype Live Demonstration Existing Solutions and Comparison Advantages of the Proposed Solution Scalability Future Scope Expected Impact The presentation material should clearly communicate the solution, architecture, innovation, technical implementation, existing-solution comparison, demonstration, and live deployment/prototype wherever applicable. Suggested Technology Domains Participants can build solutions using one or more relevant technology domains, depending on the selected problem statement. Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning Machine Learning Deep Learning Natural Language Processing Computer Vision Generative AI Recommendation Systems Predictive Analytics Software Development Web Applications Mobile Applications SaaS Platforms Enterprise Applications Developer Tools Automation Systems Cloud & DevOps Cloud Computing Serverless Architecture Containerization APIs Distributed Systems DevOps Data & Analytics Data Science Data Analytics Business Intelligence Predictive Modeling Data Visualization Emerging Technologies Blockchain Internet of Things Cybersecurity Robotics AR/VR Automation Participants are encouraged to choose technologies that are appropriate to the problem rather than using technology merely for complexity . Evaluation Framework Projects may be evaluated across the following dimensions: Evaluation Area What Will Be Considered Problem Understanding Clarity and relevance of the identified problem Innovation Originality and uniqueness of the solution Technical Approach Appropriateness and implementation of technology Functionality Working capability of the prototype Feasibility Practical possibility of implementation Scalability Potential for expansion and larger adoption User Experience Usability and accessibility Impact Potential value and real-world applicability Presentation Clarity and quality of explanation Demonstration Effectiveness of prototype demonstration The exact criteria, weightage, submission requirements, and timelines may be communicated by the organizers for each round. Team Formation Participants may form teams according to the team-size requirements specified by the organizers on the official hackathon opportunity page. Teams are encouraged to have members with complementary skills such as: Frontend Development Backend Development AI/ML Mobile Development UI/UX Database Management Cloud & DevOps Cybersecurity Research Product Development Business/Market Analysis Presentation A multidisciplinary team can help address different aspects of product development, from technical implementation to user experience and presentation. Who Can Participate? The hackathon is intended for students and emerging technology enthusiasts interested in: Software Development Artificial Intelligence Machine Learning Data Science Cloud Computing Web Development Mobile Development Cybersecurity Blockchain IoT Automation Product Development Technology Innovation Participants should review the eligibility and team-size requirements specified on the official hackathon opportunity page before registering. Code of Conduct & Originality All participating teams are expected to maintain professional conduct throughout the hackathon. Participants must: Submit their own work or work they are legally authorized to use. Respect intellectual property rights. Avoid plagiarism. Provide accurate information regarding their project. Disclose the use of third-party APIs, libraries, datasets, open-source components, or external services wherever required. Follow all rules and instructions communicated by the organizers. Any submission found to violate applicable rules may be subject to review or disqualification according to the event guidelines. Prototype & Project Requirements Participants are encouraged to focus on developing a functional and demonstrable solution . The project should clearly communicate: Problem → Solution → Technology → Implementation → Impact Teams should avoid limiting their submission to only: Static PPTs Concept-only proposals Non-functional mockups A functional prototype/MVP is strongly encouraged wherever the selected problem permits it.

title: Bharat Agentic 2026
description: BHARAT AGENTIC 2026 is a 12-hour online Agentic AI Hackathon powered by AIKart , where participants build AI agents that solve real-world problems across Bharat. Participants can choose from multiple industry domains, including GovTech, AgriTech, EdTech, HealthTech, FinTech, Manufacturing, Business, Mobility, ClimateTech, Bharat Languages, AI & Developer Tools, and Open Innovation. Hackathon: 1 October 2026 Results: 2 October 2026 Mode: 100% Online Duration: 12 Hours Team Size: 1-4 Members Prize Pool: ₹50,000 Internship: Opportunities for selected top performers Rules & Guidelines 1. Eligibility Anyone interested in AI, technology, innovation, or building products can participate. Participants can join individually or in teams. Each team can have 1-4 members . 2. Project Requirements Your project must use Agentic AI in a meaningful way. Projects should solve a real-world problem or provide clear user value. A basic chatbot or simple AI wrapper without meaningful agentic functionality may not qualify. Projects should demonstrate capabilities such as reasoning, planning, tool/API usage, multi-step workflows, or taking actions. 3. Development The core project should be built during the 12-hour hackathon . Open-source libraries, frameworks, APIs, and development tools are allowed. Existing templates, libraries, or components may be used, but significant pre-existing work should be disclosed. Teams must be able to explain their implementation during judging. 4 . Submission Each team must submit: Project name Problem statement Solution overview Agent workflow/architecture Technology stack GitHub repository Working demo 2-3 minute demo video Pitch deck 5. Submission Deadline The final submission must be completed through the official submission portal before the announced deadline on 1 October 2026 . Late submissions may not be considered. 6. Judging Projects will be evaluated based on: Agentic capability Problem relevance and impact Technical implementation Innovation User experience Scalability and feasibility Demo quality 7. Originality Projects must contain meaningful work by the participating team. Plagiarism, fraudulent submissions, or misrepresentation of work may result in disqualification. Teams must properly acknowledge third-party technologies or resources where appropriate. 8. Responsible AI Projects must comply with applicable laws and third-party platform/API terms. Projects involving harmful, illegal, deceptive, or unsafe activities may be rejected. 9. Team Changes Team formation and member changes must be completed before the official deadline announced by the organizers. 10. Final Decision The organizers and judging panel reserve the right to determine eligibility, evaluate submissions, and make final decisions regarding winners and disqualifications.

title: AppSurd'26: Code.Compile.Chaos
organizer: Indian Institute of Technology, Indian School of Mines (IIT ISM), Dhanbad
description: AppSurd '26: Code. Compile. Chaos. is a beginner-friendly app development hackathon conducted by the App Development Division of Cyber Labs - The Technical Society of IIT (ISM) Dhanbad. The event challenges participants to rapidly ideate, build, and pitch a functional cross-platform application based on an unconventional mystery prompt within a compressed 5 to 6-hour development sprint. Guidelines & Eligibility Eligibility: Open to all undergraduate and postgraduate college students interested in mobile application development, UI/UX design, and rapid prototyping. Team Size: Teams must consist of 2 to 3 members . Individual participation is not allowed. Inter-College Teams: Allowed. Team members can belong to different colleges/institutions. Inter-Specialization Teams: Allowed. Team members can be from different academic departments, branches, or years of study. Single Team Restriction: A participant can only register as part of one team. Technology Stack: Mandatory use of Flutter (cross-platform framework). Native Android/iOS or other cross-platform frameworks (React Native, KMP) are not permitted. Development Environment: Teams are responsible for bringing their laptops with pre-installed and tested Flutter SDKs, IDEs (Android Studio / Visual Studio Code), and physical testing devices or emulators. AI Assistance: AI coding assistants (e.g., GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor) are permitted and encouraged for ideation, code generation, debugging, and learning. Process & Round Details Total Problem Statements: 6 Mystery Prompts There are 6 unique mystery challenge prompts prepared for the hackathon (ranging from hyper-focused utility tools to intentional anti-UX challenges). Each team will be randomly assigned 1 prompt during the reveal stage to build their application around. Stages & Duration Stage 1: Registration (Pre-Event) Duration: Open until the registration deadline. Details: Teams register on Unstop and configure their development environments. Stage 2: Opening Ceremony & Briefing Duration: 15 Minutes Details: Overview of hackathon mechanics, tech stack compliance, submission guidelines, and evaluation rubrics. Stage 3: Mystery Prompt Reveal Duration: 10 Minutes Details: Random prompt assignment to each team. Stage 4: Development Sprint Duration: 5 to 6 Hours Details: Live development phase. Teams build their working prototype using Flutter and AI tools. Stage 5: Project Submission Window Duration: 15 Minutes (prior to hackathon conclusion) Details: Submitting source code, runnable build (APK or Web link), slide deck, and AI usage summary. Stage 6: Presentation & Judging Round Duration: 3 to 5 Minutes Demo + 2 to 3 Minutes Q&A per team Details: Teams pitch their working app live to the judging panel and answer technical questions. Stage 7: Results & Prize Distribution Duration: 15 Minutes Details: Score consolidation, winner announcements, and certificate distribution. Competition Rules Stack Compliance: Applications must be built exclusively using Flutter. Submitting applications built on other frameworks will result in immediate disqualification. Fresh Development: All project code must be written during the official 5-6 hour development window. Submitting pre-existing projects, pre-built templates, or work completed prior to the prompt reveal is strictly prohibited. Disclosure of Pre-existing Assets: Any third-party open-source packages, public APIs, or basic boilerplates used must be disclosed during submission. AI Policy & Technical Comprehension: While AI coding assistants are allowed, participants must fully understand the codebase they submit. Judges will test participants' technical comprehension during the Q&A. Inability to explain AI-generated logic will result in heavy mark deductions under the Process evaluation category. Submission Deliverables: To qualify for evaluation, teams must submit all required assets before the submission deadline: Source code link (Public GitHub repository or Zip archive). Runnable application build (APK file or live Flutter Web URL). Presentation/Demo slides (PDF/PPT format). Written AI Usage Declaration (150-200 words). Presentation Compliance: Teams must stick strictly to the 3-5 minute presentation limit. Demonstrations must show a live working application; static UI mockups or video-only presentations will not receive full functionality marks. Fair Play & Integrity: Any form of plagiarism, code theft between teams, or deliberate misrepresentation of work will lead to immediate disqualification. Organizer Authority: Cyber Labs and the appointed judging panel hold the right to make final decisions on disputes, rule interpretations, and unforeseen contingencies. Evaluation Parameters (100 Marks Total) Criterion Marks Parameter Breakdown Product 25 Application functionality, stability, UI/UX execution, technical completeness, and Flutter implementation quality. Prompt Interpretation 25 Creativity, alignment with the randomly assigned mystery prompt, and originality of the solution. Presentation 25 Pitch clarity, effective live product demonstration, UI/UX explanation, and time management. Process 25 Technical understanding during Q&A, effective team collaboration, responsible AI integration, and workflow execution.

title: Python Coding Challenge in Qiskit
description: Description The Python Coding Challenge in Qiskit is an online individual programming competition focused on solving quantum-computing problems using Python and IBM Qiskit . Participants will implement quantum-computing concepts through executable programs and solve programming challenges within the specified competition window. Participants will receive the challenge problems, a supported Python/Qiskit environment, constraints, permitted resources, submission format, and evaluation criteria. Solutions will be evaluated using the published test cases and scoring rules, followed by technical verification before the final results are announced. Rules & Guidelines 1. Eligibility Participation is individual . Participants must satisfy the eligibility requirements specified in the official event announcement. Participants must register using accurate personal information. Participants must have access to the required Python/Qiskit environment. 2. Competition Format The competition consists of programming challenges related to quantum computing . Participants must solve the given problems using Python and IBM Qiskit . Each problem will specify its requirements, constraints and expected output. Solutions must be submitted through the designated competition platform. 3. Technical Environment Participants must use the supported Python and Qiskit versions specified by the organizers. The required environment and setup instructions will be provided before the competition. Participants are responsible for ensuring that their development environment is working before the coding phase begins. 4. Coding Rules Solutions must satisfy the requirements and constraints specified in each problem. Participants may use only the programming languages, libraries and resources explicitly permitted by the organizers. Solutions must produce the required output within the specified constraints. Attempts to manipulate the judging system, test cases or leaderboard are prohibited. 5. Submission Solutions must be submitted through the official submission platform. Each submission will be recorded with its submission timestamp. Only submissions received before the official deadline will be considered, subject to the published rules. Once the submission window closes, no further modifications will be accepted unless an official correction window is provided. 6. Judging & Scoring Solutions will be evaluated using the published judging mechanism, which may consider: Correctness Number of test cases passed Execution efficiency, where applicable Problem-specific requirements Compliance with constraints The exact scoring method and tie-break rules must be published before the competition begins. 7. Use of External Resources Participants may use only the resources explicitly permitted in the official rules. Any prohibited assistance, unauthorized collaboration or sharing of solutions may result in disqualification. Participants must follow the stated rules regarding documentation, libraries, internet access and reference materials. 8. Originality & Collaboration Participants must independently develop their submissions unless collaboration is explicitly permitted. Sharing solutions, copying another participant's code or submitting someone else's work is prohibited. Organizers may conduct code similarity or other integrity checks. 9. AI-Assisted Tools The use of AI coding assistants must follow the official competition policy . If AI tools are restricted or disclosure is required, participants must comply with those requirements. 10. Technical Issues Participants should complete the environment setup before the competition starts. Technical or access issues must be reported through the designated support channel. We believe that the best way to develop engineering and problem-solving skills is to build, experiment, collaborate, and ship . Through hackathons, internships, mentorship, and hands-on projects, Invoqe creates opportunities for students, developers, and aspiring engineers to move beyond tutorials and build solutions to real-world problems.

title: HackSprint
organizer: Guru Tegh Bahadur Institute of Technology (GTBIT), New Delhi
description: HackSprint is a 6-hour hackathon where creativity, coding, problem-solving, and adaptability come together. Teams will be given a challenge domain and will have to transform their ideas into a working web application within a limited time. But there's a twist - the challenge doesn't end with your initial idea. During the hackathon, teams will encounter a surprise challenge that will force them to rethink, adapt, and enhance their solution. How creatively your team responds to the unexpected could make all the difference. From ideation and development to deployment and pitching, HackSprint takes you through the complete journey of turning an idea into a product. The clock is ticking. The challenge is waiting. Will you outthink it? Details Type: Hackathon Duration: 6 Hours Date: 17th October 2026 Time: 10 AM Venue: Guru Tegh Bahadur Institute of Technology Mode: Offline Team Size: 2-4 participants What You Need Laptop with a working development environment Laptop charger, extension board Basic knowledge of web development Familiarity with HTML, CSS and JavaScript is recommended Knowledge of any frontend & backend framework is an advantage Participants are free to use their preferred programming languages, frameworks, libraries and development tools. What You'll Build A functional web application based on the domain revealed during the event. Teams will need to submit: GitHub Repository Live Deployed Application Pitch Deck Hacksprint Flow Round 1 - Check-In & Reveal Get registered, settle in with your team, and discover the challenge domain assigned to you. Round 2 - Ideate & Build Brainstorm your solution, define your approach, and start building your web application. AI-assisted development tools are permitted, but participants must understand and be able to explain their implementation Round 3 - the Twist Just when you think you've got it figured out, expect the unexpected. A surprise challenge will be introduced during the hackathon. Teams will have to adapt their existing idea and integrate the new challenge into their solution. Round 4 - Build, Deploy & Submit Complete your application, integrate the twist, deploy your project and submit your final deliverables. Final Round - Pitch & Q&a Present your product to the judges, demonstrate your solution and defend your decisions during the Q&A. The best teams won't just build. They'll adapt. Rules & Guidlines Follow the team size. Participants must bring their own laptops and chargers. The project must be developed during the hackathon. AI-assisted development tools are permitted, but participants must understand and be able to explain their implementation. Teams must submit a GitHub repository, deployed application link, presentation and pitch deck before the submission deadline. Plagiarism, copying another team's work or unfair practices will result in disqualification. Teams must ensure that all third-party assets, APIs, libraries and datasets used are legally usable. Participants are expected to maintain professional conduct throughout the event.
