title: AXION Hackathon
description: AXION HACKATHON - STAMPERS About the Hackathon STAMPERS presents AXION HACKATHON , a 24-hour online Open Innovation Hackathon powered by Unstop , bringing together students from different colleges, universities, branches and backgrounds to identify real-world problems and build innovative technology-driven solutions. AXION is designed to give participants the freedom to choose a problem that matters to them and transform their ideas into a functional prototype within 24 hours. Participants will get the opportunity to ideate, develop, test and present their solutions while collaborating with their teammates in an intensive hackathon environment. Event Details Event Name: AXION HACKATHON Organized by: STAMPERS Powered By: Unstop Date: 11 October 2026 Day: Sunday Duration: 24 Hours Mode: Online Theme: Open Innovation Team Size: 2-4 Members Registration: Exclusively through Unstop Eligibility The hackathon is open to college and university students . Students from recognized colleges/universities across India can participate. Students from any year of study are eligible. Students from any branch, specialization or academic discipline can participate. Students from Computer Science, Information Technology, Electronics, Electrical, Mechanical, Civil, AI/ML, Data Science, Management, Design and other disciplines are welcome. Inter-college teams are allowed. Inter-specialization/inter-department teams are allowed. Teams can consist of students from different colleges and different academic backgrounds. Participants must complete their registration through the official Unstop opportunity page. Team Formation Each team must have 2 to 4 members . A participant can be part of only one team . Inter-college teams are permitted. Inter-specialization teams are permitted. Teams may include members with different technical and non-technical skills. Every team must have a Team Leader . All team members must register individually on Unstop as instructed. Teams are responsible for ensuring that their team information is accurate. Hackathon Theme - Open Innovation AXION follows an Open Innovation format. There is no single fixed problem statement that all teams must solve. Instead, participants are encouraged to identify a genuine problem and develop an innovative technology-based solution. Possible areas include: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning Web Development Mobile Applications Cybersecurity FinTech EdTech HealthTech Sustainability Smart Cities Agriculture Climate & Environment Social Impact Accessibility Automation Blockchain & Web3 Internet of Things Data Science Productivity Campus Technology Other technology-driven domains Teams are free to choose their own domain as long as the project demonstrates a meaningful problem, solution and implementation. Hackathon Format The hackathon will be conducted for 24 continuous hours . Phase 1 - Ideation Teams identify a real-world problem and develop their initial solution concept. Phase 2 - Problem Definition Teams should clearly define: The problem Target users Existing challenges Proposed solution Why the solution is needed Phase 3 - Development Teams build their prototype/MVP during the hackathon. Phase 4 - Testing Teams test their solution, identify issues and improve their implementation. Phase 5 - Final Submission Teams submit their project and other required materials according to the official submission instructions. Phase 6 - Evaluation The submitted projects will be evaluated by the judging panel based on the applicable judging criteria. Number of Problem Statements AXION is an Open Innovation Hackathon . Therefore, there is no fixed number of problem statements . Each team will: Identify its own problem → Develop its own solution → Build a working prototype → Submit the project. Project Requirements Teams are expected to build a functional prototype, MVP or demonstrable implementation. Projects may include: Web applications Mobile applications AI/ML solutions Software platforms Automation systems IoT solutions Data-driven applications Hardware + software solutions Cybersecurity solutions Other technology-based innovations The final project should demonstrate a clear connection between the identified problem and the proposed solution. What Teams Should Submit Teams may be required to provide: Project Title Problem Statement Solution Description Key Features Technology/Tech Stack Project Demo Source Code/Repository , where applicable Project Presentation/Pitch Deck , if requested Demo Video , if requested Team Details The exact submission requirements and submission method will be communicated through the official Unstop opportunity and organizing team. Judging Criteria Projects may be evaluated on the following parameters: Innovation Originality and uniqueness of the idea. Problem Relevance How clearly the project addresses a genuine and meaningful problem. Technical Implementation Quality and effectiveness of the technology used. Functionality How effectively the prototype demonstrates the proposed solution. User Experience Usability, interface design and overall user experience. Impact Potential social, economic, environmental or technological impact. Scalability Potential for the solution to be expanded and used by a larger audience. Presentation Clarity of the team's explanation, demonstration and overall presentation. Rules & Regulations Registration for AXION HACKATHON must be completed exclusively through Unstop . Every team member must complete the required Unstop registration. Team size must be between 2 and 4 members . A participant cannot participate in multiple teams. Inter-college teams are allowed. Inter-specialization teams are allowed. Participants must join the official AXION WhatsApp group. Participants must follow all instructions communicated by STAMPERS and through Unstop. Participants must submit their projects within the announced submission deadline. Late submissions may not be accepted. Plagiarism and unauthorized copying of another team's work are strictly prohibited. Teams must not falsely claim ownership of another person's or organization's project. Teams may use open-source libraries, APIs, datasets and development tools, subject to their respective licenses. Teams should appropriately acknowledge significant third-party resources where applicable. Participants are responsible for ensuring that their project complies with applicable laws and regulations. Projects must not contain unlawful, harmful or malicious content. Participants must maintain professional and respectful conduct throughout the event. Any attempt to manipulate submissions, judging or registration information may result in disqualification. Teams must be able to explain their project and demonstrate their contribution. The organizing team reserves the right to disqualify participants or teams that violate the stated rules. The decision of the organizing/judging team regarding rule violations and evaluation will be final. Event schedules or procedures may be modified by the organizers when necessary, with updates communicated through official channels. Originality & Use of AI Participants may use commonly available development tools, frameworks, APIs, libraries and AI-assisted development tools. However, the team must understand and be able to explain the submitted solution. Using AI tools does not remove the team's responsibility for: Originality Code quality Project functionality Accuracy Proper attribution where required Compliance with third-party licenses Submitting a copied project or representing someone else's work as the team's own may result in disqualification.

title: Ignite Series - Open Innovation Challenge
description: Think. Build. Pitch. IGNITE. IGNITE Series - Open Innovation Challenge is a 15-day innovation competition organized by the Startup & Entrepreneurship Club, Chandigarh University , where students get the opportunity to transform their ideas into structured, market-ready solutions. Unlike conventional competitions with predefined problem statements, IGNITE gives participants the freedom to choose a problem they genuinely want to solve and develop their own innovative solution. From identifying a problem to validating the market, developing an MVP, designing a business model, and presenting the idea through a pitch deck - participants are encouraged to approach their idea like a real startup. Eligibility Open to Students from Colleges and Universities Across India . Team Size: 2-6 Members Inter-College Teams Are Allowed Inter-Specialization / Interdisciplinary Teams Are Allowed Students from Different Academic Backgrounds Are Encouraged to Collaborate. Each Participant Can Be a Member of Only One Team . How It Works Competition Duration: 15 Days The Complete Challenge Will Take Place Through the Startup & Entrepreneurship Club's Official Platform . Step 1 - Register Teams Register for The Ignite Open Innovation Challenge . Step 2 - Develop Your Idea Teams Identify a Real-World Problem and Develop Their Proposed Solution. Participants Can Work on Areas Such As: Domains AI & Technology FinTech Cybersecurity Healthcare Sustainability Education Business & Startups Social Impact Logistics And Much More! Step 3 - Submit Teams Submit Their Innovation Along with The Required Information, Including: Problem Statement Proposed Solution Target Market Market Validation Mvp / Prototype Business Model Go-To-Market Strategy Pitch Deck Step 4 - Edit & Improve Teams Can Edit and Update Their Submission at Any Time Before the Competition Deadline . This Allows Participants to Continuously Improve Their Idea, Mvp, Business Model, and Pitch Based on Their Progress During the 15-Day Challenge. ️ Once the Submission Deadline Passes, No Further Modifications Will Be Allowed. Step 5 - Judging After the Submission Deadline, the Ignite Judging Panel will Evaluate the Final Submissions. All Teams Will Be Evaluated on A 100-Point Scale across Five Core Criteria. Step 6 - Results After Evaluation, the Results Will Be Announced by The Organizers. Winners and Selected Participants Will Receive Recognition and Certificates as Applicable. Evaluation Criteria Teams Will Be Evaluated by The Judging Panel on A 100-Point Scale across the Following Five Criteria: R1 - Team Alignment Maximum: 20 Points Evaluation Of: Co-Founder/team Compatibility ️ Balanced Skill Sets Technical + Business Capabilities ‍‍‍ Team Composition and Collaboration R2 - Market Size Maximum: 20 Points Evaluation Of: Significance of The Problem Customer/problem Validation ️ Customer Surveys and Interviews Tam / Sam / Som Analysis Market Opportunity R3 - ️ Mvp Execution Maximum: 20 Points Evaluation Of: Quality of The Mvp/live Demo Technical Implementation Design and Aesthetics ️ Ui/ux Execution Usability and Functionality R4 - Business Model Maximum: 20 Points Evaluation Of: Monetization Strategy Pricing Structure Go-To-Market Strategy Financial Model Scalability and Sustainability R5 - Pitch Deck Maximum: 20 Points Evaluation Of: Completeness of The Pitch Deck Conciseness and Clarity Storytelling Communication of The Idea Presentation Structure Total Score R1 Team Alignment - 20 R2 Market Size - 20 R3 Mvp Execution - 20 R4 Business Model - 20 R5 Pitch Deck - 20 Total: 100 Points Rules & Regulations Each Team Must Consist of 2-6 Members . Inter-College and Interdisciplinary Teams Are Permitted. Teams Are Free to Choose Their Own Problem Statement and Domain. All Submissions Must Be the Team's Original Work . Plagiarism, Copied Ideas, Fabricated Validation, or Misrepresentation May Lead to Disqualification. Participants May Use Ai Tools, Ap Is, Open-Source Technologies, and Third-Party Resources, but Their Contribution and Usage Should Be Appropriately Represented. Teams May Edit and Update Their Submission until The Official Deadline . After the Deadline, Submissions Will Be Locked for Evaluation. Judging Will Be Based on The 100-Point Evaluation Framework mentioned Above. The Judging Panel Will Evaluate the Final Version of Each Team's Submission. ️ the Decision of The Judging Panel Regarding Evaluation and Results Will Be Final. Participants Must Adhere to All Deadlines Communicated by The Organizers.

title: Jāgriti Hacks
description: Jāgriti Hacks 2026 is a national-level virtual hackathon bringing together India's brightest builders to solve real, hard problems across AI/ML, DevOps & Cloud, and Cybersecurity. All updates, round announcements, and mentor support will be shared via our official WhatsApp community - joining is mandatory for all registered participants: https://chat.whatsapp.com/FGS2jlqbEEZEysEkuKLS47 Guidelines: Eligibility: Open to all students and early-career professionals across India - undergraduate, postgraduate, and recent graduates. Team size: Exactly 4 members (fixed - no smaller or larger teams accepted). Gender requirement: Every team must include at least 1 female participant. Teams not meeting this at registration are not eligible to compete. Inter-college teams: Allowed - team members do not need to be from the same college/university. Inter-specialization teams: Allowed - members from different specializations/branches (e.g. CS, ECE, IT) can team up. Track & problem statement selection: Each team selects one track (AI/ML, DevOps & Cloud, or Cybersecurity) and one problem statement from that track at registration. Number of problem statements: 15 total - 5 per track. Format: 100% virtual, multi-round. Duration of rounds: Round 1 (PPT Submission): 26 Sept, 6:00 AM - 12:00 PM IST Round 2 (Coding Sprint): 26 Sept, 5:30 PM - 27 Sept, 12:00 PM IST (~18.5 hours) Live Demo & Technical Evaluation: 27 Sept, 12:00 PM - 28 Sept, 1:00 AM IST Final Refinement Window (Top 20 only): 28 Sept, 6:00 AM - 6:00 PM IST Final Demo & PPT Presentation: 28 Sept, after 6:00 PM IST Winners Announced: 29 Sept, 10:00 AM IST Rules: Team composition is locked once Round 1 (PPT) is submitted - no swapping members after that point. Each participant may be part of only one team for the duration of the event. Women in Tech Award: Open only to all-women teams (all 4 members female) - awarded to the highest-scoring all-women team independent of overall placement..

Rewards & Prizes: Total Prize Pool: ₹2,25,000 Winner - ₹1,00,000 1st Runner-Up - ₹75,000 2nd Runner-Up - ₹50,000 All participants also receive a certificate of participation, mentorship from industry and academic experts, pan India visibility for their project, and opportunities to take the idea forward with partner organisations. title: Code and Craft - SSN SNUC Invente '26
description: Code and Craft is the premier Design & Development competition, where you can showcase your creativity and subject your development skills to bring it to life. Code it. Craft it. Show it. Guidelines: Eligibility: Open to students from all colleges and universities Team Size: 1-3 participants per team Inter-College Teams: Allowed. title: Open Source Sprint - Hyderabad's Largest Open Source Hackathon
description: About Open Source Sprint Open Source Sprint is India's largest open source hackathon - a 24-hour building experience hosted at Malla Reddy University, Hyderabad, Telangana, on October 14-15, 2026. Powered by ElevenLabs as the Title Sponsor, the event offers ElevenLabs prizes worth ₹4.5 Lakh+, along with exciting additional prizes and swags - all with zero entry fee. title: Hackyard Build 2026
description: Important: Complete Both Registration Steps To participate in Hackyard BUILD 2026, complete both registrations by 10 October 2026: Register on Unstop. Complete the official Hackyard BUILD 2026 registration at https://hackyard.org/build2026 . Both steps are required for your Hackyard BUILD 2026 registration to be complete. If you have already registered on Unstop, please complete Step 2 using the same email address so we can match your registration. Join the Hackyard Slack workspace for event updates and to connect with other participants : Join Hackyard on Slack About the Opportunity: Hackyard Build 2026 is a hybrid hackathon organized by Hackyard for developers, designers, innovators, and student builders to turn ideas into working technology solutions. The hackathon follows a two-round format: Round 1: Idea Submission: Participants will submit their idea and proposed solution online. Submissions will be evaluated based on problem relevance, innovation, feasibility, potential impact, and execution potential. Selected teams will be invited to the final round. Round 2: Grand Finale: Shortlisted teams will participate in the in-person final hackathon at IIT Guwahati. Teams will build a functional prototype, work collaboratively, and present their solution to a panel of judges. Registration for Round 2 is completely free. Selected participants attending the in-person round will only need to pay a nominal fee for food and accommodation. Projects will be evaluated by the jury on: Build: 40% Problem: 20% Ingenuity: 20% Potential: 20% Team Participation: Participate solo or form a team of 2-4 members (maximum 4). Teams may include developers, designers, researchers, entrepreneurs, and students from different backgrounds. Eligibility: The hackathon is open to students, developers, designers, innovators, and technology enthusiasts interested in building software-based solutions. Format: Round 1: Online | Idea Submission Round 2: Offline | IIT Guwahati | Final Hackathon Come with an idea, build with your team, and take it from concept to a working solution at Hackyard Build 2026. *Hackyard T-shirt Raffle️* Want to win an exclusive Hackyard T-shirt? Follow @the.hackyard on Instagram and share any Hackyard Build 2026 post on your Instagram Story. Make sure to tag @the.hackyard to enter the raffle! One lucky participant will win a Hackyard T-shirt! Frequently Asked Questions: Participation: What Is Hackyard Build 2026? A builder experience where ideas, problems, skills, and ambitious people come together to make something real. Are Applications Free? Yes. Applications are free, open to everyone, and run online from 14 September to 10 October 2026. Do I Need a Finished Product? No. Submit an idea, problem, or skill you would bring to a build. No finished product or polished pitch deck is required. If you already have a prototype, you can include a public link in the optional work-link field. What Happens After I Apply? Applications close on 10 October. The review window and selection-result date are still to be confirmed. Hackyard will contact selected builders with attendance details before travel. If you applied with a team, connect your team with a private team code after submitting. The physical build is at IIT Guwahati on 24-25 October 2026. Can I Participate Alone? Yes. Apply solo, with a team, or as someone looking for teammates. Every person submits their own application. Teams are connected with a private team code. How Do Team Codes Work? If you choose With a team, your team must have 2-4 people, with a maximum of 4. Submit your own application first. After submission, create a team to get a private code like HYB-7K4P2, or join an existing team with a code from a teammate. Everyone on the team must apply individually. Can I Connect My Team Later? Yes. If you do not have your team code yet, submit your application and connect the team later from your application status page. Your application remains valid without a connected team. Do I Need to Be a Developer? No. Building is not limited to code. Designers, researchers, operators, founders, and people with strong problem-solving skills are welcome. Building: Who Gets the $100 Hackyard LLM Credits? Every selected project gets one $100 LLM credit allocation from Hackyard. A solo builder receives the allocation directly; a 2-4-person team shares one allocation for its project. What Does Participant Mean? A participant is one individual applicant. You count as one participant whether you apply solo, apply as part of a 2-4-person team, or apply while looking for teammates. How Do Project Rewards Work for Solo Builders and Teams? A project means one competing build. A solo participant's build counts as one project, and a registered team of 2-4 participants shares one project. Project rewards are issued once per project, not once per person. Someone looking for teammates becomes part of the project they ultimately build; if they continue solo, their build counts as one project. What Can I Build? Anything worth building. Follow one of our suggested directions or build something completely your own. AI is a powerful building layer, not a requirement. Physical Build: Where and When Is the Physical Build? The physical build is a 24-hour hackathon at IIT Guwahati on 24-25 October 2026. Event entry is free. Travel to and from IIT Guwahati is not covered. Food and accommodation will be available at a participant fee; exact amounts will be shared with selected builders before travel. When Will Prizes Be Announced? Cash prize funding is not confirmed. Final prize details will be published only when confirmed.

title: Seize da Flaq - CTF
description: Overview Seize da Flaq is a national-level Capture The Flag (CTF) cybersecurity competition designed to challenge participants with realistic, hands-on problems across multiple domains of cybersecurity. From web exploitation and cryptography to digital forensics, OSINT, reverse engineering, and other security challenges, participants will need to think like real-world security professionals to uncover vulnerabilities, exploit weaknesses, investigate evidence, and capture flags. The competition follows a two-stage format, giving participants an opportunity to prove their skills before entering the final battlefield. Stage 1 - Prescreening Round 16 October 2026 4:00 PM - 12:00 AM 8 Hours | Online The prescreening round will test participants across a diverse range of cybersecurity challenges. Teams will compete on the live platform, and the top-performing teams will qualify for the Grand Finale. Stage 2.1 - Grand Finale 21-22 November 2026 12:00 PM, 21 November - 8:00 AM, 22 November 20 Hours | On-site Stage 2.2 - Final Evaluation 8:00 AM - 11:00 AM, 22 November 2026 Qualified teams will enter the Grand Finale, an intense on-site CTF where they will face advanced and carefully crafted cybersecurity challenges. The Grand Finale is designed to test not only how quickly participants can capture flags, but also their ability to understand, reproduce, document, and demonstrate their techniques. Winner Validation The final leaderboard will not be the sole basis for determining the winners. After the competition, the Top 10 teams will be required to submit their write-ups, technical presentations, and Proof of Concept (PoC) demonstrating how they solved the challenges. The organizing team will evaluate: Technical understanding of the challenges Methodology and approach Quality and correctness of the PoC Technical presentation and ability to explain Authenticity of the submitted write-ups The final winners will be announced after the completion of the technical evaluation and validation process. Competition Guidelines The competition will run continuously for the specified duration. Sharing flags, solutions, write-ups, PoCs, or accounts is strictly prohibited. Any form of cheating, unauthorized collaboration, or exploitation of vulnerabilities in the CTF infrastructure/platform will result in immediate disqualification. Automated tools are permitted only where they are relevant to solving the intended challenges; abuse of automation against the competition infrastructure is prohibited. Participants must not attempt to disrupt, damage, or gain unauthorized access to the CTF platform or infrastructure. Final results are subject to flag validation, technical review, and anti-cheat verification. During the Grand Finale, participants are not permitted to leave the event venue after the competition begins, except in the case of a genuine emergency. In such cases, only the affected participant(s) may leave after approval and verification by the organizing team. Unauthorized departure from the venue may result in disciplinary action or disqualification of the team. The battlefield is live. The flags are waiting. Are You Ready to Seize the Flaq? Think. Exploit. Investigate. Defend. Capture.

Control your robot, defend your goal, outplay your opponent, and score by getting the ball completely across the goal line. Guidelines Team & Robot Specifications Team Size: 2 participants per team Maximum Dimensions: 350 × 350 mm (L × W) Maximum Weight: 3 kg, including chassis, kicking mechanism, and batteries Maximum Voltage: 3S LiPo, 12V DC/3s (fully charged) - IC engines, pneumatics, and compressors prohibited Control: Fully wireless (RF or Bluetooth) manual control - no wired tethers, autonomous operation strictly banned Ball Handling: at least 50% of the ball's surface must remain exposed at all times - mechanisms that fully trap, grab, suction, or swallow the ball are prohibited Participants must bring their own robot, controller, and necessary spares Pre-Event Inspection Teams must report to the arena at least 30 minutes before the official start time Every robot undergoes a technical inspection and weigh-in; robots failing weight, dimension, power, or ball-handling checks will be disqualified before the match begins Arena & Match Format Arena: 8 ft × 4 ft, with 60 cm wide goal posts on each side Single-elimination knockout format, with byes (for uneven team counts) assigned via random draw A standard match consists of 2 rounds of up to 90 seconds each; the ball starts at centre with robots inside their defence "D" until the referee's signal A goal is scored when the ball completely crosses the goal line; a round is won by the first team to score, or tied if no goal is scored in 90 seconds A team wins the match by winning both rounds, or winning one and tying the other 30-second break between rounds, with teams switching sides If the ball goes out of bounds, play pauses, robots freeze in place, and the ball resets to centre A robot that completely stops working mid-round causes an automatic round forfeit for that team (it may still play the next round if repaired during the break) An unsafe or uncontrollable robot may be removed from the match by the referee, who may also stop play for safety, ball recovery, or technical reasons Tie-Breaker If tied after 2 rounds, a 3rd Tie-Breaker Round (max 90 seconds, first goal wins) is played If the 3rd round also ends 0-0, the winner is the team with the fewest accumulated penalties across all three rounds If goals and penalties are completely tied, judges decide based on Aggression and Control Judging Criteria Penalties are tallied (not awarded as free kicks) and used as a tie-breaker: Stalling (5-second rule): holding/pinning/trapping the ball in one position for over 5 seconds - 1 penalty point Goal camping (5-second rule): parking entirely inside your own goal for over 5 seconds without playing the ball - 1 penalty point Wall pinning (5-second rule): pinning the opponent against the arena wall while fighting for the ball for over 5 seconds - description: Overview: 12-Hour Offline AI Hack Day in Indore About the Event: Most hackathons end the exact same way: you spend the weekend writing code, show a slide deck, and after the event, the project is abandoned and forgotten. We are here to change that. Organised by TECHhelp4U and backed by Major League Hacking (MLH), with Google Gemini as the official technology partner, Stage 02 // System Matrix is an action-packed, 12-hour offline building sprint in Indore. This isn't just a competition to win prizes-it's a launchpad for your next venture. We want builders to step in with a founder mindset: pick a real problem, build a working AI product using code, and show a clear future roadmap for how you plan to turn your build into a real startup. Top-performing teams will earn direct mentorship, ecosystem support, and fast-track invitations to Stage 03 (Kurukshetra) to help turn their prototypes into active companies! What Should You Build? (100% AI Tracks): Stage 02 is exclusively focused on artificial intelligence. We encourage teams to leverage Google Gemini to build intelligent, practical solutions across any of the following focus areas: The Google Gemini Spotlight Track: Build smart applications utilising Google Gemini's multimodal and large-context capabilities: Multimodal Problem Solvers: Applications that process text, audio, images, and video together to solve real-world problems. Deep Context Engines: Tools that analyse large repositories, documents, or knowledge bases in seconds. Context-Aware Assistants: Helpful AI companions that understand user context and automate daily workflows. Autonomous Agents & Workflows: Self-operating task agents that can plan, execute, and troubleshoot without manual oversight. Autonomous research, document synthesis, or customer support workflows. Intelligent bots that assist software teams with code review, automated testing, or bug detection. Developer & Creator Productivity Tools: Smart developer tools, CLI utilities, and automated debugging assistants. Workflow enhancers for writers, creators, designers, or product teams. AI for Real-World Industry Impact: Healthcare & Wellness: AI tools that help organise clinic notes, assist patients, or streamline records. Education & Learning: Personalised interactive tutors and regional language learning tools. Commerce & Small Businesses: Automated bookkeeping, smart support assistants, or intelligent fraud detection. Competition Rounds & Structure: Round 1: Online Application & Idea Screening (Online): Register your team of 2-4 members on Unstop. Submit a brief summary of the problem you want to solve, your planned AI architecture, and your team's background. Shortlisted teams will receive official invitations and an entry badge for the offline finale in Indore. Round 2: The 12-Hour Offline Hack Sprint (Indore): Kickoff & Mentor Sync: Arrive at the venue, set up your workstation, and review your architecture with industry mentors. Live Product Demo: A working application running live. No video recordings or static Figma screens are allowed during judging. Startup Roadmap (1-Page Summary or Short Slide Deck): Target Customer: Who has this problem, and why will they use your solution? Business Model: How will this product sustain itself or generate revenue? Future Milestones: What are the next 3 to 6 steps you will take over the next 3 to 6 months to launch this? AI Integration & Tech Depth - 30%: How effectively is AI, including Google Gemini, integrated into the core product logic? Is the code clean and well-structured? Problem-Solution Fit & Startup Value - 20%: Does the project solve a real, painful problem that people or businesses would pay for? Future Startup Roadmap - 20%: Does the team have a realistic 3-to-6-month post-hackathon plan to scale this into an active venture? Teams must balance speed, control, and defensive strategy to outmaneuver their opponents in a fast-paced knockout tournament - bringing their own robot, controller, and spare parts. Guidelines Team Size & Eligibility 2 participants per team Open to undergraduate/postgraduate students and eligible participants from colleges/institutions Valid college/institutional ID is mandatory Only registered participants may compete; one participant cannot be registered in two teams for the same event Team composition cannot be changed after the registration deadline without written approval from the Event Coordinator The registered team captain is the official point of contact Robot Specifications Specification Requirement Maximum Dimensions 350 × 350 mm (L × W) Maximum Weight 3 kg, including chassis, kicking mechanism, and batteries Maximum Voltage 3S LiPo, 12V DC/3s (fully charged) - IC engines, pneumatics, and compressors prohibited Control Fully wireless (RF or Bluetooth) manual control - no wired tethers, autonomous operation strictly banned Ball Handling At least 50% of the ball's surface must remain exposed at all times - mechanisms that fully trap, grab, suction, or swallow the ball are prohibited Pre-Event Inspection Teams must report to the arena at least 30 minutes before the official start time Every robot undergoes a technical inspection and weigh-in; robots failing weight, dimension, power, or ball-handling checks will be disqualified before the match begins Arena & Match Format Arena: 8 ft × 4 ft, with 60 cm wide goal posts on each side Single-elimination knockout format, with byes (for uneven team counts) assigned via random draw A standard match consists of 2 rounds of up to 90 seconds each; the ball starts at centre with robots inside their defence "D" until the referee's signal A round is won by the first team to score; if no goal is scored in 90 seconds, the round is tied A team wins the match by winning both rounds, or winning one and tying the other 30-second break between rounds, with teams switching sides If the ball goes out of bounds, play pauses, robots freeze in place, and the ball resets to centre A robot that completely stops working mid-round causes an automatic round forfeit for that team (it may still play the next round if repaired during the break) Tie-Breaker If tied after 2 rounds, a 3rd Tie-Breaker Round (max 90 seconds, first goal wins) is played If the 3rd round also ends 0-0, the winner is the team with the fewest accumulated penalties across all three rounds If goals and penalties are completely tied, judges decide based on Aggression and Control Judging Criteria Penalties are tallied (not awarded as free kicks) and used as a tie-breaker: Stalling (5-second rule): holding/pinning/trapping the ball in one position for over 5 seconds - 1 penalty point Goal camping (5-second rule): parking entirely inside your own goal for over 5 seconds without playing the ball - 1 penalty point Wall pinning (5-second rule): pinning the opponent against the arena wall while fighting for the ball for over 5 seconds - 1 penalty point Aggressive ramming: intentionally and repeatedly ramming the opponent instead of playing the ball - 1 penalty point Hand touches: manually resetting a flipped/stuck robot - 1 penalty point each Disqualification The following will result in disqualification: Exceeding the published dimensions, weight, or voltage limits Using a wired controller or autonomous operation Ball-trapping/suction mechanisms that leave less than 50% of the ball exposed Deliberately damaging another team's robot Receiving unauthorized external assistance Cheating, misconduct, tampering with another team's equipment, or misrepresentation of identity Poor social conduct, misbehaviour, foul/abusive language, or intentional damage to the arena or opponent's robot The Event Jury/Referee/Technical Committee holds final authority on match decisions, technical eligibility, penalties, disqualification, scoring, rule interpretation, and safety decisions. Right to appeal: penalized teams may present their case to the Event Coordinators, but the administration's verdict is final. NOTE-: Registration Fees are not refundable.

title: Digital Twin Challenge 2026
description: The future of medicine is proactive, not reactive. At the upcoming Happiest Health Reimagining and Reforming Healthcare in India Summit - 2026, Bengaluru , we are exploring the frontiers of digital health, focusing heavily on the concept of the Digital Twin. A Digital Twin in healthcare is a dynamic, virtual replica of a patient, constantly updated with real-time data from wearables, paired with Electronic Health Records (EHR). By simulating a patient's unique physiology, it can predict adverse health events before they happen and personalize treatment protocols. We are inviting the brightest minds from India's top university incubators to build the foundational prototypes of this future. We challenge student teams to build a proof-of-concept (PoC) Digital Twin Model focused on predicting a specific, localized health outcome. Because building a complete, whole-body Digital Twin is beyond the scope of a short-term project, teams must select one specific chronic or lifestyle condition prevalent in India (e.g., Type 2 Diabetes, Hypertension, or Cardiovascular risk). Eligibility Open to students interested in AI, healthcare, data science and digital health, including students from relevant technical, medical and interdisciplinary backgrounds. Team Formation Guidelines: A team will consist of 1-4 students, and the one who registers the team will be the team leader. Inter-college and interdisciplinary teams can participate. Only full-time students can participate. All the team members are required to verify and confirm their details to form a team. There is no restriction on the number of individuals/teams from an institute. Modification of team post registration will not be allowed. Two members from each of the finalist teams will need to travel to Bengaluru to present their solution in front of an audience at the summit. (Happiest Health will sponsor travel and stay) Phases of the Challenge: Phase 1 - Prototype & Code Submission The teams build their Digital Twin proof-of-concept and submit the completed project with required documentation as specified in the submission guidelines below under GitHub repository. Submitted solutions are evaluated by the technical and expert panel. Top 5 teams will be finalized by the jury, and an email communication will be sent to top 5 shortlisted team by Happiest Health The prototype must successfully demonstrate the fusion of two data streams: Static/Historical data: Simulated Electronic Health Records (demographics, past diagnoses, lab results, genetic markers). Dynamic/Real-time data: Simulated or open-source time-series data from consumer wearables/IoT sensors (heart rate variability, continuous glucose monitors, sleep stages, step count). The output: A working algorithmic model that ingests these two streams and successfully predicts an adverse event (e.g., predicting a sudden glucose spike 2 hours in advance, or flagging a high-risk cardiovascular anomaly based on a week of sleep and heart-rate data). Teams must also present a conceptual UI dashboard showing how a doctor would interact with this virtual patient. Navigating data constraints (The sandbox rules) We recognize that access to real patient data is restricted by privacy laws like the DPDP Act and HIPAA. Teams are strictly required to use anonymized, open-source, or synthetic datasets for training their models. For EHRs: Teams may use synthetic patient generation tools (like Synthea) or anonymized clinical databases (like MIMIC-IV). For sensor data: Teams may utilize open-source wearable datasets or generate their own synthetic time-series data mimicking Apple Health, Google Fit, or dedicated medical IoT devices. Submission Guidelines : Submit the project through a public GitHub repository link. Include all the details mentioned below in the README file of the repository. Team details and college/incubator information Project Title Problem statement and healthcare use case Technical stack, AI/ML model or framework details Minimum 2-5-minute video explaining and demonstrating your prototype. The video can be recorded as a PowerPoint presentation or uploaded as an unlisted YouTube video. Open-source license details Architecture diagram in PDF/PPT format Presentation in PDF/PPT format with project details and outcome Submission Instructions Folder name: Team Name_College Name Set the GitHub repository link access to Public, Ensure that all files and links are accessible to the evaluation team. Submit only the Team leaders name, phone number, email id and Public GitHub repository link on the submission platform. Phase 2 - Final Jury Presentation After the initial screening, the top 10 teams will present their solution and demonstrate their working prototype to the expert jury virtually, showcasing both the technical implementation and real-world healthcare impact. Phase 3 - Summit Showcase The top 5 teams will be invited to present their solution at the Reimagining and Reforming Healthcare in India Summit 2026, Bengaluru, on 20 November 2026. Winners will be announced following the final evaluation. Travel and stay for two members from each team will be sponsored by Happiest Health. Rewards & Opportunities Grand Finale winners/winning team will receive INR 1 lakh cash and a certificate. 1st Runner-Up/1st Runner-Up team will receive INR 50,000 cash and a certificate. 2nd Runner-Up/2nd Runner-Up team will receive INR 30,000 cash and a certificate Two teams will receive a Special Recognition Award of INR 10,000 each. The winning teams will earn PPI Opportunities to intern with Happiest Health.

title: Amazon Selling Partner API Integration Challenge
description: The Problem: On Amazon, the delivery promise a customer sees - "Get it by Tuesday" - is among the strongest drivers of conversion. It is not one national number. It varies by pincode, and follows directly from three things Plantex already controls: where stock sits, how much sits there, and order cutoffs. Plantex already plans stock placement against demand clusters and runs the rebalancing engine that acts on those plans. This project closes the loop - measuring the delivery promise those placement decisions actually produce, at pincode granularity, continuously. A working internal prototype already does the hard part: it queries the Selling Partner API (getFulfillmentPreview) for an estimated arrival date for a given SKU to a given pincode, and assembles a SKU x pincode matrix. Your job is to take it from a script to a system. Project Scope: In Scope: Collection: Automated, scheduled, resumable gathering of delivery-promise data via the Amazon SP-API. Storage: A queryable store that holds history, so the same SKU x pincode is comparable week over week. Analytics: Promise by cluster, SKU and category; trend detection; root-cause separation. Interface: A dashboard, or a clean Power BI dataset, readable by a supply chain manager in seconds. Calibration: A method for quantifying the gap between the API-reported promise and the live storefront promise. Alerting: Notification when a cluster degrades materially. Out of Scope: No web scraping. No storefront scraping of amazon.in, flipkart.com or any marketplace - no HTTP scraping, headless browsers, proxy or VPN rotation, no third-party scraped datasets. A first-party API exists that returns structured, authoritative data with no blocking and no account risk; reaching for a scraper instead is a poor engineering judgement and is scored as one. Any submission containing scraping code or scraped data is disqualified before scoring begins. Also out of scope: competitor pricing or catalogue data; any write operation against Amazon (the system is strictly read-only); customer personal data; mobile applications. Working Environment: Teams build against the SP-API sandbox plus a supplied set of several thousand real, anonymised API responses served by a local mock server. Production credentials are never issued externally; shortlisted submissions are validated against the live account by Plantex engineers, with the team present. Deliverables: Four tracks. Tracks A and B are mandatory to qualify. C and D separate a strong submission from an adequate one. Track A - Collection Engine (Mandatory): Scheduled, unattended execution at a configurable cadence. Client-side throttling to the published limit (2 req/s, burst 30) with exponential backoff on HTTP 429. Idempotent and resumable - an interrupted sweep continues without duplicating work. Structured logging and a per-run summary: calls, successes, failures, throttle events. Classified handling of every documented failure mode, including DeliverySLAUnavailable, ItemQuantityNotAvailable and HTTP 403. Credentials from environment or a secret store, never from source. Track B - Data Model and Storage (Mandatory): A schema supporting the time-series question: the same SKU x pincode measured weekly over months. A justified storage choice - PostgreSQL, SQLite, DuckDB or Parquet all acceptable; the reasoning earns the marks. Ingestion that is safe to re-run, plus a documented query interface for downstream consumers. Track C - Analytics and Interface: SKU x cluster promise matrix with clear visual banding, and week-on-week trend per cluster. Root-cause split - unfulfillable (stock placement) versus slow (transit), each quantified. A join against FC stock position showing which SKUs are misplaced relative to demand. Delivered as a web dashboard or a clean Power BI dataset with a sample report; both count equally. Track D - Calibration and Alerting: A reproducible method for measuring the offset between the API-reported promise and what a real customer sees, applied per cluster. A statistically defensible alerting rule separating genuine degradation from noise - state the false-positive rate it implies. Notification delivery by email or webhook.

title: Grevix AfterCode
description: Grevix AfterCode is a 24-hour online solo hackathon built around one simple idea: One Builder. One Idea. 24 Hours. No Boundaries. Unlike traditional hackathons, participants are not given a fixed problem statement. You choose the problem you want to solve, decide what you want to build, and choose the tools and technologies you want to use. AI coding agents, APIs, no-code/low-code platforms, design tools, open-source technologies, and traditional development are all allowed. But there is a twist. During the 24-hour challenge, your original plan will be disrupted by unexpected challenges. The goal is not just to see what you can build. It is to see how well you can adapt when the plan changes. The AfterCode Challenge System The hackathon is divided into 3 phases of 8 hours each. Phase 1: Build Hours 0-8 Start with an idea you genuinely want to build. You decide: What problem you want to solve Who you are building for What your product should do Which technologies and tools you want to use How you want to approach the problem At the end of the first 8 hours, the first unexpected challenge will be revealed. Phase 2: Adapt Hours 8-16 Participants receive a Challenge Card containing a new requirement, constraint, or change. The challenge may require you to: Change your target user Modify or remove a core feature Change the intended use case Introduce a new interaction Work under a new constraint Rethink your original solution You decide how to respond. You can adapt your product, rebuild it, simplify it, or completely change your approach. At the end of the second 8-hour period, another Challenge Card will be revealed. The Challenge Cards will not be revealed before the hackathon. Phase 3: Rebuild & Ship Hours 16-24 The second unexpected challenge is introduced. You now have the final 8 hours to adapt your product, improve your solution, fix what matters, and prepare your final submission. At the end of 24 hours, your product must be ready to ship. Human + AI AI tools are allowed and encouraged. Participants may use AI coding agents, LLMs, APIs, AI design tools, and other AI-assisted development workflows. However, participants remain responsible for: Their decisions Their implementation Their use of AI-generated output Their final submission The core philosophy of AfterCode is: AI can help execute. The builder decides what actually matters. Eligibility Open to everyone Students, developers, professionals, freelancers, and independent builders can participate No specific college, degree, specialization, or programming background is required Participants can participate from any country, subject to applicable Unstop requirements Participation is strictly individual Team participation is not allowed No college, specialization, or team-based restrictions apply Technology Rules There is no mandatory technology stack. Participants may use: AI coding agents Large Language Models (LLMs) APIs No-code/low-code platforms Design tools Cloud services Open-source software Programming languages and frameworks of their choice Participants are responsible for complying with the terms of service, licenses, and usage policies of the tools and services they use. Submission Participants must submit their completed project before the final submission deadline. The submission may include: Project name and description Problem being solved Solution overview Working demo or live link, where applicable Source code or repository, where applicable Technologies and AI tools used Short explanation of how the project evolved through the AfterCode challenges Detailed submission instructions will be provided to registered participants before the submission window. Judging Criteria Projects will be evaluated using the following criteria: Problem Significance - 25% How meaningful and relevant is the problem being addressed? Creativity & Originality - 20% How unique, creative, and differentiated is the solution? Execution & Functionality - 25% How effectively does the product work, and how well has the idea been executed? Effective Use of Technology/AI - 15% How effectively are technology and AI being used to build and improve the solution? Real-World Impact - 15% What potential does the solution have to create meaningful real-world value? The amount of code generated will not determine the winner. Judges may also consider how effectively participants responded to the unexpected challenges introduced during the hackathon. Build Log Participants may be asked to document parts of their development journey through short checkpoints. Examples include: What did AI do? What did you decide? What did you reject? The purpose is to capture the human decision-making behind the final product rather than evaluating only the final output. Rules Participation is strictly individual. The project must be created during the official 24-hour hackathon period. Participants may use existing libraries, frameworks, APIs, and development tools. AI-assisted development is permitted. Participants must not submit someone else's project as their own. Plagiarism, fraudulent submissions, or deliberate misrepresentation may result in disqualification. Participants must respect the terms of service and licenses of all third-party tools and resources used. Participants are responsible for ensuring that their project does not violate applicable laws or third-party rights. Challenge Cards must be followed according to the instructions provided during the event. The final submission must be submitted before the official deadline. Grevix reserves the right to disqualify submissions that violate the event rules or demonstrate dishonest participation. Judges' decisions will be final. Event Structure October 11 → October 12, 2026 24 Hours Total 0-8 Hours: Build 8 Hours: Challenge 1 8-16 Hours: Adapt & Build 16 Hours: Challenge 2 16-24 Hours: Rebuild & Ship 24 Hours: Final Submission The AfterCode Philosophy No fixed problem. No fixed technology stack. No predetermined solution. Just one builder, one idea, and 24 hours to see how far you can take it. Build. Adapt. Rebuild. Ship. One Idea. 24 Hours. No Boundaries.

title: DataHeist
description: DataHeist is a four-hour CTF × Machine Learning challenge where teams crack a series of challenges to uncover datasets, identify which data is useful, and build the best predictive model for a real-world problem. Think fast, investigate smart, and turn the right data into the strongest predictions. Event Details: Mode: In-person Venue: Delhi Technological University (DTU) Date & Time: 16th October 2026, 11:00 AM Duration: 4 hours Guidelines: Team Size: 1-3 members. Eligibility: Students from different colleges and specializations are eligible to participate. Multiple teams from the same institution are allowed. Teams may use the internet and publicly available resources for research during the competition. Event Format: Single Round: One continuous, approximately 4-hour competition. Crack the CTF: Solve a set of CTF-style challenges to obtain the datasets needed for the modelling task. The Twist: Not every dataset you uncover will be useful. Some datasets may be intentionally bad, while others contain the information needed to build an effective solution. Build & Predict: Analyze the available data, develop a predictive model, and generate predictions for the given real-world problem. Submissions & Leaderboard: Rolling Submissions: Teams may submit their predictions throughout the 4-hour competition. Evaluation: Each submission will be evaluated against the hidden test data using the competition's specified evaluation metric. Live Rankings: Once evaluated, the resulting score will be used to update the leaderboard, allowing teams to track their performance throughout the competition. Iterate & Improve: Teams can refine their approach and make further submissions during the competition, subject to the competition's submission rules. title: Signalpost: Build An Agent That Finds Company Information
description: Overview Start and submit on Builderr: https://builderr.ai/challenges/signalpost?utm_source=unstop&utm_medium=challenge_listing&utm_campaign=signalpost_2026. Registering on Unstop does not submit your entry. Build an agent that finds company information online. What to Build Give your agent a Norwegian company number. It searches permitted public sources and returns company facts, source links and dates. Make sure each fact belongs to the right company and keep profiles current. What to Submit At least 1,000 company profiles Your repository link Exact commit hash One command to run it Model/API details Expected run costs How We Test and Score Every agent receives the same 100 random companies each day. Find useful information (35 points), match it correctly with evidence (30), update correctly (20), give useful explanations (10), and make it easy to use (5). For coverage, we compare what your agent finds with a checked collection built from submissions and Builderr crawlers. To qualify: at least 65/100 overall, 21/35 coverage, and all published accuracy, evidence and execution requirements. A material wrong-company publication or fabricated financial value fails the entry. Qualified agents are ranked by their average score across completed daily tests. Daily limits: 45 minutes, 2,000 outbound requests and $10 in declared external API costs. Development and API usage can incur costs. Rewards $2,000 main cash prizes: $1,200 / $500 / $300. Separate $500 JBOX bonus: $250 / $150 / $100 for qualifying agents built with JBOX. Awards require qualification; participation does not guarantee a prize or job. How to Enter Build your agent, then email your code and required files to submit@builderr.ai. This online challenge is hosted and evaluated on Builderr. Students and professionals may participate under the published eligibility and team rules. AI coding tools are welcome; working code is required.

title: Jugaad
organizer: Sant Longowal Institute of Engineering and Technology, Longowal, Punjab
description: Overview TechFEST 2026 is North India's premier technical festival. This is a paid opportunity with the packages mentioned below: Select Your Registration Package Registration for the techFEST'26 package is compulsory for accommodation and other perks, while participation in individual events is free*. www.techfest26.com Prepare yourself for a journey of technology, creativity, and celebration. Mark your calendars and be part of the magic of techFEST'26 at SLIET. JUGAAD - Scrap to Solution Welcome to JUGAAD - Scrap to Solution by Sant Longowal Institute of Engineering and Technology, Longowal, Punjab! JUGAAD challenges participants to design and build innovative and practical solutions using scrap or recycled materials. The event focuses on creativity, sustainability, and converting waste into useful products. Participants are encouraged to think like product developers and create solutions that can be used in real life. About the Opportunity This event provides students with a platform to showcase their creativity and problem-solving skills by turning discarded materials into functional and useful products. The focus is on practical innovation, sustainability, and the real-life usability of the proposed solutions. JUGAAD also highlights the importance of upcycling, responsible waste management, and exploring the hidden potential of discarded materials to work towards a more sustainable future. Objective Reduce the burden of waste management that threatens public health and the environment. Encourage innovative ideas for waste utilization, process modifications, and technical advancements. Explore the unused potential of discarded materials and transform them into useful solutions. Promote sustainability through creativity, innovation, and responsible use of resources. Themes / Problem Statements PVC Pipe Vertical Farming / Kitchen Garden Unit Build a modular vertical farming system using used PVC pipes for growing vegetables or plants in limited spaces such as balconies or rooftops. Cardboard & Scrap Wood Functional Furniture Create usable and reasonably strong chairs, tables, or shelves using cardboard and wooden scrap materials. Packaging Waste Reduction Develop low-cost reusable or biodegradable packaging solutions using natural fibers, recycled paper, or textile scraps for local products. Educational Kits from Cardboard & Scrap Design engaging and low-cost educational or science kits for children using cardboard and other scrap materials. Old Solar Panel / Battery to Low-Cost Street Light Make a functional low-cost street light using discarded solar panels and batteries suitable for rural areas. Portable Disposable Dustbin for Travelers Design a low-cost portable dustbin that rail or bus travelers can use for 1-3 days and then dispose of. Waste Tyre + Plastic Bottle Roadside Seating & Planter Create roadside seating and plant holders using old tyres and plastic bottles. Scrap-Based Insulated Vegetable / Fruit Carry Bag Make an insulated carry bag from old cloth, foam, or packaging materials to keep vegetables and fruits fresh for longer. Waste Paper & Cardboard to Seed Starter / Nursery Tray Create biodegradable seed trays or nursery trays from waste paper and cardboard that can decompose in soil. Engineering Innovation: Waste to Resources Open Theme - Students can showcase any innovative solution related to Sustainable Development Goals, Engineering, Innovation, and Sustainability using waste or scrap materials. Rules & Regulations Decorative items are prohibited. The Judge's decision is final. Every participant can participate in only one team. Every member must contribute actively to the project. Maintain proper decorum throughout the event. Participants should clarify all doubts before the event. Teams must ensure that their projects are based on the use of waste, scrap, recycled, or upcycled materials. Any form of plagiarism or unfair practice may lead to disqualification. Judgement Criteria Projects will be evaluated based on: Innovation Creativity Presentation Effective use of recycled / upcycled materials The decision of the judging committee will be final. Team Specification Each team can have a maximum of 3 members . Participants from any institute and any academic branch may participate, provided they possess a valid ID card from their respective institute. Every team must select a unique team name that should not be inappropriate, offensive, or conflicting with another team's name. Each team must specify a Team Representative with whom Team techFEST'26 can communicate regarding further information and notices. Each participant can be a member of only one team. Certification Policy Certificate of Excellence for top-performing teams. Participation Certificates for all eligible participants. Prize distribution based on judge-assigned points. Important Note Participants must follow the registration guidelines provided by Team techFEST'26. The organizers reserve the right to modify the rules, prize pool, dates, venue, or timing of the competition if deemed necessary under unforeseen circumstances. All guidelines are subject to change. Participants are advised to regularly check the official techFEST'26 website and social media platforms for updates. Any changes or announcements will be posted through the official channels. Adherence to the latest rules and regulations is mandatory for all participants. Note Team techFEST'26 reserves all rights to modify or change any or all of the above information without prior notice. The updated rulebook will be posted on the website.
